Here’s my overall review — a mix of what I genuinely appreciated and the parts where I couldn’t fully agree with the author 😁 The three attachment patterns were very well explained, and I loved the concise sentences that sum up whole ideas. The book is also beautifully organized. Here are some quotes I loved the most: "Dependency paradox: the more effectively dependent people are on one another, the more independent and daring they become." "It’s tempting to forget that, in fact, people have very different capacities for intimacy." "You will no longer ask yourself, ‘Why is she always pushing me away?’ Instead, you’ll say, ‘It really isn’t about me at all; she just doesn’t feel comfortable with too much closeness.’" "The more attuned you are to your partner’s needs at the early stages — and he or she to yours — the less energy you will need to expend attending to him or her later." "After all, it takes two willing individuals to create intimacy." "Be brave emotionally." "Understanding that your continual arguments actually have a hidden subtext to them — that they’re genuinely irresolvable — changes your perception of your own role dramatically." "They learned to be thankful for what their mate does do and to overlook what he or she does not do." "You perceive the relationship as something fragile and unsettled that can collapse at any moment. These thoughts and perceptions make it hard for you to express your needs effectively." "Never taking blame for a date’s offensive behavior — when a partner acts inconsiderately or hurtfully, secures acknowledge that it says a lot about the other person rather than about themselves." "Pulling away when things are going well (e.g., not calling for several days after an intimate date); keeping secrets and leaving things foggy to maintain your feeling of independence."

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I wished I had read this book before, but as the saying goes: "The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is now." Attachment theory, commonly used to understand children behavior, is applied to romantic adult relationships by the authors and it is... fascinating. Long story short, there are three main types of people in this world based on their attachment style: - Anxious people are often preoccupied with their relationships and tend to worry about their partner’s ability to love them back - Avoidant people equate intimacy with a loss of independence and constantly try to minimize closeness - Secure people feel comfortable with intimacy and are usually warm and loving The book goes deep into each one of them, more on ones than others--a bit disappointing. Regardless, the important part is how they interact among each other and for that, the book is already super relevant. I did all the quizzes and exercises, so I did learn a lot about myself and my tendencies. Some things I was pretty certain about, some others were very deep revelations. I felt much better afterwards... super hopeful, almost as if my relationship toolkit had been upgraded. In addition, I really appreciated the examples of how society celebrates or condemns certain attachment styles for no good reason--and that while some activation strategies could be seen as super negative--in reality, they have good reasons to exist. We do need people with the whole range of styles. The goal here is that, no matter your attachment style, there is a path to fulfill your needs while also fulfilling the ones of your partner. Something else. I kept wondering about how the "coming out" experience of many of us who aren't straight shake our "natural" attachment style. That would be a great follow-up reading.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I did enjoy reading this book, it is very insightful and informative to adult attachment and relationships. I personally had many ‘A-ha’ moments while reading. Even if you are secure, this book helps you recognize moments you or your partner were acting anxious or avoidant, and the proper ways to react. Attached. is very easy to approach and read. This book offers a plethora of tools, techniques, rubrics, tests, and real world scenarios; making it easy to comprehend and integrate in your real life. That’s being said, there are some pitfalls to Attached. I’d like to acknowledge. If you do some research about this particular book you’ll find some controversy. Yes I do think this book is implicitly biased in favor of the anxious attachment type, this is prevalent in the real world scenarios and overall attitude of the writing. It’s also worth mentioning that there is no mention of same sex relationships in the writing. Lastly I’d like to point out that this book can seem very repetitive, they drill the points into the ground, at some points I felt like a high schooler taking an elementary test, or reading an entry level textbook, which admittedly is what this book is likely trying to be. In all, I would recommend this book to anyone with an attachment system or anyone looking to learn more about relationships, and how to keep them healthy and thriving. I closed the book feeling like I had learned information I will continue to use in my daily life.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Positive: The emotional triggers and actions in response to these triggers are accurate, its very easy to recognize your own thought patterns in the attachment descriptions. It brings some comfort knowing that some people with the same unexplainable problems can overcome it, the only thing you need is emotional self reflection and honesty. If you are honest enough to accept that your reactions to triggers are causing problems for yourself (the hardest part), then it opens the door for you to look for solutions. could definitely bring comfort to know that when acceptence is the first step to growth, the only thing you have to do after that step, is restructure some thought patterns using positive associations, ignoring your habituated thoughts and tricking yourself that discomfort is actually good by viewing it in a different way. Not hard, do this all the time. Just Pavlov yourself. Negative: I dont agree with the personality they try to associate with avoidants, they make it seem like they are emotionally handicapped at reading themselves and others, and dont care about the feelings of the partner. They make it seem like avoidant is a personality type, but its just a response to intimacy. Avoidants can also bring comfort, while the book dismisses this part. Maybe there are more types of avoidants, rooted in what the original reason was for the behaviour?? Also they contradict themselves by saying that when a relationship doesnt bring peace of mind, you should run. But the whole concept of an avoidant is that they arent at peace with closeness, so their advice would only reinforce avoidant behaviour.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is the kind of book I wish I had read before I started dating/“finding love”, which is an area of my life that I find is filled with more challenges or complexities than I had expected. I didn’t know about attachment styles until my friend gifted me this book and I’m so grateful to know now! Attached is a great “Intro to Dating/Getting to Know Yourself” guidebook of sorts. Identifying my attachment style and learning about it (and the others) has provided me with the tools and perspectives around how I can work on myself to become more secure as an individual, to identify the way these attachment styles manifest in different relationships and situations, and to use effective communication and an understanding of these attachment styles to introduce security into a relationship (no matter what stage it is at). Levine and Heller do a tremendous job debunking misconceptions with real life scenarios and also providing invaluable skills that can help all of us have more fulfilling and life-expanding human relationships. As they share in the epilogue, “Relationships are one of the most rewarding of human experiences, above and beyond other gifts that life has to offer.” And I appreciate this book for adding another dimension to my life that allows me to expand on the gift of the experience, especially in an area where I didn’t have the vocabulary for it. This is a highly readable book that I would recommend to everyone!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book made me so mad! There were some sprinklings of useful information in here, but mostly the book would offer advice like “communicate effectively” without really offering examples of how to do that. But what really got to me was how much the book played into stereotypical gender roles. They mention at one point that while women are often seen as having an anxious attachment style and men as having an avoidant attachment style, this is not true. But they then proceed to have almost every example fall into these categories, often with women whining about how their boyfriend won’t call them. Then at another point, the author gives an example of when attachment styles aren’t compatible and says that you have to just deal with your partner’s attachment style and then gives and example where an avoidant man doesn’t want to parent his kids because he had kids in a previous marriage and the author then proceeds to say the woman just has to deal with this if she wants to stay married. Wtf is that?! And finally, every single example of a couple in this book is a heterosexual couple. There is one example that includes a gay person and they are portrayed as a villain because he chooses to date a woman while questioning his sexuality. The author actually uses the word agenda here to describe this person wanting to date a woman so they don’t have to come out to their family which seems like a big and offensive assumption on the author’s part. I could go on but essentially, I found the book lacking in useful information and filled with harmful stereotypes. I imagine there is a better book out there for someone interested in learning about attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A helpful and practical book about how attachment styles (anxious, avoidant, and secure) can affect your romantic relationships! This book was very engaging, helping you think about ways to improve your own relationship habits and communicate better with their partner about your needs. I appreciated that the book referenced a good deal of scientific information and medical/therapeutic experts while also providing insightful examples from real-life relationships. One part of the book I liked were the interactive quizzes that help you determine your own attachment style as well as the attachment style of your partner. It was also helpful to have scenario-based examples where they give you a short story about how someone behaves in a relationship and then you are tasked with guessing their attachment style. It was interesting to learn that attachment styles exist on a continuum and can shift based on life experiences. In fact, studies indicate that approximately 20-30% of people experience changes in their attachment styles over time, often in response to significant life events or relationship experiences. For example, a person with an anxious attachment style may become more secure if they enter a relationship that provides consistent support. Or perhaps a person with an avoidant attachment style may become more comfortable with intimacy if they have more exposure to secure relationships and vulnerability. Additionally, people’s attachment tendencies can evolve due to therapy and/or personal growth. Perhaps the most helpful section in the book was about effective communication and dealing with conflict in relationships in a secure, constructive, healthy way. The authors list the five principles of effective communication as (i) wear your heart on your sleeve (ii) focus on your needs (rather than your partner’s shortcomings) (iii) be specific (about what is bothering you) (iv) don’t blame (try to stay calm to keep things from spiraling into a dueling match) (v) be ass

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book outlines "attachment theory" - how people express themselves in relationships falls into roughly three buckets: * Secure: doesn't have any issues expressing love * Anxious: is more of the "clingy" type * Avoidant: is cold, tends to withdraw or easily break things off Basically if you're a secure type, you're all good but if you're an insecure type (anxious or avoidant), and your partner is also an insecure type, you're probably going to experience some relationship issues. Actually the book goes one step further and basically says "if you're both insecure types you're probably never going to be as happy as you would be if you dated a secure person, but whatever". A bit of a spicy take but could be true though. Some of the criticism I saw previously when reading reviews for this book is that it's pro-anxious and anti-avoidant. While I did feel that vibe a bit (the author definitely seemed a tad more sympathetic to anxious types) as a self-diagnosed avoidant I didn't really feel personally attacked or anything. If anything I could agree with a lot of the things the author pointed out (although reading about it is one thing, actually putting it into practice is a hell of a lot harder...).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Damn, I figured this would be super interesting but I would go as far as describing it as enlightening after having finished it. The 3 main attachment styles- avoidant, anxious, and secure- are more or less self-explanatory. Avoidants fear and shy away from intimacy as they get close to someone, anxious individuals crave intimacy and fear rejection and abandonment, and secure people (the majority of the population by the way) are effective communicators and are flexible and highly attuned to their partners emotional needs. I think the thing I found most interesting was that research has shown that there is no significant difference in happiness levels between secure couples and mixed couples (either secure-anxious or anxious-avoidant). Unsurprisingly, the secure couples were significantly happier than anxious and avoidant couples. Random notes: Activating strategies - thoughts and feelings that compel you to get close physically or emotionally to your partner Protest behavior - acting out when your attachment system is activated Avoidants end relationships more frequently, and are in the dating pool more often and for longer periods of time. Avoidant-avoidant relationships are insanely rare. They are more likely to date people with different attachment styles Attributes of secure types: - great conflict busters- don’t feel the need to act defensively or to injure or punish their partner - Mentally flexible, not threatened by criticism. They’re willing to reconsider their ways and if necessary, revise their beliefs and strategies

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Бих казала, че това е едно доста полезно четиво, особено ако се вълнувате от такъв тип теми. Понякога обичам да експериментирам с такъв вид книги, защото ти отварят очите за отношенията между хората. Показват как "да се четем" по-лесно и да си бъдем полезни в отношенията. Естествено човек разбира много неща, докато чете такъв тип книги - за себе си и за околните, защото човешките взаимоотношения са едни доста особени връзки, които имат нужда от "превод". Честно казано, не знаех колко наистина имах нужда да прочета тази книга и то точно на този етап, в които се намирам. Много благодаря, че ми я препоръчаха! Като цяло я четох много дълго време, защото имаше упражнения, които трябва да се правят, да се преосмисли написаното. Такъв тип книги не можеш да минеш през тях като през поредната и да я затворих, да я забравиш. Направих си и доста бележки, които ще са ми необходими. Всяка една емоция в човешкото ни съществуване се базира на това какъв вид привързаност имаме - от любовните отношения, до тези връзки с приятелите и роднините и е хубаво да си знае човек от кой вид е и какво има нужда да "излекува" в себе си. За хора, които обичат такива книги - препоръчвам я! А вие можете да ми препоръчате подобни книги, с които да обогатя мирогледа си.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Eh, I am honestly a bit embarrassed to include this on my Goodreads account, but I did read it so might as well. There's a lot of critique about how differently the three attachment types are treated (ranging from 'a gift from god' to big bad evil) which is honestly super valid. It might be a comfort for some to read, and I guess when taken with a grain of salt can be a bit helpful in navigating how to deal with different people and manage your own emotions and communicate your needs effectively. But so much of this book was repetitive fluff, the examples seemed extreme always - I get anxious attachments are nervous and needy, but it's not like you're a screaming psychotic mess every time your partner doesn't call you back. Why couldn't there be advice on how to deal with the small anxieties or the less obvious displays of 'unmet attachment needs'. I don't know, 2 stars feels generous but also stingy as I did find some value in this. Also fyi but likely as no surprise, it's incredibly heteronormative and seems to exclusively discuss monogamous relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Just my opinions, but what I didn’t like about the book: 1. discounts ability/desire to change and work together through these things 2. I think we each at times display traits of all of these; doesn’t seem like clear boxes (see NYT review) 3. Also doesn’t consider balance of working through these issues along with ALL OTHER parts of a relationship; what else is there in a relationship that makes it feel worth it. 4. How much of this is culturally US based? Maybe not much but the book seemed rather American and had me wondering. In other cultures there may also be a different prioritization of attachment style vs. other important things in a relationship 5. In the anxiety category, how much of this has to do with specific anxiety toward a relationship vs generalized anxiety? Seems like an important distinction for holistically addressing it as an issue 6. I think some degree of independence in a relationship is essential; codependency does not make sense as a goal to me 7. In broad strokes these categories seem to make sense but also dig into WHY; why is someone anxious? Or avoidant? I think this is also part of why they did not feel like they fully made sense to me 8. This book was not actually very helpful for understanding avoidant people and just paints them as villains to be shed or avoided.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Love Wins This book was a gift for me from a caring heart. Ever difficult at times to digest, it is necessary to face mistakes if you mean to learn, grow and keep going forward. To learn is to understand where you have been and how you got there. Sometimes we learn from the autopsy. Facing my own truth has been humbling and humiliating. Ingredients for evolution. To not repeat painful mistakes and to help others to avoid that path for themselves. Always remember that the better you know and understand yourself, the better for all of the world. Finding true love, while tricky for many, is well worth getting RIGHT. As I have heard before, enter a marriage with eyes wide open; once married, close them halfway. Sounds about right. Bottom line: Love Wins. The messages received from the many stories involved with this book have helped me to understand that many others have had similar struggles. Emotional intelligence is a skill well worth acquiring. The information contained within this book will certainly bring you closer to this goal.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attachment theory - one of my favorite psychology concepts to learn about!! Been meaning to read this for a long time and I’m glad I finally did. Overall, an accessible read based on good research that offers valuable insight for anyone who wants a better understanding of themselves and of how they show up in relationships and even friendships. Though, few observations : I did sense a slight inequality in how anxious and avoidant attachments were depicted. It’s almost like this book was mostly written for anxiously attached people, sometimes dismissing avoidantly attached people’s needs and doubting their ability to become secure and be good partners. Also, why are we completely leaving out insecure disorganized attachement?? I don’t even reckon it was mentioned in there and I do think this book would have benefited from talking about it. Lastly, this book did feel a bit black-or-white at some points, as if you should put yourself in only one category; when attachment is really a spectrum and you could present anxious/avoidant/secure traits depending on the time and context. “The most important take-home message from this book is that relationships should not be left to chance.” I genuinely believe this book could change many people’s lives.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached is a must read for anyone who wants to navigate interpersonal relationships with a better understanding of the psychological imprint we bring to our relationships-based attachment style. The book is more of a practical guide on recognizing the protest behaviours of each attachment style and working on establishing effective communication in a relationship rather than a theoretical exploration of the types. It was really interesting to read about the parallels between 1940s "tough love" parenting methods and today's mainstream dating beliefs centered around "playing hard to get" and appearing emotionally independent in order to appeal more to your love interest. The book made me realize that millennials are often taught to employ the deactivating mechanisms of avoidant people in order to stir interest and make themselves appear more desirable. We are constantly advised to appear a little unavailable, not show too much interest and thereby arouse someone's anxious attachment mechanisms. The authors pointed out how misguided this advice is given the fact that avoidant people are the least likely to form healthy and satisfying relationships with others. Furthermore it asserts that adults, like children, have a biological precondition for a certain degree of emotional and physical dependency and without it, they feel less psychologically secure. The authors explain that there's a certain "dependency paradox" that forms where a secure base in the form of a warm partnership is necessary for an individual to take flight, take risks and be more creative.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: What a great way to start my reading year off!! Really setting the tone for self-awareness and growth. Not only did I get the opportunity to self-diagnose myself with an anxious attachment style (romantically), I got to self-diagnose all my ex's and boy - is there ever a trend. Levine and Heller detail the 3 attachment styles separately (anxious, avoidant and secure), how those type of people interact with each other and gave many examples of situations you might find yourself in if you're in a particular type of relationship (ex. the anxious-avoidant cycle or secure-secure or whatever). There was one example that I almost fell out of my seat when I read because it hit so close to home. If you're interested in learning more about why you act a certain way with different people and are willing to do the work (there's always work to be done) then I would recommend giving this a read. The good news is over 50% of the population have secure attachment styles so there's still hope for us all!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: i think i get what they were trying to do but it wasn't it for me... tem uma boa premissa e até tem uns pontos muito válidos e que deviam ser do conhecimento de todos mas eu não consigo superar a perpetuação de toxicidade em relações, que o motivo está ligado aos attachement styles, usando isso para se desresponsabilizar das suas ações e não haver um único apelo a quererem-se compreender melhor, a fomentar a relação consigo próprio, auto-descoberta e trabalhar nos problemas que têm (porque todos os temos) foi demasiado simplista e muito bias, discordo em muitas coisas nele mas pelo menos no facto de comunicação ser a chave concordamos e foi o que "salvou" este livro acho muito errado esperarmos que uma relação ou alguém nos venha salvar, vamos sempre precisar de relações na nossa vida e aprendemos mesmo muito com elas, mas eu não acho justo dizer que a responsabilidade de sermos felizes recai noutra pessoa não odiei mas irritou-me muito 🙊

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: There was a time that I didn’t completely despise self-help and pop-psych books. I think this one would’ve been a lot more insightful back then - especially since I was, without a doubt, an anxious-avoidant type for the majority of my 20s. I think it could have set me up for quite a bit more happiness had I read it in college or high school when it came out. 4 stars for teaching how to identify attachment types, for demonstrating what happens when secure individuals date anxious and avoidant types, and because I recognize the value that this can bring people who are still trying to sort out their romantic neuroses. Knocking off a full star for sophomoric grammar and spelling problems. Any editor worth the name should know not to clear a manuscript with the word “posses” as a verb and not a description of a group of men, or allow run-on sentences in a work not meant to be stylistically artistic. I also absolutely hated the negative treatment of avoidant types and a plethora of non-sequitor anecdotes. P.S. we all know you were talking about 500 Days of Summer at the end. Clever move, honestly; unfortunately, the authors, predictably, fell into the trap of blaming Summer for the fact that Tom was 100% the problem.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Decent introduction to the psychology of attachment styles in romantic relationships. Both authors do a good job of breaking down academic theory into an interesting overview of the secure, anxious and avoidant types. There are quizzes, relatable scenarios, and tips for how to manage your type, as well as the response to other types authentically. Lines I liked: Most people are only as needy as their unmet need. The dependency paradox: the more effectively dependent people are on one another, the more independent and daring they become. Dependency is a fact, it’s not a choice or a preference. Wen two people for an intimate relationship, they regulate each other psychological and emotional well-being. Nothing that brings two people closer than understanding and being understood by one another. We are social creatures and live best in relation to others. The fundamental premise of a good relationship; that the other person’s wellbeing is as important as your own.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was recommended to me by my good friend Lauren. Thank you Lauren! I’ve been having a lot of trouble with relationships and dating lately and now have a much better understanding of why this is so. This book is clear and concise, and outlines everything you need to know about attachment theory. I learned that I have anxious attachment issues, and that has made me not communicate so effectively while dating and in relationships. I also learned much about conflict resolution and communicating effectively, and this will definitely help me in future dating endeavors. I don’t read much non fiction or self help books but I highly recommend this one. Also take notes if you can! I’m hoping to move to a more secure attachment style and communicate more effectively in the future, and this book helped me with all of this. Do yourself a favor and read it!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book is a really accessible way to reflect + learn + improve your relationships. Now for criticism… I think this theory can be pretty reductive. When thinking about myself and other people I know while reading it didn’t feel like any attachment style fit us super great, and I wish we were labeling the behaviors instead of the people. Also, wish there was more gender analysis. They said “women can be avoidant and men can be anxious! It’s not gendered!” And then in almost every example women were anxious and men were avoidant. If there is a gender trend then discuss why and the implications of it. If not, be better about how the examples are gendered. Also- every relationship mentioned was heterosexual. Ditto to the critiques that say this book vilifies avoidant attachment. Also- would like more tips for anxious attachment folk about how to get a secure attachment. “Communicate!” and “don’t date avoidant attachment people!” feel… discouraging.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: In today’s hookup culture, where avoidant attachment styles are often glamorised and anxious styles unfairly dismissed as weakness, "Attached" by Amir Levine is an essential read. "Attached" provides plenty of real-life examples of attachment styles, some of which were painfully relatable. These examples made it easier to identify my own attachment style and provided practical strategies for navigating challenges in future relationships. I loved how the book encouraged engagement by asking readers to guess the attachment style of individuals based on the struggles they shared. Additionally, there were multiple-choice questions that helped determine your attachment style too. Although I loved this book, I did find myself disagreeing with the part where it states that it is okay to rely on your partner for happiness. Your happiness is your responsibility, and the book suggesting otherwise gave the impression that your romantic partner should bear the burden of fixing you. This is an unhealthy expectation, and I wholeheartedly disagree that this level of codependency is not a bad thing. I also would have appreciated more insight into the disorganised attachment style, which the book does not cover. However, I do understand it may be less common than the other three (avoidant, anxious, and secure) and likely more complex to explain, perhaps even deserving a dedicated book of its own. Overall, this book was an easy read and very useful.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Core Takeaways on Relationships & Attachment 1. Relationships are deeply rewarding They’re among the most fulfilling parts of life, but many people know little about the science behind them and are influenced by myths. 2. People have very different capacities for intimacy Intimacy capacity varies greatly, and mismatched attachment styles can cause significant unhappiness—even between people who love each other. 3. Partnership means mutual responsibility In healthy relationships, both partners see it as their job to care for each other’s emotional well-being. 4. Your attachment needs are valid Depending on a close partner is natural and wired into your biology—you shouldn’t feel guilty for needing closeness and support. 5. A good relationship should build you up It should boost your confidence and bring peace of mind. If it doesn’t, that’s a red flag. 6. Authenticity is everything Playing games or pretending to be someone you’re not pushes you further from genuine happiness.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I really enjoyed this book. I liked the idea that we each have a style of attachment. I’d like to think that it can change more than we think. I think at times I have been very anxious in my attachment style, but I feel a lot more secure attachment now, though every once and a while, I do see my anxious attachment style come back. I feel like the explanations of different styles helped me to understand some of my dating experiences before I got married, and even though I have moved in from those, it helped me a lot to understand why they happened. I think the emphasis on secure communication styles is probably the most important thing I will take moving forward. I think when I am able to securely communicate my needs, that’s when I find my husband responds well and then I find that we can better meet each other’s needs.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Why five stars? Why is a guy whose 99% business reading a relationship book? The second question answers itself. As for the first, anytime a book allows you to see yourself, not so much as you like to see yourself but in a more unvarnished truthiness kind of way... well that’s a five star book. There were a few key passages that for me were ‘ah-ha’ moments which actually triggered immediate course corrections within current relationships of different levels in my life. Understanding that some of our bad behaviours are not ‘what everyone does’ is important. Understanding how to own them and halt them is ultra valuable. This book gave me that. But to be fair I’m usually able to find a golden nugget in just about any book and I’ll often assign 5-stars to something due to a single paragraph amongst 50,000 other words that didn’t necessarily resonate.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A nice little intro into the interesting concept of attachment theory, which is quite illuminating for me personally and helps explain why I seemed to be different persons altogether in my different relationships, which is something that has been puzzling me forever. (Spoiler alert: It's the level of security from the other person that calmed or amplified my anxiety, which in turn made me either indifferent or just obsessed.) In my serious relationship with someone "secure", and I, an "anxious," was guilty of mistaking that security for lack of love - a lesson I learned to my regret much, much later. And now, I was recommended this book by a friend who, learning that I might be dealing with an "avoidant", told me to run as fast as I can. He's got a point. I think I just truly understand for the first time what "we're not compatible" really means: it's exactly this. This clash in attachment styles. The book lays it all out, like a punch to the friggin' gut, that this right now is probably as good as it's ever gonna get, and it's nowhere near good enough.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: If you’re a person who would like to have healthy friendships and relationships, I recommend this book. I wish I’d read this book ten years ago. I learned a lot about the way I approach relationships and how to better communicate with others. I learned how to recognize attachment styles and how to self-regulate when an attachment-triggering situation comes up. I really appreciate how affirming the authors are regarding different people’s relationship needs. Whether you have an insecure, avoidant, or secure attachment style, your needs are completely legitimate. The trick is learning how to effectively and unapologetically communicate your needs with others and respectfully address their needs in turn. I’d like to give this book to everyone I love since this book was such a gift to me.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: As someone who puts on a lot of self-help books while driving… this was actually one of the best self help books i’ve read on effective communication and maintaining relationships(controversial take - I swear I’m not being contrarian on purpose). I personally found it really useful, and I fit the anxious attachment style to a T, and to my horror realised recognised many of the avoidant attachment styles in many of the men I had been interested in in the past. Is it perfect? No, but I think this book has really given me the gift of realising that the issue of incompatibility does not always fundamentally lie in the more “needy” partner who is asking for affection, and it has really allowed me to move on from my fear of rejection by people who are emotionally unavailable (you don’t vibe with my frequency of, or need for affection? thats cool, all the best in your search for love but this is something that is important to me that i should not compromise on in a r/s as it will make me unhappy, so bye!) If you play stupid games , ling ma says in bliss montage, you win stupid prizes. if you pretend to be unavailable and distant, you’ll just get the attention of avoidant types. I think this book was really freeing and affirming in just, reassuring me that my emotional needs in a relationship were valid and will be met with the right person, instead of making me squash my own tendencies and desires down. Well. That was a sort of rambly and personal reflection but yea. I will be making all future partners sit down and listen to this cover to cover on 1.75x with me.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I felt that this book accomplished what it set out to, though in a hyper-practical way, devoid of much substantial philosophical discussion of what attachment theory is fundamentally. I was hoping for a bit more of that. Instead, basic advice about relationships were frequently summarized in an abundance of lists, bullets, and acronyms. Modern research was definitely listed and briefly referenced, but there were few attempts to dive into the research in a substantial way. To the authors’ credit, I think they did a great job of introducing the attachment styles on a very basic level, and I’m certain that this self-help guide would be useful for someone who has struggled with relationships for years and wondered why. This will be a book that I will recommend to a very narrow population, but it definitely serves its purpose.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: For me i only read the parts of this book that felt applicable to me, but i really felt validated. It was surprising to see how so much of who you are is explained simply through your attachment style. I can see myself returning to parts of this book now and then when/if needed. I will add, this book seems primarily geared for those with an anxious style. I also didnt read much on if you were to find yourself in an anxious/anxious situation. I also agree with other reviews that it really rewarded those with secure and kind of categorized avoidant people as more cold- when i think they need the same warmth that was written for those with anxious. Anyways rant over idk how to rate this book 3-4?

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: i liked it but it was sorta repetitive in its anecdotes and also because i’ve learned about attachment theory before (shoutout to my professor who was mentioned in the book!). as a result, i felt like i skimmed through some parts. i feel like this would be a great read for someone who has not really been exposed to attachment theory because they do give a pretty good intro to it and equips you with the tools to think, discuss, and reflect on your relationships. it didn’t make me feel like i was over-intellectualizing my relationship experiences and i did enjoy how i was able to put some science and research into things i was going through at the time of reading the book. kinda found the exercises annoying sometimes and skipped through most. as someone who leans more anxious, i feel like this book definitely catered to me more than secure or avoidant people

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was good! Very accessible and easy to read, I tore through it. Honestly, I knew a lot about the content and research already because of tiktok + therapy. If I was still in a toxic relationship (like I was 3 years ago), I would have been completely mind blown while reading this. Growth! Would have been 5 stars but I found it a bit meandering, grasping for a higher page count. Additionally, they only focus on straight couples. I wish they'd incorporated other factors into their research, such as: queerness, class, race, ability, etc. It would have been interesting to see more examples which included these factors so I could understand more complex situations/relationships. But it's a nearly 15-year-old book so I don't entirely blame them. Reading this will give me foundations to approach future reading :-)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A captivating exploration of the psychology of human attachment, in the context of romantic relationships. It is structured very well, with Levine first laying out the basic framework that is used throughout the book (that there are 3 primary attachment styles) followed by helping the reader decipher which attachment style best describes them (but not in the same way a goofy internet quiz might!). Delving deeper, the majority of the book which dissects common challenges in relationships from the vantage points of the 3 distinct attachment styles, allowing us to understand what might be going through the minds of those with different styles to our own and granting us deeper insight into what might be going through our own heads. The layout and style of this book make it an easy read, and one that I would recommend to those interested in gleaming deeper insights into how humans behave when they get into relationships. I would however caution against using this framework as anything beyond an initial matching strategy in the context of informing yourself of how you or other people may behave in specific situations. The implicit assumption beyond the first two chapters that Levine’s schema is absolute is a dangerous one, as it is not the be all and end all as far as the analysis of human relationships is concerned, especially given that its provenance is based on taking a theory of childhood attachment and applying it to adults.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: it was really therapeutic, and helped me to realize a lot of negative coping mechanisms, or "protest behavior" that I have been using in my own life, I gave it a solid 4 out of 5 stars, my main concern is that it focuses very heavily on Cis/Hetero relationship dynamics and unintentionally supports some weird gender stereotypes (it tries to mitigate this but the majority of their examples lean into a gendered dynamic, and they only use one gay couple in the whole book) HOWEVER, the bones are there, and all the ideas and concepts were extremely helpful for me in processing my feelings and learning to be kinder to myself! I think they should update the book or release a version that explores more queer relationships, but I think the existing text is extremely useful

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I was torn between 4 and 5 stars and essentially decided for 5 because I didn't have any major cons regarding the book :) I thoroughly enjoyed this. A big part of that comes from the fact that attachment theory is something that came up a lot in my therapy sessions and I am deeply aware where on the "spectrum" I belong. Some of the facts mentioned in the book were like knives to my heart. Also coming from an anxious-avoidant ex relationship made the book relevant to say the least. I definitely think this book is for anxious or avoidant individuals because if you're secure, well, there isn't much to improve. A few things that call for improvements: 1. The authors' message is basically if you're anxious, find someone who is secure. Sure, they also mention some techniques to avoid the toxicity of your attachment, but I wish they would spend more time on personal improvement rather than just telling people to surround themselves with healthier people (i guess??). 2. The authors oftentimes mention research that doesn't take into consideration attachment theaory (fair point). Nevertheless, they also proceed to make conclusions solely based on the attachment theory and possibly not take into consideration other circumstances in people's lives? Or that's how it felt to me anyways. Overall, for me this book meant a lot of learning and rationalising the oftentimes unhealthy ways I react in my romantic and non-romantic relationships. I would recommend this to anyone struggling to forget about their situationship, going through a messy breakup or maybe just struggling with finding a happy relationship. :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5 star Mixed feelings about this books. +ve: 1. The underlying attachment theory is scientifically supported. This book is a reader friendly to apply the Bowlby's attachment theory to adult romantic relationship 2. That means this book is definitely more useful than the self-help or popular dating advice from so-called "relationship coaches" (e.g. "No contact rule?!" - if you are still browsing such articles, its more worthwhile to spend your money on Amir's book) 3. Again, reader friendly, easy to understand, a starting point to learn the dynamics of our actions and (in)actions for the avoidance. I can imagine this book can be potentially life-changing (slight exaggeration), at least truly eye-opening, for individuals who have been experiencing chronic relational problems and is finding no soothing answer elsewhere 4. Lastly, and honestly, who doesn't want to know why we or your phantom ex, your crush, or your romantic partner will behave in such way? How to evaluate whether to quit a relationship? Why I keep on repeating a similar pattern of falling in love with the wrong person? Who's the right person? How to keep the relationship? -ve: 1. If you have a psy/counselling background, this book may be too simplistic 2. Hold Me Tight: Seven Conversations for a Lifetime of Love is of more relevance and dives deeper into the tension of couple's conflict through examining our emotional responses/behaviours when our attachment system is breaking down

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was amazing. I listened to it and I was transfixed. It really explains things in such a relatable way and gives real qualitative examples and research that you can truly relate to scenarios in your own life and relationships. Don't think of this as self help book. It's a way to understand your own attachment style and behavior to make the most of your relationships. It helps you to understand what other people's styles are as well, and which styles may be a bad fit with yours. This isn't a typical self-help/relationship book at all, it's based on real psychological evidence and research, but it's still palpable and very easy to understand.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was really interesting. I wouldn’t say it has all the answers & is a self help book but it definitely starts the conversation. The big takes away for me - effective communication is key. Something bothering you? Say something girl. Otherwise it will festers and blow up in your face & you’ll have wasted precious time. - the relationship inventory was the most eye opening part. That excel spreadsheet on my failed relationships was genuinely eye opening. Reflection holds the key! - the chapter on conflict is a must read for everyone - attachment styles are malleable. It’s not set it stone. You can improve! - you want a soulmate? Gotta get out there with your heart on your sleeve. No point going out w a closed heart. You’ll only hurt yourself & others

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: For me, this book relied too much on categorizing people and behaviors into anxious or avoidant. It’s like it was competing with he’s-just-not-into-you-style dating guides, as opposed to helping readers authentically explore and understand attachment and how it might relate to their experiences. Rather than fixating on the labels, I would’ve loved to hear about how to tune into values, emotions, bodily sensations, and intuitions in the search for secure attachment experiences. On the plus side, the final chapter on effective communication was excellent. And a couple of the quizzes were really fun. Side note: no serious book that refers to women as “girls” will get more than two stars from me.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I am anxiously attached, so from my perspective, I thought it was a wonderful read. It helped me to better understand myself and past unsuccessful relationships. I really did date a ton of avoidant men, and now it’s evident why I did so… the insanity “felt” like love. If you’re secure, this book doesn’t offer much in the way of advice, but I doubt a secure person is seeking much relationship advice unless they’re dating an insecure type. If that’s the case, this book will hopefully help you understand how their brains work and be able to better meet them in the middle and respond in positive ways to their seemingly outlandish actions or comments.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Good intro to attachment theory. The questionnaire is helpful if you’re not familiar, both for identifying your attachment style but also that of your partners or ex-partners. Case studies and examples were helpful, though I have to agree with others that this book is probably most useful for anxious-style folks. Either way, I found it helpful and appreciated the details on how communicating your needs clearly (and timely, before they become overwhelming) and de-escalating conflict work. They sound obvious, but it’s nice to see specific examples and reflect on ways I’ve missed doing those things.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Validation and Aspiration Never has a book had me in sheer tears of reflective validation and a heart full of hope at the same time. I think a great way to understand Human Attachment would be to read this book after reading Love Sense: The Revolutionary New Science of Romantic Relationships by Sue Johnson. Johnson does a great way of getting one to understand where Attachment Science/Theory comes from and why it's important. Levine's book doesn't spend a ton of time on the where, but instead jumps right in with real world examples that if you have an insecure attachment style or have loved someone who does, will have you shook with their accuracy. Then, the book is full of hope and inspiration for those seeking a healthy relationship and all the tools to access your own style and how to navigate around other styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I very much enjoyed some of the ideas in this book, especially the bits about how relationships work and the practical advice, and the stuff on deactivating strategies. But overall it felt kind of basic and a bit too focused on attachment styles as the main fix for relationship issues. The takeaway seemed to be: 'Just date a secure partner, and everything will be fine,' which felt way too simplified. The categories - secure, avoidant, and anxious - felt a bit rigid and didn’t really consider all the other things that affect attachment. As someone who’s more avoidant, I also thought the book painted avoidant types in a negative light, like we’re the heartless or difficult ones. Still, I liked the relationship advice and found the explanations of attachment behaviors interesting.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Описувати "500 Days of Summer" у кінці книги було необов'язково... Книга доступно розповідає про біологію та еволюційне значення прихильности. Мені сподобалося, як автори роблять акцент на тому, що залежати від інших — базовано, бо не залежати від інших та могти покладатися на себе — абсолютно різні речі. Сподобалися схеми активації тривожників та схеми дезактивації уникливих. Сподобалося завдання на інвентаризацію стосунків. Цікаво було почитати типові прояви протестної поведінки (поведінка, яка "вмикається" через найменшу ознаку "небезпеки" — розриву стосунків) та типові способи знецінення партнера. Усе це очєнь інтересно. Як зазначав хтось у коментарях, автори неначе більше захищають тривожних, ніж уникливих партнерів. Приклади стосунків, які наводяться із розділу в розділ, інколи можна назвати аб'юзивними, і справа там не в типах прив'язаности. До речі, не було жодної інформації про дезорганізований тип прив'язаности, що мене дуже засмутило, бо що робити тривожно-уникаючим партнерам — хто його зна. Якщо тривожні люди тягнуться до близькости, а уникливі — уникають, і для кожного є свій алгоритм роботи з думками, то що робити представникам того типу прихильности, який поєднує в собі ці два механізми? А в атвєт тішина-а... Словом, непогана робота, пояснює звичні і не дуже звичні нам усім моделі поведінки. Хоч я не можу назвати конкретних речей, але склалося враження, наче постійно виринала одна і та сама інформація по сто разів. Відчуваю, що чогось начебто не вистачило. Мій відгук можна було б підсумувати назвою однієї з глав цієї книги: МИ ПОДОЛАЛИ ДОВГИЙ ШЛЯХ (ТА НЕДОСТАТНЬО НАБЛИЗИЛИСЯ)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm not usually a fan of self-help books; I use reading as an outlet to escape reality, and they tend to be geared toward looking inward and how to improve yourself as a little human, so this was a journey for me. This was the second time someone put this book in front of me, so I took it as a sign that it was time for me to give it a read. I did end up finding this book to be very insightful. I wish I had it on Kindle to highlight some parts that resonated with me and could reference later if I found myself in a communication rut in my future relationships. I have an avoidant attachment style, but working toward being secure 😅😂

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The only good part about this book was the part about effective communication. The other 90% were super arbitrary and it felt like they were just yapping without actually having any knowledge. Like, this book felt like what I imagine reading a transcript of the conversation between two stoners who have read one book about psychology to be like. They think they know interesting things, but it feels like they have no idea, and they are just saying random things hoping it somehow makes sense in the end. Key takeaways: Communicate effectively. Give others the benefit of the doubt that they have your best interests at heart until proven otherwise. (thank me later)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book provides some good insight into basic attachment styles and how it impacts relationship. I do think there could be been more provided for the disorganized and avoidant attachment. I think there also could have been more grace given to if you are in an anxious avoidant relationship. That does not mean you are locked in to a terrible relationship. However, the book provided a beautiful insight to how to create that secure base even with an anxious partner and avoidant partner. It’s restorative to think on a marriage with attention to these patterns can heal attachment wounds and provide corrective experience for both attachment styles. We are wired to heal.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I usually don't read these kind of books, but the word science in the title caught my eye and I was curious. It turns out this book is actually pretty interesting, it kind of reads like a lengthy pamphlet with plenty of research and examples to back up discoveries. In regards to relationships, the authors discuss 3 "types" of people: those who are secure, anxious, and avoidant. All though the examples are a bit simplistic at times, this book really opened my eyes to the types of people in relationships and how/why they act the way they do. Would recommend as a quick read to pretty much anyone- regardless of relationship status!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Recommended! Reviews of this are more polarized than I expected. Like any work on psychology or relationships, it probably shouldn't be taken as 100% ultimate truth, but for me it was an enjoyable, very insightful read. I think most (all?) human behavior is heavily influenced by peer behavior, so it's useful to read examples and cases in which my behavior is reflected, and read others that prompt improvement. No doubt there is much more to know than which box you fit into to understand why we behave the way we do - no single book could contain that. For what it's worth, by the book's measure I'm slightly more secure than avoidant, and hardly anxious at all.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a great introduction to attachment theory. There have been many "sciences" in love - from personality traits to love languages. I can definitely see how attachment theory has come to the frontier of these sciences. The book tells the proportionality of attachment types - 50% secure, 25% anxious, and 25% avoidant, and how forces of attraction and disengagement work in each of them. It views our attachment instinct as an extent of how humanity learned to evolve as a species (but not as individuals) in creating protest behaviors, as well as how each person was raised during childhood. It gives insight in analyzing our own behaviors, but not too much of advice on how to change to "secure" attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Wow, I’ve had this on my list for years and wish I read it earlier. It explains so much about my romantic relationship dynamics, past and present. I have an anxious attachment style and married someone with an avoidant style—and this book helps me better understand the way we interact with each other and gives actionable ways to improve our communication. I highly recommend this book for single people especially, but also those who find themselves in a relationship where one of the partners has an anxious or avoidant style (you can take a quiz online).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Okay at first I was very intrigued by this book. I really wanted to understand the reasons why we do what we to when we are in a relationship and being written by psychologist makes it easier to understand. I was scared it was something like coaching a relationship lol but it wasn’t. I really admire that it stood up for dependency and it doesn’t portrait it as something negative . Otherwise, there were moments where I really felt that being looking for love meant something like training and that after enough training you would just find a person ? I don’t know . I encourage you to read this book if you want to work on the way you handle intimate relationships if you think you need to work on something or maybe to heal yourself, but there is no need to be obsessed with it. ✌🏼

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this is a great book that encourages you to really think about your own attachment system in the context of your own relationships so that you get the most out of it. I think it was really information and interesting, without being too intimidating or overwhelming due to excessive scientific terminology or details about research. It’s a very approachable psychological novel. I really enjoyed it and took away a lot of positive things from this book. I can see myself coming back to this book in the future and going over some of the chapters when I need them.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Amazing book! As someone who is anxiously-attached when I’m delving into deeper connections. This book basically read and understood my struggles in a way that was reassuring and filled with clarity and hope. The book came by at the right place and time and I can recommend everyone to read this book, and especially try to solve its activities. What I don’t like is the lack of explicit sections for fearful-avoidant because why 4-5% of the population have it, it’s still millions of people that would need to decipher their needs and wants. ⭐️4.8/5

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this is a super important read for anyone dating, or struggling with dating. I know for myself I have negative dating traits that I have developed through childhood or my past relationships. There were so many times during reading this book that I was like “yup that’s me a T” and I think it’s helpful to read the science behind to feel less alone in this negative traits and also learn what you can do to correct the behavior and develop positive traits. I noticed alot of the behaviors of you are this style of dating so you’ll likely do this in response to this I had definitely done. I think for anyone out there dating who has recognized any behaviors in themselves or their partners this is a very important read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: ⚠️vulnerable and possibly cringe review alert⚠️ Initially started this book at the start of a relationship last year (never finished it lmao) and recently restarted after the relationship ended due to conflicting attachment styles. This was super eye opening and comforting and has already done so much to help with my ✨healing journey✨. I’ve been supplementing this with the podcast “On Attachment” and am slowly going through my highlights/notes with my therapist. Looking forward to using the things I’ve learned once I start dating again 🤪

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm glad to have this attachment theory as a tool in my toolbox. It was especially valuable for me to have time listening to this book and to reflect particularly in how my attachment styles interact with non romantic relationships. But it's a shame that this book is so heteronormative in language and practice. Also there is almost no analysis presented on how childhood experiences and systemic oppression might affect our attachment situations. I would like to read a book that is inclusive of trauma on interpersonal, societal, and institutional levels.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3 stars because, overall, it has really good concepts. I’m an attachment theory stan & it was nice to to read about it in an intimate relationship perspective. But after a bit, I personally found it getting a big stagnant. Not sure if it’s my psych/social work background & I don’t wanna sound pretentious but I was kinda like, “yeah, I get it” 🥴. Anyway, I liked it for what it was overall & want to/will recommend to friends because I feel like it is beneficial information.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: My best friend is a therapist and had mentioned attachment theory in a recent conversation and said that this was the book that explains it most clearly. Thing is, my friend did such a good (and honestly very succinct) job in talking about attachment that the book felt pretty redundant. It was like many self-help books where the premise is laid out in clear bullet points at the beginning and then pads itself out with lots of examples and scenarios. The book focuses on heterosexual romance, and does not talk about other forms of love or relationship such as family, friends, and colleagues. I agree with the advice of the book that if you are attempting a long-term romantic relationship with someone that you should state your needs and make sure the other person is willing to meet them, but how does that work with people who you are not trying to form a life partnership with?

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A good introduction to attachment theory with practical guidance and many scenarios and space to apply principles to yourself. Ideas presented in this book put words to my own experiences and I have improved confidence in finding security in relationships and conflict resolution. I was interested to learn how genetics play a role in our attachment styles and how our relationships with pets act as a secure presence in our lives. I wish the book included more on how attachment styles come to be. Furthermore there was little on gender, sexuality and polyamorous relationships - all the scenarios presented were in heterosexual monogamous relationships. I also wonder how attachment theory can be applied to relationships with friends and parents. Found the book a bit repetitive especially towards the end.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Mi psicóloga me sugirió leer este libro para así comprender mejor mi comportamiento y actitudes en relación con otras personas y ha sido lo mejor que he podido hacer. He aprendido muchísimo sobre cómo estamos predispuestos a ciertas conductas además de que me ha resultado una lectura muy sencilla y didáctica. Me ha encantado que sea un libro con ejercicios para así poner en práctica lo estudiado. Sinceramente, un 10 este libro.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A sobering realization of everything bad that has ever happened to me in life! But seriously, this book is a must-read for wherever you are in your relationship journey. Provided eye opening theories and real world practices to shift into secure behavior in both platonic and romantic partnerships. Offered clarity on many frustrating patterns I found myself in when dating and interacting with the rest of the world.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Things I learned from this book * Those with anxious attachments should avoid avoidants, making snap judgments when reading others emotions, and believing that there’s not many fish in the sea BECAUSE THERE ARE MANY FISH IN THE SEA * Those with avoidant attachments should learn to recognize their avoidant tendencies, forget about finding the perfect one, and distract themselves * Codependency is not a bad word * For those with insecure attachment styles your best bet is finding someone with a secure attachment style * communication is truly key

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Brilliant, well-educated, science-based book on love and attachment. A much deeper understanding of how dependence works from an anxious perspective. Although there’s definitely bias towards anxious types, but that’s merely a product of the meta analysis used for those book - not a bias on the author. Although educational, this book cannot be considered the ‘be all end all’ for attachment theory - you need a wide variety of sources exploring more varied papers.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: so I think I went into this book thinking it would completely blow my mind and I'd have this groundbreaking revelation about relationships. it was much more subtle then that, but still deeply insightful. although it didn't blow my mind, I do feel like I come out of reading this book with a better understanding of myself and how I approach relationships, as well as being equipped with some important strategies for having secure and stable relationships in the future. I especially appreciated the tips on how to manage conflict securely. definitely a worthwhile read!!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I give this book 5 stars. It resonated so deeply with me that I plan to purchase a hard copy. It addresses common relationship patterns, which sometimes seem predictable but hit differently by viewing it in various situations. Personally, it helped me identify my attachment style—anxious-avoidant—and provided guidance on how to shift towards a more secure attachment style. It emphasizes the importance of seeking secure attachments for healthier relationships and becoming a secure partner.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Good intro to attachment theory book. Should possibly be required reading before entering the dating pool lol fully on-board until the final thoughts where the author paints zooey deschanel’s character from 500 days of summer (movie is not named but heavily implied) in a bad light. summer was clear in her intentions and securely communicated what she wanted with joseph gordon-levitt’s character, not her fault that he ignored all that and haphazardly thought she’d eventually fall in love with him. anyway. i’ll defend 500 days of summer with my life.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I thought this was interesting & a good overview of the attachment types- I didn’t like how the proposed solution for the insecure types was generally just to find a secure partner? Obviously that can help but is not the ultimate solution because that puts a lot of pressure on the secure partner. The feelings of insecure attachment styles are certainly valid and should be addressed, but not at the constant expense of the secure 😅 Otherwise, was good!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This work offers a decent introduction to attachment theory. I was anticipating more depth, so the examples seemed reductive at times. I would have appreciated information on the anxious/fearful avoidant type instead of solely focusing on the dismissive avoidant behaviors. This is especially true because a few of the dismissive examples were presented in a way that came across as minimizing emotional abuse.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I 100% read this so as to be able to discuss it with a person who has been raving about it. Though I found parts of this really dry and obvious, and other parts deeply traumatizing, I give high marks to the hilarious conversations that ensued as a result of reading it. Book: ⭐️⭐️. Hysterical follow-up: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I liked the author’s scientific approach to managing a successful relationship - much better than the abundant “dating advice” commonly found online. There are three main attachment styles “anxious”, “secure”, and “avoidant”, and the “secure” people have the most fruitful relationships. Taking the quiz in the book makes me realize that I am both “anxious” and “secure”. The anxious part of me could make me clingy and doubtful in early dating stage and beyond, but the way to become a better person in relationship is to try establish a secure foundation myself and communicate in a calm, true-to-self, and non-critical way. Lot to learn on this journey...

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I read this book on the recommendation of someone who found it useful in thinking about their own romantic interactions, and the main things I got out of it were (a) that open communication is always a good idea, and (b) that this book basically sidesteps other individual factors that play into being a human, like mental health issues and neurodiversity. After going through the exercises in this book, I didn’t really come up with an attachment type that I’d say defined me, and had to conclude that I’m a robot. It was an interesting read though, and I can see how it would be useful for someone with more cooperative brain wiring.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I put this book down for a bit last year, but highly recommend it. It's a very easy read, and definitely taught me a lot about relationships and what to look out for when it comes to forming attachments to people. Everything mentioned can easily be applied to family and friends as well as romantic partners.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Although I learned alot from this read, it is also increasingly frustrating to be self aware enough to recognize changes that you can apply willingly to yourself - but when it comes to the people around you (dating/relationships) you cannot force them to apply/learn it for themselves. Yet again another lesson in only being able to control yourself, not others and my question is where the hell are the others who are actively doing the work too ??? Seeking male with secure attachment style, SOS.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book makes a lot of broad strokes and sweeping claims. I appreciate the scientific evidence, but I didn’t always feel like the claims were fully supported. Even those that were fleshed out were driven home laboriously, repeating the same points over and over. I did learn some things from this book so I’m not mad I read it, but I have some suspicions and one glaring question: you’re therapists in New York City and couldn’t find any gay couples to include in your psychology-of-love book? Hmm… Anyways watch Couples Therapy on Showtime!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Well shit. I could have used this book a long time ago! I learned SO much about myself, but also had many aha moments in regards to past relationships and life choices in general. No matter what your relationship status is this is an extremely helpful and necessary read (I think so anyways). Side note: will also help dispel all the dysfunctional and unrealistic bullshit rom coms and Hollywood have convinced us is normal/healthy in love.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very insightful to get a view of how relationships and thus attachment styles work. It shows, by using many clear examples, how attachment styles can impact the way partners react on each other and what you can do yourself to influence/improve this, or if its better to leave... It is by no means dully written. A must read, especially if you are having the same issues in dating or relationships over and over again; it very likely has to do with attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Levine wrote a comprehensive guidebook about understanding various attachment styles. The writing style is highly practical, and it provides a detailed questionnaire to determine a couple's attachment category along with examples and fill-in-the-blank exercises. The book concludes with specific tools tailored to each attachment style to improve relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Going into it I knew I would hear concepts i’ve heard before already and could potentially walk away with no new subject matter. I enjoyed listening to the couples’ experiences from their interviews and even more liked the scenario analysis as it made my own experiences feel seen. Also reminded me that relationships should be backed by conscious decisions. :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Bardzo mi się podobała ta książka. Gdzieś tam słyszałam o stylach przywiązania, ale nigdy nie zostało mi to wytłumaczone, a autorzy tej książki robią to bardzo dobrze. Mnóstwo życiowych przykładów, opinie tego typu książek powinno się pisać po sprawdzeniu zawartych w niej rad. Teraz mogę jednak powiedzieć, że otworzyła mi oczy, na tematykę stylów przywiązania i tego, jak dobieramy sobie partnerów w związkach, szkoda, że nie przeczytałam jej kilka lat temu. Podobały mi się też ostatnie rozdziały na temat skutecznej komunikacji, generalnie polecajka

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I did NOT expect to finish this is three days, but I just wanted to know more. Excellent room for reflection and insight. Everyone should read this!! I feel a better connection with myself, how I operate, and how I’d like to go about connecting with others. This is not just about romantic relationships, though the overwhelming emphasis is on them… and what it says about romantic connection is INVALUABLE. You need to read this!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I enjoyed the way this book pushed back against the hyper individualistic view that is accepted as the cool ideal. Humans are social and need people and healthy attachments come from healthy communication with yourself and others. I found this book a refreshing update on attachment styles. It also gave good practical advice that I enjoyed sharing.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I love psychology and understanding human relationships SO this was an enjoyable read the whole way through! It’s so important to be honest and upfront about your needs. How else will you be happy? I also love how they said codependency is a part of a healthy relationship. You and your partner are a team. You should feel safe with them and trust them to take care of you and vice versa. Beautiful stuff, we love love people 💜💜💜

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This probably would have been more helpful if I was in a relationship. I did enjoy the last third where it focused on effective communication and how to change your ineffective communications into effective ones though. I don’t think I fit well into either anxious, avoidant, or secure so I didnt know what to pay attention to. I thought the book was okay, I know my friends love it though.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was recommended to me by a colleague. A doable read, quite theoretical at times, but balanced nicely with practical examples and even some helpful assignments. Overall, it’s interesting and eye-opening, especially if you want to understand your own relationship patterns better. Definitely worth picking up!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5 stars! It was a useful guide with lots of research to back up their claims. The layout of the book made it digestible and easy to follow. I also like how they included the views of a secure attachment in each section. My biggest issue is the lack of the disorganized attachment style. As someone with this attachment style, I feel like I got nothing from the book. I read the anxious and avoidant sections, and although I could relate a little to both, I think I would’ve benefited from a disorganized attachment perspective on each topic.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Sehr interessant die Attachment Theorien besser zu verstehen und anhand vieler Beispiele näher gebracht zu bekommen. Ich muss allerdings sagen, dass mir gerade bei den Paarbeispielen wo es um Care-Arbeit geht, leider überhaupt nicht berücksichtigt wird, dass ein Mann in einer hetero Beziehung nicht im Haushalt „hilft”, sondern der Haushalt genauso auch seiner ist und die Frau nicht dafür allein verantwortlich sein sollte. Dieser Gedanke hat mir gefehlt. Ansonsten supi.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Until avoidants can become self aware enough to stop breaking the hearts of us anxiously attached lovers, this is necessary how-to guide to spot red flags before you’re already in too deep.
