book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Mmm. I'm on the fence about this one. It was almost 90% irrelevant to me personally, being an old married with very good lines of communication. :) I did not like the first 40% or so. It was far too pop-sci, cherry-picked study, women's magazine guff for my taste - but perhaps since it was irrelevant to me personally I'm being rather harsh. It's also not the book I thought it was, since I was looking for something rather more about attachment in all adult relationships than heterosexual romantic ones. Oh well. However, it's the kind of thing I'd like to give to people in their twenties when they're having either dating trouble or thoughts about long-term relationships. Or people who have "turbulent" relationships at any stage. People who look to Cosmo and Hollywood for romantic advice, people who believe in one true love. People who've come out of serious relationships in their 30s with some damage and aren't sure why the people in their dating pool are so difficult to get on with. Anyone who thinks playing games like "hard to get" is normal or has tit-for-tat arguments that escalate out of all recognition. Chances are you have some qualities of the "anxious" or "avoidant" types illustrated here (or your partner does), and you'd probably get a lot out of this, despite the cringy way it's presented.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is absolutely worth reading if you're at all interested in the concepts. The attachment system theory explains a surprising amount of relationship issues. I'm somewhat familiar with the concepts because Esther Perel mentioned them in her TED Talk "The secret to desire in a long-term relationship", but it helped to read about them in more detail with examples. A couple of caveats: 1) I don't think the population breakdown is 25% Anxious, 25% Avoidant and 50% Secure worldwide, only in those Western countries they listed. I'd guess that a lot more of the populations will be Insecure in Asian countries, for example. 2) Furthermore, if you're in a relationship that is not working out independent of attachment principles, then this book will not help and will possibly confuse you. It's possible to be Secure and be with a Secure partner and have things still be incompatible, and the authors acknowledge that. I recommend The Tao Of Dating: The Smart Woman's Guide To Being Absolutely Irresistible for a more holistic view of relationships. But reading "Attached" definitely helped explain many of the guidelines mentioned in "Tao". I'm still impressed at how right Dr Ali Binazir's intuition is though.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a free audible last year. It was interesting to listen to it. It covers the research in adult attachment and found that adult attachments are the same styles as infants, anxious, avoidant and secure. Then it covered how the different combinations might react to each. There is a survey that the reader can take to determine their style and some hints on how to determine the partners style. The next part covers basically effective communication skills. For an audio self help at first it seemed kind of silly but then I realized that a person can access each chapter to access the different parts so it actually could be used as a self help. An interesting fact for those that are older and still in the dating field. The pool of possibilities are mostly made up of avoidants because they are the ones who don't get married or attached so easily. It isn't that they don't want to be in an intimate relationship but their style keeps them from it. Overall, it was okay, the readers were clear and easy to follow. The material was useful and I don't really need it personally at my age but we all can get better at effective communication but I think it will be a handy resource for my job working with people.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Simple concept - but brilliant ones usually are. It comes from much more academic research (see John Bowlby), but is written here in plain English, with stories and checklists, thus putting this book in the Self-Help category. The central idea is pretty powerful, no matter the wrapping. It allows us to reframe relationships in - I believe - a very helpful, non-judgmental, efficient paradigm. No more Mars or Venus, codependent, independent and Prince C/Harming, no gender, cultural, sexual wars. No - just the middle balanced way (Secure attachment style people) and the usual 2 extremes (Avoidant and Anxious) who tend to specifically find and hurt one another. Yes, this will help. My whole family is Avoidant, and I am, perhaps inevitably, Anxious. I only ever knew, loved, dated Avoidant people (what a miserable realization!). To spare myself, I started acting very Avoidant, and actually taking on some of those traits has helped me be more balanced. I’ve been working on Secure - it’s looming over the horizon, yay! I just wish the book dug into more specificities - what happens when 2 Anxious hook up? Can people change their style in different areas of their lives? Any links with narcissism? - but it's pretty damn good and self sufficient as it is;0)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I got this book from my therapist and I finally figure out my attachment style. I'm anxious and this explained a lot not only about my love life but my friendship life. It showed me that I have many friends that are avoidant type and a few secure types. The thing I hated about this book was that for an anxious person like myself who is married, this book caused panic attacks and made it seem that there was no hope with my secure type husband. I hated the book until part three. The book lacks better examples, most of the examples are way too black and white and I think most people can relate to them. Do I think this book is correct about the emotional attachments styles? Yes. Do I think people can change their emotional attachment styles? Yes! The book is good for singles or even people who are divorced. The biggest thing this book lacks is better advice for anxious people and how to "control" their emotions better to reach a better form of communication with their partner. It also doesn't tell them how to soothe themselves to keep a calm mind. This book contains a lot of good information but lacks advice how to achieve what they are aiming at. The book needs BETTER advice, BETTER tips, and BETTER suggestions for all types. Lacks better examples and details.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Self-help books aren't really my jam, and I'm also not on the market for a lover. However, this one came recommended from a few sources ("life-changing," as per one), and I did think it had some interesting points. In a nutshell: we're all predisposed to one of three attachment styles, and recognizing yours (and others') will help you find more satisfaction in relationships. However, our attachment styles can also change, and so we're not simply doomed to be Avoidant or Anxious (or even guaranteed to be Secure) forever. The book also gives some tips for Effective Communication™, which, if a bit oversimplified, are still good to remember. If you're a person who wants to be in a lasting relationship and repeatedly finds yourself struggling with that (or enjoys books that cause you to begin categorizing everyone around you--ahem, Art of Speed Reading People --I'd definitely recommend this read. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I read this book on a friend's suggestion. I open with this sentence to form the premise that I don't usually read books on relationships. I was initially skeptical that this book would also turn out to be one of those romantic "doctrines" that try to tell you how men and women should act in order to secure a love interest. Examples of these doctrines include women playing coy/hard to get, men pursuing, people acting uninterested or hiding their feelings, which in my opinion is pure BS. I was pleasantly surprised that this book is anything but that. I like the author's approach and language - it attempts to provide scientific evidence for the three behaviors without getting too clinical. And as you read the book, you would be able to exactly pinpoint what kind you are, or were, at a certain point in time. It also helps affirm that what you thought were only your abstract thoughts about relationships, can, in fact, be extended to most people (i.e. You are not alone). I also appreciate how the author draws parallels between relationship behaviors to the mother-child or person-pet bond. I am positive everyone would benefit from reading this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The "Attachment theory" presented in the book is interesting, but I'm afraid that it only provides a superficial answer to any deep-rooted problems you have. Imagine this book is like a band-aid given to people with ruptured organs. The anxious ones are reassured that they are perfectly fine, it's not their fault that their relationships do not work out, and they just need to find the ones that can satisfy their attachment needs. At the same time, the avoidant is portrayed as psychopaths that avoid intimacy at all costs, as toxic people that the anxious ones (or anyone!) should avoid. This kind of portrayal is unhelpful at best, and damaging at worst. The book never discussed why people behave in anxious or avoidant manners, what gives secure people such security, what made them that way... It does not encourage readers to find ways to find the root cause and fix what is broken inside, but tell them to find external solutions. It is better to realize what is your current state, what's the desired outcome, and gradually change your behaviors so you can better co-exist with everyone. Categorization is helpful, as long as you remember that human is multi-dimensional.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Últimamente estoy muy interesada en los libros de psicología y, concretamente, en los de psicología de pareja. ¿No es fascinante ver los nexos de unión entre el mundo de la ciencia y el del amor? Al igual que me sucedió con Los límites del amor de Walter Riso, Maneras de amar me ha parecido una obra imprescindible para saber cómo establecer un equilibrio proporcionado y satisfactorio entre el amarse a uno mismo y amar a otra persona sin egoísmo. Eso sí, mientras que el libro de Riso pretendía ser un manual sobre el límite entre las relaciones sanas y las tóxicas, esta obra de Levine y Heller es más un estudio científico que clasifica los tipos de apegos que las personas adultas pueden desarrollar, siendo estos el apego seguro, el apego ansioso y el apego evasivo. Este libro te ayuda a identificar tu tipo de apego y el de tu pareja, analiza cómo se relacionan los miembros de parejas de diferentes apegos y da claves para tener más empatía y autoconocimiento. Tal vez me ha faltado que se analizaran las parejas minoritarias de ansioso + ansioso y evasivo + evasivo, pero a grandes rasgos es un libro absolutamente interesante y necesario para aumentar nuestra inteligencia emocional.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think attachment theory has a lot of merit but this book is so filled with contradictions I cannot see how it’s helpful as an analysis of how attachment theory translates into relationships… for example: the book states that your attachment style comes from childhood and summarizes attachment theory, but then states that your attachment style can change partner to partner and over time. If your style is a product of your childhood, as stated, how is it that each partner can evoke a different attachment style? This book also suffers from pathologizing normal behaviours… sometimes someone isn’t just avoidant, they are seriously not that into you… based on how the theory is laid out in this book, the same person can be avoidant with one person and anxiously attached to the next. This would be much better explained by that person’s desire for the other, vs a learned relational style… There are so many exceptions and caveats to the application of attachment theory in this book that I think that this book is popularized because it introduces attachment theory to a general audience but a very simple stress test of it’s applications shows way too many holes.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book attempts to summarise the scientific research on adult attachment and provides tools to identify different types and how they relate to each other in relationships. Accordingly there are basically 3 different attachment types: Secure, Anxious and Avoidant. The formation of these types are speculatively credited to evolutionary biology, but also developmental psychology. These attachment types thus become character traits and manifest themselves in adult relationships. The book does good work to create awareness on anxious and avoidant behaviour in relationships. It suggests that the readers both self-assess to find out their type and to look out for cues in their partners. There is merit in understanding certain behaviour patterns, but I wasn’t convinced that these are set in stone and universal. I believe every relationship establishes unique attachment dynamics and particular behaviours that cannot be narrowed down to three types. Nevertheless, the research is useful, and it is worth expanding our understanding of psychological elements that are relevant to relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: While the key takeaways of the book were disclosed in the early chapter that explains the three attachment styles, the exams throughout the book were incredibly helpful. Learning how attachment styles can evolve over time or with different partners was incredibly enlightening. Loved the self reflection that this book led to and the patterns that it helped me find in my own behavior.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 2.5 stars rounded down. This book had a lot of promise, but it's written as though the two authors both have anxious attachment styles and dated avoidant attachment styles. So many of the examples of avoidant attachment styles are people being straight up mean/borderline abusive/belittling/etc, which is different than the way I imagine most avoidant people actually are (e.g. perhaps needing more space or distance than an anxious person). Like: "Throughout their hiking trip in Guatemala,...Gary would walk ahead of Sue, occasionally making snide comments about how lazy and incompetent she was for walking so slowly." Avoidant? Maybe. Complete asshole? Yes. These are not necessarily the same thing lol. In broad strokes, the suggestion for anxious people is to avoid dating avoidant people. The suggestion for avoidant people is to change lol. C'monnnnnnn. Maybe it's true if you believe the examples in the book are what actually constitutes an avoidant attachment style, but I think they're pretty far removed from typical or average and reflective of people being jerks more than anything.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Given how ubiquitous the attachment theory and the corresponding “labels” are in the popular culture, I was excited to look at the actual research, or at least a book based on it. Many facts and recommendations were new to me. Things that jump to mind: * I loved how, at least when giving classification tests, each attachment style was represented by a set of beliefs or typical behaviors pertinent to it. Not only it shows nuance and the spectrum nature of the styles, it also gives a clue as to how one could address some of these beliefs to change their attachment style. * Another new finding: while I did know that attachment styles can change in adult age, it was interesting to learn that the correlation between the attachment style of a child and the style when they become adult is only ~0.35. Gives hope! * Examples of different dynamics were enlightening too. I must say, though. Some of the statements felt a bit too black-and-while and categorical. Made me question the truthfulness and nuance of everything else. I hope, I could eventually check the sources :) Overall, enjoyable and thought-provoking book. Definitely deserves a re-read not in audio someday!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I wasn’t gonna review this book cause it’s obviously a personal issue and I’m not really a self help person but I know therapy is more beneficial when you do homework so here we are! It’s so corny but I feel like this changed everything. I really hope I’m able to retain all the amazing advice I learned in this book but this is definitely one I want to purchase so I can always reference it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A super interesting concept about the ways in which we attach to our significant others. The theory here is that there are three styles and we each present with one of them. The styles all make perfect sense to me, but the theory is that only 1/4 of people change their attachment style every 4 years. According to the theory, some styles go well together and others are doomed. My husband and I have been together for 6 years and we've each been through all of the three styles over the course of our relationship; mostly the changes are triggered by life events. He was avoidant when we started dating and I was anxious. If I'd blown him off (as the book would have recommended), then I would have missed him developing into a secure and him pulling me into a secure attachment style. So, while I think the concept is interesting, it is a bit limiting and seems to have an all-or-nothing approach that certainly didn't completely resonate with my life and relationship experience. Still a good read and plenty of interesting and applicable insights can be found within.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book greatly simplifies relationship dynamics to the point where its only fault would be that of over-simplifying it. Attachment theory on the surface sounds completely plausible and I would definitely recommend this book to those individuals who find themselves constantly in "bad" relationships because they would likely benefit the most from it. Essentially Attachment theory is an evolution from human infant psychology when researchers realized that adults do not differ much from infants. Humans are social creatures that thrive best when in intimate relationships with others. People are often ill-suited for navigating the challenges of how to achieve that level of intimacy they need. Most problems occur when people don't understand their own or their partners' attachment style and end up paired with someone whose style contradicts their own. Avoidant and Anxious are the two styles that should pretty much avoid every being in a relationship together. All in all a fascinating theory that simplifies the relationship-drama we seem to be so addicted to.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: What I love most about this book is that it does not try to change you or convince you that you should be/feel differently. Your relationship expectations are what they are and it is perfectly ok to have those specific needs: to desire to be loved or expect support from your partner, or be in pain/disappointed when a relationship ends. I also found of great value the differentiation between love and attachment and the bluntness about how important it is to know what kind of personality suits our own style of attachment. Even if we cannot change who we are, becoming aware of certain un-serving behavior can help ones dating life tremendously. Moreover, the information and techniques regarding effective communication can not only be used in romantic relationships but also in our every day to day life. It is a very common mistake we make: when we find ourselves in a conflict situation, we instantly take it as a personal attack and react defensively. Listening to what the person is trying to say and effectively communicating can save us a lot of unnecessary drama and wasted energy.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
reviewer_name: Sandra The Old Woman in a Van
review_body: I have already gifted this book to two people so that must say something about what I think of its relevance. This is a very assessable book for anyone wanting to understand relationships and attachment. It doesn't require a lot of inner work on how you got to where you are or why you mite have a certain attachment profile, it just goes with what you have. So if you struggle with relationships this is an excellent book to help you decipher what might be going awry. I think solutions might be a little more complicated than just identifying your attachment style and commiting to some new behaviors though. I would have given this book 5 stars if they would have pushe dthe reader a little further to explore or peel back the onion on why they may be anxious or avoidant - and to consider working with a therapist experienced with attachment issues. But that said this is an exceptional, assessable book - with questionnaires and ample examples. I did find the tables hard to read on my kindle paperwhite - I could not enlarge them and had to work hard to read them.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Uhhhh this was a miss. The message seemed to be that your attachment style is valid as long as it's not avoidant lol. It seemed overly sympathetic with anxious tendencies and then really demonised avoidance. Obvs reading this as someone with a tendency towards avoidance I didn't love that lol. The solution seemed to be for anxious people to match up with secure people who would put up with their behaviours and kind of putting it on the partner to dance around these issues as opposed to getting therapy and doing the work on yourself. I already know a lot about attachment theory from studying my psychology degree and I was hoping for some new insights but I don't think i really got a lot from this book. I think it would be good for someone anxious who knows nothing about attachment and wants to be absolved of 90% of the responsibility for the way they act in relationships lol If you actually wanted to learn about how to act in less toxic ways or how to handle an insecure partner, you'd be better off finding some reddit forums or going to therapy

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: When my friend Jen recommended this book to me 2 years ago, I gave her a dark look for her efforts. Much to her credit, she knew exactly why. "I know," she said, "The secondary title makes me want to stab myself in the eye. But the theory is interesting." And after 2 years wasting away on my shelf, the book jumped out at me as I was packing for a long weekend. If this book were a cogently written 5 page article, I would have loved it. While there are significant generalizations that are not universally true, the theory of attachment laid forth is an interesting prism in which to view romantic and other relationships and forced me to think about my past and current relationships differently. However, as a 270 page book, it's wearying and the last 70 pages are a particular slog. Well-worth the investment of half an hour to read the first 50 pages. Hopefully, less compulsive souls than I am can stop reading there.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I've had an anxious style for a while and this has been very shell-opening. I really enjoyed the examples in the book and the message: communicate your needs wholely and securely (not 'protest behavior') and how your partner responds will tell you if a relationship is feasible and desirable. When? Because you can't only talk about your needs 24/7 when you feel emotional or like you want to protest (be snide, mean, back them into a corner). "Unlike effective communication protest behavior never gives you the opportunity to unequivocally address your concerns. Your partner may respond negatively, but you're never sure if he or she is responding to your need or to your protest behavior." "Secure principles for making conflict work: 1. Show basic concern for the other person's well-being. 2. Maintain focus on the problem at hand. 3. Refrain from generalizing the conflict. 4. Be willing to engage. 5. Effectively communicate feelings and needs."

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Great introduction to the concept of attachment theory, guiding you in how to assess your attachment style and that of your romantic partner(s), and how to use that understanding to be mindful of pitfalls and problems that can arise in relationships between people with different attachment styles - common misunderstandings, sources of conflict, and ways in which people can reinforce rather than break cycles of harmful behaviour through simple misunderstandings and lack of awareness. Worth a read if you want to invest some time in introspection and working on yourself and potentially your relationships. My criticism would be that it's very heteronormative, and the language feels a little clunky in that it's constantly referring to theoretical partners with wording like "he or she", i.e. "Consider if he or she has an anxious or avoidant style" etc, when it could just be inclusive and linguistically simpler if it used "they."

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think there are some aspects of this book that were quite helpful in determining my own attachment style and how that manifests in my life. Unfortunately, most of the examples were too simple and didn’t taken into account external factors like trauma or emotional/mental well-being. There seems to be a gross bias toward the secure and anxious attachment styles and most examples villainized the avoidant person and victimized the anxious person. While there were tidbits sprinkled throughout the book on how to assuage an anxious person’s doubts and protest behaviors, there didn’t seem to be an equal amount of effort put into how to help an avoidant person when their attachment style rears its head. The general conclusion is that it is not worth pursuing any type of romantic relationship with an avoidant person but an anxious person can be successful in a relationship as long as it is with a secure person.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This review is limited to the audio book. I felt like I would have gotten more out of actually reading the book instead of listening to it. This is a rarity for me. I enjoy listening to books during longer drives and while doing chores. As a happily married man I do think I was able to identify my role in our marriage and how my wife and I can better interact and live with each other. Marriage is work. It's happy work but work nonetheless. This book is probably more helpful for people who are a little less self aware and are single. I fall into neither of these categories. I did learn some very interesting things about the research in this book. I'm guessing I would have given the book another star had I actually read it in paper form or if I were younger and single. Reviews are so damn personal aren't they?

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: One of the best books I have EVER read on love and relationships—and I've read ALOT of them in my 51 years. As someone with an anxious attachment style, the chapter about "me" (aka my attachment style) described me EXACTLY and is what's been going on in my head/behaviour with every single relationship I've had since my mid-twenties (all with people who have avoidant attachment styles). After reading this book, I feel better equipped to screen out unsuitable people who will play havoc with my attachment system (and ultimately leave me unhappy and unfulfilled). Having said that, this book doesn't judge attachment styles. They are what they are. If you identify as avoidant, you will benefit from the strategies detailed in the book too. If you are in a relationship, you will also benefit from reading this book. I can't speak highly enough of it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I found this book helpful in explaining how attachment styles work in relationships and contribute to their success or dysfunction. However, I think the book focused too much on the attachment styles manifestations (in a repetitive way) and not enough on why and how people's attachment styles are the way they are. It also seemed to glorify people with a secure attachment style and talk about people with insecure attachment style in a pathologizing way, disregarding the social factors that contributed to their insecurity. I also found it to be extremely heteronormative, with only one mention of a same sex couple among the many case examples. This book effectively explains some of the manifestations of attachment styles in adulthood, but definitely does not provide a complete framework for understanding attachment theory.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book proposes a split of human attachment systems into 3 categories, based on 2 decades of studies across human relationship psychology: 1. Anxious , the needy type. 2. Avoidant , the type which likes to keep their distance in relationships. 3. Secure , the type which communicates well. At times, these categorizations might feel too rigid. Illustrated in the book are: - characterizations for each of these, - tips for handling each category and - tips for managing relationships depending on the combination of attachment systems in the relationship. Also, the book serves to guide the reader towards improving his current relationship model by looking back at his or her behavior in previous relationships and how this could have been better managed with the information from the book. A useful book for the information it proposes to provide.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is based on research that divides the adult attachment styles to three: Anxious, secured and avoidant. There are many truths in it and even some self-testing questionnaire to check where you’re at, and some good advice for your specific attachment type. But in my gut feeling, the human rainbow of possibilities can’t possibly be divided to just three, and while I did find myself agreeing on many subjects, I do believe some of us are a blended mixture of each of those three attachment types combined, with some traits stronger and some less strong. The problem is that this book doesn’t really dive into the question of those different balanced and mixtures and keeps those three types as hard, distinguished facts. Still, it’s a very good take on relationships, perhaps a bit psychologically simplistic, but full of interesting things to think about nonetheless.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Heard a lot about this book and just got around to read it . Found it Eye opening , not the typical relationship advice as it made me realize how damaging some of the advise we hear on social media or by people around us can be . Its applicable to any relationship not just a romantic one. Fun to apply to yourself and couples around you. Key points for me ; -Understanding the different styles can make you more empathic to people with any of the 3 styles as you realize why they do what they do. -Helps name another aspect of a person that can make them a good or bad fit regardless of values and character. Easier to name pinpoint why someone is suitable or not. -More accepting and at ease with your and other people’s needs. -Brilliance of clear communication , Loved the communication correction /rephrasing examples feel it’s useful and a good reminder for anyone.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5* Sách về ứng dung thuyết gắn bó hiếm hoi được dịch ra tiếng Việt. Hiểu biết về thuyết gắn bó giúp chúng ta biết cách đối thoại khi những căng thẳng trong mối quan hệ xuất hiện. Góc nhìn từ thuyết gắn bó sẽ giúp chúng ta hiểu được những phản ứng như chạy trốn, than phiền của đối phương... không mang mục đích tấn công mà thể hiện rằng họ đang cảm thấy bất an trong mối quan hệ. Phần lớn thời gian trong sách phân tích về các kiểu gắn bó như lo âu, tránh né, an toàn. Người đọc còn có thể biết được kiểu gắn bó của mình qua các bài test khác nhau. Phần giải pháp để đối diện với các kiểu gắn bó có phần giới hạn và không có tính áp dụng cao. Sách phù hợp cho người muốn tìm hiểu về cách mà chúng ta tương tác với những mối quan hệ thân thiết. Là nền tảng khá tốt để tiếp tục đào sâu nghiên cứu.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: كتاب رائع تمنيت لو كان قد تُرجم من لغته الأساسية عند مروري به مصادفه ، لأجده لي زوايا مكتبة جرير بنسخته الأولى.. تعتبر العلاقات موضوع شائك دائمًا ولأجل هذا تستمر له البحوث والدراسات ومثل هذه الكتب الرائعة. ينتمي الأفراد سواء كانو متزوجين ام غير ذلك إلى ثلاث أنماط أساسية ✔️نمط التعلق الآمن، والذي يشعر بالإرتياح تجاه الحميمية ✔️قلق، ويميل الى القلق بشأن قدرة شريكة على مبادلته العاطفه ✔️إجتنابي، يساوي بين الحميمية وبين فقدانه للإستقلال مايجعله يحاول باستمرار تقليل فرص التقرب. يحتوي الكتاب على العديد من الأمثلة والإستراتيجيات التي تمكنك من للإنتقال لمستوى آمن وواعي من العلاقه باستخدام أداه رائعة تم ذكرها وهي "التواصل الفعال" والتي من شأنها قلب الموازين في أي علاقة تقريبًا. ✨إقتباسات✨ - تعتبر العلاقات إحدى أكثر التجارب البشرية المثمرة، ولكن على الرغم من الأهمية التي نوليها لعلاقاتنا الأكثر حميمية، فإن معظمنا لايزال يجهل الكثير جدًا عن العلم الكامن وراء العلاقات العاطفية.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An easy read for technical writing, but it didn't wow me as much as other psychology & self help books have. I expect I'd have a much different reaction if I had read this 6 years ago, or 3 years ago. I probably would have saved myself (and others, I can admit) some heartbreak if I was more aware of my reactions at the time - both anxious & avoidant - but alas, hindsight's 20/20. Some updated examples (the book felt so dated to me!) would be great, but I also wouldn't have minded leaving those out & just focusing on the analysis. I want to do some of the exercises in the book, but as a (seemingly) secure person now, I'm not sure if digging into the "why" of the past is necessary. It's probably enough to know I've been on both sides of the coin & now feel and am secure! (Most likely because of the bad experiences, as the authors state - they can change your attachment!)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm a psychologist in private practice and have recommended this book to quite a few clients. Unlike other self-help books which can really be hit or miss in terms of appealing to a wide audience, this one has been deemed excellent by every person I loaned it out to and several went out and got their own copies so they could mark them up with notes. Great distillation of attachment research into useable insights to help the reader understand their own romantic relationships. Why do I keep getting involved with partners who reject me? Oh- I am an anxious type who has been pairing up with avoidants! How can I know if a partner is securely attached? What are the warning signs that a potential partner has attachment issues? Questionnaires and checklists included.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I usually don't like 'relationship books', given how sometimes they feel a little airy-fairy in intent. However, I really enjoyed Attached. The breakdown of attachment styles made significant sense, and I could see how I fell into the same traps over and over again, and it offers clarity to situations when I would think "I'm acting crazy! Why am I so irrational!!??", to expand it to a more chemical and psychological response as someone who is anxiously attached. Although the 3 categories may seem quite simplistic, I found it extremely helpful in creating frameworks for me to better discern and maintain my current and future relationships, and better reflect on those I've had in the past. Highly recommend this book. It's also really great "book club" fodder.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Absolutely loved this book. Will definitely read it again. It really has opened my eyes to the attachment styles that I see in the people I have relationships with, whether it be the relationships that I share with my family, friends, or guys I date. Having a better understanding of one's attachment style is so important because it helps you know why they behave the way they do and how to respond to certain behavior. It helps you recognize their thought-process and prepares you better in what to expect when it comes to their actions. Everyone should read this book to have a better understanding in how people work and avoid time-wasters as well as how to improve relationships and, most importantly, communication in our overall relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I’ve enjoyed this book, I felt it was a great introduction to the adult attachment theory, a quick easy read, that explained a lot of patterns we tend to follow in relationships not just romantic ones. With that said it doesn’t exempt the authors from a bit of shortcomings: 1) As I understood people tend to fall on either or group, but I think it could be more of a spectrum rather than rigid categories. 2) I felt it soothes the anxiously attached people by repeating over and over again that all they need to do is find a secure partner and stay away from avoidants, exempting them from self reflection and improvement to try and understand why they are anxious to begin with. 3) I felt it harshly portrayed avoidants as cold and uncaring people.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Gosh, this book is like having to read through 20 issues of Cosmo, and about as helpful. I mean, yes, basically, at a very basic level, it explains attachment theory. And it has quizzes!!! Who doesn’t love a self help book with quizzes?! But I feel really sorry for anyone “avoidant” who accidentally stumbles upon (or is forced to read) this book. It caters solely to anxiously attached individuals, doesn’t deal with disorganized attachment at all, doesn’t go into tackling core wounds or how to repair those wounds, and instead just gives Cosmo level relationship advice. Are there a couple of useful nuggets in here? Sure. And some helpful phrasing for those unsure of their wording in partner discussions? Yeah. Other than that? Pass.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I thought this was interesting! My only complaint is that I felt like he was saying, “if you’re anxious you will have a hard life and often be stressed, if you’re avoidant you are sort of a jerk, if you’re secure I have nothing to tell you…you’re perfect.”

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a great book to understand the different characteristics of attachment styles. The book claims that having effective dependency with a partner can fuel one's own growth and make one more daring. Infact having a secure base can encourage one to be more creative, pursue dreams, and take risks. The author provides questionnaires to guide an individual to identify their attachment style and their partners. The book provides a space for readers to introspect on their past relationship and helps identify things they can work one. The key takeaway from this book is that having effective communication regarding your needs and expectation with your partner is the key for the relationship to succeed. Would totally recommend this book :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book would be useful for people who fall hard for each new romantic partner and keep getting dumped. As someone in a happy long-term relationship, I didn't find it very interesting. The primary recommendation to be up-front about your needs, and to walk away with haste from someone who doesn't want to meet them, seems reasonable. I think that both of these pieces of advice would be hard to carry out for those who have been dumped a lot. For this reason, this is not advice one would probably want to give to a friend or family member without careful consideration of how to deliver it in a manner that it would be welcome.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was recommended to me as part of a course on the science of happiness. It opens with the assertion that the modern approach to relationships often emphasises independence and emotional self-sufficiency, and that this can impede the development of intimacy as a result. Also, that intimacy promotes happiness and that it is therefore worth learning to value dependency. The balance of the book deals with the three main attachment styles; namely, secure, anxious and avoidant. I found the style of the book easy to read and understand. For anyone who has experienced repeated relationship problems, i’m sure it would be extremely helpful.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Super quick and easy read. I found it really clear cut and simple, and fascinating. I already knew about attachment theory, and how people are generally classed into secure, anxious or avoidant... yet this gave me more information and understanding. There’s an aspect with which this book allowed me to feel into the idea of a secure and respectful attentive partner in a new way. As a single person happily choosing a period of celibacy, it was interesting how this book made me start to want looking for a partner. I’m not going to yet, but it was nice to feel that impulse. It also gave me a lot of hope and further solidified my framework of what I’m seeking in another (and myself).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It felt too simplistic and shallow. I disagreed with some of the implications the author's made about avoidantly attached people and didn't think they said very interesting things about the desires of avoidants. I also don't think they thought about how a history of abuse or mental illness could affect the attachment style, nor how gender dynamics played a significant role in most of the relationship examples they gave. Two stars because the concept was new to me and I do think there is merit to some of what they said, particularly in the basic concept of avoidant, anxious, and secure attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 2.5 stars. I didn’t love how the author(s) showed extra sympathy towards ppl with anxious attachment style, but portrayed the avoidant attachment style as selfish and abusive people, all the while claiming there’s no good or bad attachment styles, only different needs. There’s just a distinct bias, which made people who have the avoidant style like myself, feel invalidated and unworthy of respect and love (effective communication ;). Also why were most examples of anxious AS women and avoidant men (ughhh the sexism). The good thing is, the book is short….and I guess I did learn more about intimate relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It’s cute. It’s mainly like a social-psyche book about the attachment styles and the importance of recognizing traits of the 3 main ones and strategies to improve your own style. It rlly emphasized the importance of using open and honest communication with ur partner and traits of the emotionally immature. V good read for anyone currently in a relationship, looking to be in one, or just getting out of a 1.5 month situationship that ended suddenly with no closure as to y, especially since she demonstrated interest in furthering the relationship multiple times throughout (no, I will not elaborate).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Meh. I could see how the information contained in this book could be helpful to someone. That someone, however, is not me. I've been in enough relationships, made enough mistakes and learned valuable lessons from each of them. Nothing someone else has written will ever be more helpful to me than that. If anything, reading this book assured me that I do have a thorough understanding of the way I am. It is interesting to have some of the research gathered in one place like this... though, honestly, I think for any of the stats I'd rather just look them up on the internet.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A straightforward look at adult attachment styles and how they affect and determine our relationships. The theory is very simple: people fall into one of three basic attachment styles--secure, anxious, or avoidant. The way those play out in relationships depends greatly on the attachment style of the other person. This very basic concept actually explains so much about the dynamics of interpersonal relationships. This book would be a useful tool for anyone in any phase of a relationship (looking for a partner, dating, in a longterm relationship etc.)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I really don't like self help books. However, I didn't find Attached to be that offensive. The authors provide several different angles for each definition and occasionally root these angles in psychology. It was nice to have these definitions of attachment, but I'm not sure anyone needs to go through the entire book to understand these. I wish the book went into a little more detail about the other contributing factors to attachment style beyond childhood security. As an aside, I'm totally not waiting for anyone to call (anymore).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Most relationship advice really teaches you to avoid being needy by denying your needs. This book has a radical thesis: We should be looking for people who can actually meet these needs, instead of putting up with people who won't. Suddenly, my relationship problems (and even that of my friends) make sense in a whole new light. I have a better sense now of who to look for and who to avoid. The big takeaway: Learning to be honest and unapologetic about what you need is way better than expecting your partner to read your mind.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Okay, so reading a relationship self-help book is sort of weird when you're in a happy marriage, but I'm fascinated by attachment parenting and a good friend told me this book uses attachment theory to explore adult romantic relationships, which sounded awesome. It was a pretty interesting read, particularly as I tried to categorize myself, my friends, and our various romantic relationships, but I jumped around a lot when I didn't feel like something applied to me. I think this would be a great book for people dating or in a relationship that they're not sure about.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very helpful advice, however, as an avoidant attachment type, I feel the book unfairly depicts avoidants. Although it discusses the avoidant-anxious trap, it places the blame on the avoidant, and fails to acknowledge that when anxious partners needs go unmet, despite if avoidant use "effective communication," they can become abusive. Avoidants may be aware they are mistreating the anxious, but the anxious can grow manipulative, using verbal and physical abuse to regain control. Good book, but lacks a holistic picture.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book is great and necessary for everyone to read to learn how to effectively communicate with their loved ones, not just romantic partners. It provides a lot of insight into our attachment styles and creates awareness about mistakes we all make when engaging in any form of conflict. Three stars because the book used very cis/heteronormative examples of love and relationships, as well as conventional forms of intimacy. It could have definitely been more LGBTQ friendly and geared towards different ways of loving/experiencing intimacy.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Read this based on a good recommendation and have now recommended it to many friends! It is quite concentrated but still a good read. "Attached" focuses on romantic relationships but the theory stretches to all other relationships as well, so it is manifoldly an interesting read! These types of basics should really be thought at high school instead of pure history of psychology. I recommend it to everyone who wants to read about attachment theory and how different attachment styles affect our everyday lives. 👌🏻💖

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Definitely helpful, especially if one is new to the concepts this book focuses on. It can be an extremely validating book, but also a frustrating one. Occasional landmines of irrationality, such as the idea that experiences can only be meaningful when shared, or that avoidants can only improve by hitting rock bottom. Still, I feel I understand myself and others more clearly after reading this book, and for that I am grateful. Confirmed my belief that direct and effective communication is always the way to go.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Friend recommended this to me a year ago and just got around to it. Good intro to attachment theory but oh my god there is a severe bias against avoidant types and they are villianized throughout while anxious types are coddled. Pretty much nothing useful/constructive to secure types. Major takeaways are de-escalation of conflict and being assertive/open about what you want out of a relationship. Communication is key. But these things could have been distilled down quicker without the hundreds of repetitive case studies (mostly between anxious and avoidant types)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A quick and helpful read on attachment styles and healthy relationships. I wish I read this book sooner and read more into attachment styles to better understand myself as a person and how I express myself in relationships. A big portion of this book is helpful for anxiously attached people in particular which may be why I enjoyed it as much as I did. This book wasn’t as in depth as I would’ve liked and I still have so many questions, but for an introduction to attachment styles, I think that this book is a treasure - especially for anxiously attached types.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Temat omówiony w książce w zupełności nie potrzebuje aż takiej objętości tekstu - 1/3 spokojnie by wystarczyła. Sama warstwa merytoryczna całkiem okej, chociaż na moje odczucie zbyt dużo zostało wytłumaczone wyłącznie jednym, prostym kryterium jakim jest tytułowa teoria więzi. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I found this book very helpful. The infrastructure it creates to help us understand our natural tendencies towards relationships was very informative. I especially appreciated the plethora of real examples outlined in detail that I could relate to and see myself in and how I’m guilty of falling into those same traps. Perhaps a little heavy handed at times and focusing too much on anxious people, but overall I enjoyed it and feel I’ve already begun implementing some of the principles on my own life.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book can be very useful to people as a compatibility decoder. Based on what you learn about yourself, you can spot clues in other people’s behavior that will help you realize if you will be compatible based on attachment styles. I wish this book had delved more into attachment theory beyond significant others to more authoritatively touch on friendship, family, work etc. Also would have been nice if they just used they instead of spelling out she or he literally every time or worse s/he.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a great book. I did not know anything about the 3 attachment styles. Those styles are anxious, secure, and avoidant. I wish I had learned this information when I was 18 years old because I think it would have helped me avoid a lot of heartbreak. I am anxiously attached, and I have always found myself with the avoidant attachment style. This is not a good match. It explains how to communicate affectively and how to avoid the wrong relationship if you're not in it already. Overall, it's a great book on understanding adult attachment styles. I highly recommend it!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very useful at this particular point in my life, going through a separation. Allowed me to understand myself and my wife better. Learned effective ways to communicate which will hopefully help us if we decide to give our marriage another try. In the meantime, I need to really try to remember those subconscious impulses that are maladaptive and harmful, and which drove us apart. Good for anyone who is going through a painful time in their relationship and are trying to understand why this might be happening and how to, maybe, fix things.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It breaks down three attachment styles: anxious, avoidant and secure, and discusses how they interact. It's the best relationship book I've ever read, and it made me feel much less pathetic after getting slapped with the codependent label by an insensitive therapist. Also, it made me feel much better about my decision to end a painful 15 year friendship with an avoidant who belittled me. This book is a must read for anyone who resembles the stump in The Giving Tree.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Pop psychology at its best, and most useful. The book is devoted to understanding one's own attachment style, and using that knowledge to improve romantic relationships. I think this book goes beyond that by promoting healthy self-reflection and teaches actionable techniques that improve communication, all of which are applicable to non-romantic relationships, as well. Now I just have to get all the other people I've ever had difficult relationships with to read it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A good baseline introduction to adult attachment research. The sections on anxious/avoidant pairings gave me an understanding of the thread connecting my previous relationships. What is usually brushed off as bad taste has now been refined to be an unrelenting faith in the brief promising highs that accompany avoidant emotional unavailability. This book could use an update to be less focused on heterosexual masc/femme relationship dynamics.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is unfortunately (but understandably) named like a BS self-help/relationship book but inside, attachment theory provides some valuable research-backed insight into human behavior. In the same vein as The Four Tendencies by Gretchen Rubin, which I also recently read - no single model can explain all human behavior, but I do think this is a useful framework for understanding how people behave in relationships (not just romantic ones).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book is amazing. It is talking about the attachment styles between lovers and how they can affect the relationship. It will help you understand a lot about your partner. The most important thing that the book is discussing things based on a scientific experiments and researchs. It is opinion, it is science. The book will help you understand what kind of attachment style are you and your partner style as well. It is very important book to read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A good introduction to the attachment styles that helped clarify a few things for me in light of recent events. However it is just that – introductory – and is also quite repetitive. Probably less useful for avoidant-attached people, as it has the tendency to demonise. As an anxious/avoidant myself, I did find it illuminating in quite a few ways. This is one you can easily dip in and out of to get what you need.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book gives insight into the different types of attachments you can have in a relationship. I was surprised at how interesting the book was in terms of relationship attachment styles and and how accurate the details could be. I really enjoyed the book and I would recommend this to anybody who has an interest in learning about relationship dynamics or why people behave the way that they do in difficult relationships.

review_body: DNFing at page 85 not because I didn’t find parts of this insightful and interesting, but because of the clear bias against people with avoidant attachment. The section on “why you shouldn’t date avoidant people as an anxiously attached person” was the final straw, which I say as an anxiously attached person. It’s a shame because I really got something from parts of this and was looking forward to gaining some more insight, but it is hard to ignore the anti-avoidant rhetoric.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Well-written, with a nice combination of friendly pop psych and some serious research. I gritted my teeth against the often repeated assertion that everyone wants to be in a relationship, but then that's what we'd expect from an attachment-avoidant type like me, isn't it? Overall, very interesting and probably quite useful.

So simple yet so true. I highly recommend this book to pretty much anyone. I recommended it to several of my friends who also recommended it to their friends.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Great science-based self-helpy book about attachment theory and how it applies to all our relationships. It's laid out clearly with lots of tangible examples and strategies and really made me think. I listened to the audiobook which I wouldn't recommend since there are some quizzes and visual elements to the book, it seems.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Found it simpler to understand and more easily applicable than "Hold Me Tight." It was a good read and I do recommend it. My one caveat is that it can be a bit condescending and advice giving...do this...don't do that. Not my favorite tone in the world. I also feel a little bad for "avoidants," they seemed to get a lot of hate in this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached explores the well-researched, but not-popularized-enough attachment systems, how they were formed, and how an understanding of them could help us move toward healthier forms of attachment and communication with those we love. Don't let the quizzes at the beginning turn you off. The book is full of science and case studies.

review_body: Rachel and Amir are very warm and straightforward writers - the book is composed of their case studies and findings. It makes me think about my own needs in relationship, and I learned some great guidelines for relationship. For example, from thinking “Am I good enough for her” or “Is she good match for me”, to “Will she meet my emotional and growth needs in life”. Another mental shift is around self-reliance. Self-reliance may feel contrasting to mutual support, which a good relationship depends on. Express my needs openly is a sign of maturity. Great quotes ----------- Getting attached means that our brain becomes wired to seek the support of our partner by ensuring their psychological and physical proximity. If our partner fails to reassure us, we are programmed to continue our attempts to achieve closeness until they do. Attachment principles teach us that most people are only as needy as their unmet needs. When their emotional needs are met, and the earlier the better, they usually turn their attention outward. This is sometimes referred to in attachment literature as the “dependency paradox”: The more effectively dependent people are on one another, the more independent and daring they become. Once we choose a partner, there is no question about whether dependency exists or not. It always does. An elegant coexistence that does not include uncomfortable feelings of vulnerability and fear of loss sounds good but is not our biology. If you want to take the road to independence and happiness, first find the right person to depend on and travel down it with them. If we are unsure whether the person closest to us, our romantic partner, truly believes in us and supports us and will be there for us in times of need, we’ll find it much harder to maintain focus and engage in life. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: There’s one major problem with this book, and that’s the massive over simplification of its main topic: attachment styles. Part of me puts that down to the nature of writing to make complex ideas accessible and applicable to a wide range of people; the book is aiming to give a straightforward understanding of attachment styles and behaviour patterns so that the reader might tackle their own, and it does achieve that to a pretty reasonable degree. But that doesn’t hide the big gaping hole where all the nuanced discussion should be. People with anxious attachment styles are characterised as highly vulnerable individuals who simply require a nice partner to meet their emotional insecurities in a kind way and then they’ll finally be able to have a good relationship. They are afforded a huge amount of sympathy for their problematic behaviours, which are often explained away as being the result of being in relationships with people who have an avoidant attachment style. There are definitely reasonable points made about how having your basic emotional needs met is often demonised as being “needy” and that we live in a world that demonises the idea of relying on others, and that we should be more embracing of needing human connection. This book does however, seem to have a very large focus on the idea of just needing a reassuring partner who is happy to respond in a supportive way to the constant barrage of anxious thoughts and behaviours of an anxiously attached person. Though the writers do touch on the need to interrupt your own protest behaviours and try to change those thought patterns, I do feel that they seem to absolve anxiously attached people of any real responsibility and that it’s simply not their fault. In all the scenarios of different relationships, anxiously attached people seem to only be portrayed as the poor victims of selfish, emotionally avoidant individuals. review_body: The following are some of my main takeaways from the book: 1. Attachment Theory: 3 types of attachment: secure, anxious, avoidant with the following being the respective population distribution 50%, 25%-30%, and 20%-25%. This originally stemmed from a theory about children’s relationships with their parents called the strange situation test—a secure base (a parent/loved one) allows a child to explore, develop, and learn, and if a child lacks a secure base, they will be unable to maintain focus and engage in life—this theory was then applied to adult relationships. 2. Dependency paradox: the current generation has a belief in the codependency myth, which is “your happiness…should come from within and should not be dependent on your partner. However, “being attached [inherently] means that our brain becomes wired to seek the support of our partner by ensuring the partner’s psychological and physical proximity.” Therefore, “dependency is a fact it is not a choice or preference.” “If you want to take the road to independence and happiness find the right person to depend on and travel down it with that person and that’s the essence of attachment theory.” Essentially, by being dependent (on the right person) you’re more independent and are able to be your fullest self. If you have an unsecured base, then you are worse off then being independent. Right Person > Alone > Wrong Person 3. review_body: The idea: - There are three attachment styles: secure, avoidant, and anxious. - Sometimes these seem to be three different categories, sometimes they seem to be on a 2D axis - with anxiety on one axis and avoidance on the other. - People with a secure attachment style are ideal partners; they buy you flowers and rub your feet after you've had a long day. - People with an avoidant attachment style don't like getting tied down. If you get up in their personal space and try to tie them down then they'll start backing away slowly. - People with an anxious attachment style need constant reassurance that their beloved still cares about them. If you don't show them enough attention then they'll throw a tantrum (the authors call this "protest behaviour"). - Secures can successfully date anyone, and if you're not a secure then you're bad and should feel bad. - Two avoidants rarely date, because there isn't a strong bond between them to hold them together. - Because avoidants tend to form weak bonds, they end relationships and move on quickly, and so are over-represented in the dating pool. Bad points of the book: - It sometimes reads like a "greatest hits" of bad pop-psych. - Science-y terminology that doesn't seem to really mean anything ("activated attachment system") - Strong conclusions from minor neuroscience observations (something something amygdala activation something something avoidant attachment) - Totally made up evo-psych explanations (in unstable evolutionary environments, anxious attachment was the best strategy) - Oxytocin. - The whole thing reminded me in Myers Briggs. I mean sure, maybe the three qualitatively different kinds of attachment which apparently someone came up with using intuition are correct. But also maybe when you create your categories using a formal, objective method you actually get a model consisting of five fairly bland dimensions, about which the most positive thing that can be said is "they form a nice acronym". review_body: This framework did not resonate with me. Rather than anxious vs. avoidant personality types, I think it is more helpful to talk about people's different needs and capacities for intimacy, which may reflect a combination of both attachment styles. This framework has a lot of black and white thinking, missing out on the nuance of disorganized attachment types and dismissive/fearful avoidant types (though I'm not sure if those sub types came out after this book was published). I was initially interested in the framework when I read polysecure, which talks a lot more about parental wounds that create different attachment styles and that emphasize you can have different attachment styles for different types of relationships. I absolutely hate the way secure attachment types are portrayed - they are literally called "the 'supermates' of evolution." (pg 149). Like they are absolutely perfect and to date them is to heal yourself. I had many questions for myself that felt unanswered - I feel generally securely attached in most of my relationships, but of course I feel insecure at times. Isn't that normal? But the key is even with my insecurities I still try to abide by the principles of securely attached people, being available, vulnerable, supportive, etc. (pg 174). I do disagree with the secure principle of "view yourself as responsible for your partner's well-being." That to me is the definition of co-dependency. I of course want to do everything I can to add to the love and joy the people in my life feel,  but I can't be responsible for their well-being. I think this whole book has a very normative view on the "right" amount of intimacy. I feel very open to intimacy, but I don't always want to drop everything for the people in my life, nor do I expect them to do that for me. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: - Missing fearful-avoidant attachment style - Heteronormative, mononormative approach to the prevailing literature on attachment (eg. avoidants fear marriage and date often, anxiously attached people wants stability and long-term partnerships) - Lack of critical view on gender (eg. more women are anxiously attached, men who are avoidant are cold hearted villains) - Dubious claims on how codependency is healthy and the natural way to approach human connection - Irresponsible advice to anxiously attached people to 'not feel guilty about their needs' even though the needs and behaviours listed in the book are pretty damn concerning (eg. getting anxious after a partner, who works a full-time job, did not text for an arduous 5 hours, creating internet profiles to stalk their dates??). One of the biggest pieces of advice was to seek out secure people, who will definitely be able to provide a secure base and assurance for them. No word on whether someone secure would actually like to subject themselves to anxious, obsessive behaviour and become an emotional nanny... - Absolutist, one-dimensional views. For example, the view that avoidants all have low self-awareness and are resistant to change, and secure people's only role is to provide security. There was also no word on the variations of attachment styles in different contexts or over time, or within the same person. I scored exactly equally on all three styles. I didn't know what to do with that information. - Probably a lot more but I stopped reading after this.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A life transforming book falls a little short of a solid 5 star material. This is my first reading on marriages and relationships, obviously I want to get better, accept my limitations and become my better self as a partner and as a parent. This book introduces to Attachment theory and it's types, barely reading the first chapter I got to know my attachment style and my partner's and that clearly explains the trouble in our marriage. Instead of getting disappointed, I started focusing on what this book was to offer and I was immensely satisfied upon finishing this book. This book thoroughly covers the types of attachments, checklist to evaluate your attachment type and helps find out others' attachment type. The precautions in choosing a partner w.r.t. your current attachment style, If you're already in a relationship how to become better, the clash of attachment styles and most importantly why secure attachment style is the pivot for a long-lasting, happier and healthier relationship. There are a lot of strategies and tips included to help becoming a secure in a relationship with conflict-resolution, effective communication and secure basic principles. That's being said I'm relieved that I gave this book a try and have a clear picture in my mind how to apply these to make my relation better. The only downside I noticed in this book is that, not enough material covered on Avoidant attachment and ofter portrayed Avoidant as a villain and Anxious as a victim which is a bit biased which I'm happy to ignore when compared to the amount of knowledge I gained.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Early in the book, the authors talk about how universal their theories are... and then proceed to focus only on what they consider the more likely scenarios. If you are monogamous, neurotypical, hierarchical in relationships, het- and cis-normative, sexual, and fall into one of the main attachment styles, then you might find this book somewhat helpful. But if you don't fit into these neat categories (if you're polyamorous, neurodivergent, a relationship anarchist, lgbt+, asexual... or even if you fall into one of the categories that the authors mention but don't think are important enough to elucidate - such as avoidant-avoidant bonds or disorganized attachment styles), then you are likely to be as disappointed as I was. I gave them the extra star for recognizing how important attachment styles can be to relationships, but I just couldn't bring myself to give them any more. EDIT: I did some research of my own on attachment styles last night, and - after seeing how much great information is out there that these authors missed or ignored - I've revised my rating to one star.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was GREAT -- very enlightening around the three types of relationship styles: anxious, secure, and avoidant. One of the most enlightening things for me was that anxious-avoidant is a very common combination -- one person is looking for more closeness, and the other is actively avoiding it. Pretty soon, they both propogate each other's exact triggers and only make things worse! Avoidants don't date each other (they are both on the look-out for new and shiny), and an anxious-leaning person can be more secure IF in a relationship with a secure person. What I loved about this book is that there are no judgments -- just explanations for why we can feel so crazy sometimes trying to make a relationship work! And that codependency isn't necessarily a dirty word -- we are hard-wired to feel more secure and able to explore the world in a partnership where we are actually somewhat dependent on the other person -- the key is to have that dependency be matched and SUPPORT our highest growth, not take away from it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm a bit miffed at myself for leaving this on my list to read for so long -- I wish I had read it sooner. It's a refreshing perspective on attachment theory as it relates to dating and relationships, and was extremely helpful in identifying some of my own tendencies and pitfalls, as well as observations of others. By helping to put things in perspective, I believe I can utilize the information presented to make mindful decisions about my interactions with others, as it pertains to my needs, my tendencies, along with the styles of others'. Definitely a recommended read, for anyone -- existing couples, singles, newly single, forever single. Everyone can benefit. A couple of my favorite passages: "The study demonstrates that when two people form an intimate relationship, they regulate each other's psychological and emotional well-being. Their physical proximity and availability influence the stress response. How can we be expected to maintain a high level of differentiation between ourselves and our partners if our basic biology is influenced by them to such an extent?" "Well before brain imaging technology was developed, John Bowlby understood that our need for someone to share our lives with is part of our genetic makeup and has nothing to do with how much we love ourselves or how fulfilled we feel on our own. He discovered that once we choose someone special, powerful and often uncontrollable forces come into play. New patterns of behavior kick in *regardless* of how independent we are and *despite* our conscious wills. Once we choose a partner, there is no question about whether dependency exists or not. *It always does.* An elegant coexistence that does not include uncomfortable feelings of vulnerability and fear of loss sounds good but is not our biology."

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I disliked more of this than I liked. I skimmed the last third because I found that the book kept landing on general relationship advice that could have been simply reduced to an article (as opposed to expanded to seemingly endless vignettes). I continued reading because I was interested in the adult attachment research occasionally mentioned. However, the ways in which this book reduces people into 4 limited categories of attachment undermines the nuances and complexity of human beings. It would be great if it were easy enough to just "find a secure person' and live 'happily ever after', but the reality is that it's not that simple. The descriptions of avoidant and anxiously attached types are irritatingly generalized. Attachment can change over time and this was mentioned only briefly. Overall, this book feels divisive and judgmental about non-secure types without offering readers much information. (Also? Non-secure relationship combinations are not akin to emotionally abusive relationships, but you wouldn't know that from this book.) Skip this and read Dan Siegel and/or John Gottman.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 2 stars makes this sounds much worse than it was. I thought it had a lot of helpful/positive info about healthy communication and productive ways to handle anxiety, but mostly it was just these two psychologists dividing everyone in the world strictly into three categories (anxious, secure, avoidant) with no overlap and then making up lore about how these categories date, ie anxious/avoidant doomed to fail, secure/anxious possible but tricky, avoidant/avoidant is sort of a bigfoot situation of Does Not Exist. I understand that “lore” is not the correct term for “psychologists expanding on psychological concepts” but the book ditches the science very early on and is generally just dating self-help, so the vibe is more “relationship yu-gi-oh” as you learn what behaviors do and don’t mesh. Everything is stated as very absolute in a way that reads as oversimplifying complex issues! Sporadically helpful but generally kind of fluff.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Amir Levine's book is by far one of the most logical and cogent frameworks for thinking about and making sense of 'Love'. He decodes and organises the new science of Adult Attachment into neat categories of attachment styles and spends the rest of the book explaining how to figure out your attachment style, your partner's style, how each attachment style approaches relationships, which styles clash with each other and how to overcome such a confrontation. Whether you want to keep the love your have or find love, this book is a godsend for all rationalists who prefer order to instinct. After all why leave one of the most important aspects of your life to chance!

Why did they leave out disorganized attachment? It wasn't even included as a style. 2. I really appreciated the way they approached anxious attachment - describing it as an evolutionarily adaptive strategy, which should be embraced and used rather than changed or suppressed. Avoidant attachment was also described as evolutionarily adaptive but the general theme of the book was, if you meet an avoidant you have two options: 1. There was a section on what the avoidantly attached person might do to become more securely attached but it was dismissive of this as a real possibility.
