review_body: For the longest of time, I find myself leaning towards the perspective that self-help books are nothing but a series of rhetorical advice that are common sensical - its purpose coming in the form of timely reminders than anything awe-inspiring or mind-blowing. Not until I picked up this book, and started doubting myself. I recently came to learn of attachment styles, and Attached (written by neuroscientist Amir Levine and psychiatrist Rachel Heller) was one of the most critically acclaimed book that breaks down this area of psychology research. The fundamental theory is that our attachment style is influenced by our relationship with our parents during our growing up years and extend into how we perceive or act in relationships during adulthood. That said, our attachment style is malleable, and having self-awareness of our (and others) predominant attachment style is the first big step to improving our relationships, especially romantically. I could find myself relating to the common activation/deactivation tendencies, challenges and blind spots the more I devoured the book. It felt as if suddenly everything makes sense! Effective communication is often overlooked and over-generalised, but is indeed a core facet of any strong and stable relationship. I do find value and would recommend this book, even for those who do already possess a secure attachment style. Unfavourable external factors can and may waver even the most secure individuals if they are not able to recognise the potential blind spots or loopholes early enough.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: i was very disappointed by this. i immediately knew it was going to be super elementary? when i read the first example couple. idek if thats the right word but man did this oversimplify it. they took a whole book to say what i think i mostly knew from various reddit threads on attachment. there were a few moments that made me think, but mostly i was shocked at how biased they are in favor of anxiously attached people, at times even demonizing people with avoidant attachment style. i also didn’t like how they focused on just accepting your attachment style and had a few pages on improving your security. (especially anxious people. the whole book was telling me that if you’re anxious you just need to find someone secure, and if you’re avoidant you should change or be forever alone) like wtf?? this was a good intro to attachment theory if you don’t know much about it, but fails to address the complexities that trauma, abuse, and external factors can have on your relationships. i cant stress how much this felt like something you’d read in 10th grade health class one thing i did kind of self-reflect on (that the book didn’t address) was i think you can have different styles depending on the partner/circumstance (which makes sense to me). ex: when you’re not actively seeking a partner you could tend towards avoidant behavior, which i think says more about your needs due to an external factor than it does about your attachment style anyway if anyone has any good material they wanna rec on attachment style pls lmk cuz this wasnt it bruh. also this was hella embarassing to read on the train i mean i aint no hater to self help books but this ones cover is embarassing

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: All things considered, there is quite a bit that you can shred philosophically as this is a secular work and not written from a biblical worldview or value system.(purpose of life and people, epistemology, etc.) Our views on these things are important and thus thoughtfulness must be used throughout, as with any book. The writing style is informational instead of inspirational, and content is substantial, research focused, almost formal. Not fluffy, but also not too dense as there is a good amount of repetition and continuity. Other reviews commonly debate the helpfulness of perceived "labeling" in this work. I didn't find it to overgeneralize how terrible these people are or how important those ones are, but I see this is sensitive and may be upsetting. 🤷‍♀️ I liked this book because I found it to be helpful in how we think about issues such as neediness, independence, communication and conflict-resolution. However, this book isn't primarily about understanding you or others. It's highly practical in specific ways in these areas and others. I liked this book because it was helpful for me. (Thank you, Amy) probably in my top 3 in the year so far, alongside Dan Allender's "Healing the Wounded Heart." 5 stars-- Excellent

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Maneras de amar es una buena introducción a la psicología del apego adulto, desde un punto de vista práctico. De forma amena y muy accesible explica la ciencia detrás de los diferentes apegos, y procede a desarrollar los tres tipos de apego principales (ansioso, seguro y evasivo). El libro busca ser lo más útil posible a un público general, y está lleno de ejemplos de parejas en los que se nos anima a identificar sus estilos de apego, así como tests y tablillas para examinarnos a nosotrxs y nuestrxs compañerxs. Es un manual práctico, repleto de consejos acordes a cada estilo de apego, así como herramientas sobre comunicación eficiente, detección de mecanismos de activación y de estrategias de desactivación. Cualquier persona puede beneficiarse de leerlo, y especialmente aquellas que se encuentran en una dinámica relacional ansioso-evasiva. He echado en falta más desarrollo acerca de cómo los estilos de apegos se relación con vivencias pasadas, así como información acerca del estilo de apego desorganizado. Como he comentado, se trata más de una guía práctica y no de un libro de texto de psicología que trate pormenarizada los detalles y ramificaciones del apego adulto, y su cometido lo cumple ejemplarmente.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think these are the kinds of books that should be required reading at schools. This book is critical if you are someone with Anxious or Avoidant attachment styles or if your partner has one of these styles. If you’re both secure I still think it would benefit you enormously, but this is especially necessary reading for the other groups. I personally found so much language and understanding for myself and my own attachment style (anxious) and it has been an eye opening and challenging read for me. This information will truly be invaluable to my relationship. EDIT: After reading the review of someone who is an Avoidant type, I would like to revise my review to include the following: while my initial review still remains true, I find it also worth noting that certain undertones are present, in that the authors do seem to be a bit biased toward Anxious styles. At various times it made me feel that if my partner was Avoidant style that there would be no hope for us and it would mostly be his fault for pushing me away. There is a kind of sense that Avoidant styles are a lost cause unless you want to sacrifice your own dreams/desires. Which I do find to be unfair and not necessarily true.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: الكتاب هاد ضروري جداً يقرأه كل شخص بالغ عاقل راشد بالعالم ، بتخيل لو كل حد بيقرأه وبيفهمه بالطريقة الصحيحة حنعيش بمجتمعات طاغي فيها التفاهم والحب وحُسن التعامل والمُعاملة، بيتعرف الشخص نفسه لأي نمط هو بينتمي من خلال التمارين الموجودة في الكتاب وكيف ممكن يتحسن ويفهم حاله أكتر والاهم انه حيستوعب كيف يتعامل مع "شريك حياته" وقديش حيقدر يقلب حياتهم للاحسن بطريقة خيالية . الكتاب نوعاً ما ثقيل على العقل لكن ممتع جداً بنفس الوقت ، يعني بالعامية "قد ما بتحسه تقيل وصعب وبده تركيز قد ما هو مفيد وبيشد القارئ وبخليه متحمس ليعرف أكتر عن حاله وكيف بيقدر يتعامل بطريقة احسن مع شريكه او شريكته او كيف يحسّن من نفسه . الكتاب اغلبه ابحاث وقصص حقيقية وحقائق علمية . كتير عجبني انه احنا البشر بس نحضن حد بنحبه جسمنا بيفرز مادة اسمها "الأوكسيتوسين" وهو هرمون بينتج بكتير طرق "بعد العلاقة الحميمية" او عندما نعانق شركائنا عشان هيك سموه "هرمون العناق" . تشير نتائج علم الاعصاب الى انه يجب علينا تغيير اولوياتنا ،لأنه عندما نتخلى عن التقارب وعناق شركائنا! فإننا نفقد ايضاً دفعة من هرمون "الأوكسيتوسين" ما يجعلنا اقل تقبلاً للعالم من حولنا وأكثر عرضة للدخول في خلاف . احضنوا بعض يا جماعة ، كل يوم الصبح قبل ما تنطلقوا على دواماتكم ومشاغلكم احضن زوجتك واحضني زوجك ، خصصو ٥ دقياق قبل ما تفتحو باب البيت وتنطلقو لتحضنو وتعانقو بعض وتحبو بعض ❤️ الكتاب رائع جداً ومفيد الى ابعد حد .

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: As an anxious attachment girlie myself, this book provided very realistic insights and tangible steps to heal through being anxiously attached. Although I have already done research independently before reading this book so I had prior knowledge, this book was very digestible in understanding what type of behaviours you do and therefore overcome them. Even just understanding the term “protest behaviour”, I find it much easier to identify when my behaviour is unproductive because of my attachment style and then know that the solution is communicating my need effectively, which was also discussed in the book. I think those who are anxiously attached like myself could gain great insight in navigating that in a relationship. It’s very specific on what to do when in a relationship or finding love, I think also learning about it seperate from the book has also helped me gain insight on how to manage my emotions and fill my cup so I’m more secure anyways. This was very tailored to how to navigate in a relationship. I found it incredibly helpful, digestible and tangible, with actionable steps to be a better partner in an anxious attachment space. I truely do recommend this book, incredibly helpful and insightful and truely could change the trajectory of a relationship if practiced, which will lead to being a more secure partner. Enjoyable and incredibly helpful.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Some parts are really informative. Their whole explanation on why attachment is valuable and the dependency paradox was great. I also think the red flags they discuss are valuable. The weed out theory in which you communicate your needs early on in the dates is tangible, useful advice. My core issue is that most of it focuses on anxious attachment and villainizes avoidants. A lot of it was like oh this is going wrong in the relationship, Tom must have an avoidant attachment style and is incapable of love. Samantha needs to either communicate her needs to him or they should break up. And then they don’t act like it’s a bit strange for Samantha to be calling Tom 15x a day. They imply that if Tom only reassured Samantha she’ll stop calling so much (but still check in frequently). I think they place way too much emphasis on the responsibility for the partner to soothe the insecurely attached partner. I like this secure base theory but you also have to be able to regulate yourself at some points. In a lot of their examples, it seems like the avoidant person doesn’t really like their partner (sorry). Or the examples they give of avoidants aren’t about their avoidance, these people were just assholes. Like I’m sorry I don’t think Mark is calling Belinda fat and wanting to sleep with other woman because he likes Belinda so much he’s afraid of their unique intimate connection. He’s just a jerk.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I appreciate the lens of attachment to look at relationships. This book irritated me bc for the majority of the book, they talk as though attachment styles are fixed identities, when actually they can vary wildly over time based on relationship experience and psychological work/self-awareness. The majority of the book made me feel like I am probably a defective person who is bad at relationships bc I have some avoidant tendencies. It also didn’t seem to acknowledge that avoidance is at its root the same as anxiousness, but just a different strategy for dealing with anxiety surrounding intimacy. Rather than treating it as a different way of coping with the same needs, it treats it as a polar opposite personality type, which misses the point I think. The last section of the book talks about secure communication practices which anyone from any attachment style can use. If anyone can learn secure practices, it would probably be helpful not to refer to human beings as anxious, secures and avoidants. Regardless, there are some fun quizzes in here and the last section is very helpful. Probably not my number 1 relationship book recommendation, though.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Insightful read - was incredibly relatable in many ways, highlighting certain patterns of behaviour I unconsciously fall into. We all have traits that are secure, anxious and avoidant, and in fact it's about seeing which ones we identify within our behaviour, interactions and relationships. I enjoyed reading the book with the illustrative examples/anecdotes that convey the principles with clarity. It also helped to challenge some of my patterns of thinking: a degree of emotional dependency is natural and will lead to greater security and paradoxically independence, how certain attachment styles are more prone to viewing emotional and sexual intimacy as separate, and how we often "view conflict as a zero-sum game", when really we should consider that the other person's well-being will infuence our own. However, one of its pieces of advice for those looking, is to seek out secure partners, and it appears to be written predominantly for those who have an anxious attachment style. I reckon that it's not quite as black and white as that, as we all share traits from each of those. Overall enjoyable and insightful read. Would recommend for people wanting to gain insight into themselves, their partners and the concept of attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I listened to this as an audiobook, but that was a mistake - this is clearly a book that needs to be read/engaged with in hard format. I know there's some sort of accompanying PDF, but, while I was driving, I didn't exactly have the capacity to consult it. I also wasn't able to take the test, and hearing the various options read out to me wasn't exceptionally interesting. Now, all that being said, I did think there were some useful tidbits in here. Did it change my life? No. I also wasn't able to readily identify who would fit exactly into which category (which was sort of the whole point of the first half of the book). I do think this would have been really useful to me early in my twenties, early on in my dating life. There were a lot of lessons in here that I feel that I learned the hard way. Then again, I don't think any of these are meant to be employed by someone under 25.... I think I would recommend this to friends of mine who are struggling in relationships. It's a softer blow than "he's just not that into you." The whole idea that you should sort of force someone's hand early on - coulda saved me a lot of time in the SECOND half of my twenties lol.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Explained what was healthy about the healthy relationships I’ve been in, in a way that gives me a newfound sense of what to look for, value, and how to communicate. This line blew my mind: “Most people are only as needy as their unmet needs.” Despite the softer hues assigned to people with an anxious attachment style in this book, and avoidants being almost villainized, the most treasured takeaway from this book was not screening out people exhibiting “undesirable” attachment patterns. The chances of meeting someone with an anxious/avoidant attachment style is inevitable (only ~50% of people display secure attachment styles) - and what if we’re attracted to them not Because of, but Despite their attachment style (or guilty of deactivating/anxious responses ourselves)? The authors provide useful ways to co-create a secure base, and clue you into scenarios where leaving might be a better alternative to sticking it out. They also highlight the power of secure priming - a person with an insecure attachment style can continue to draw from past relationships or friendships with people who have a secure attachment style (there’s hope for all of us!).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached was more than just informative, it was transformative. It helped me realize that different people can bring out different attachment styles in you. While I’ve always considered myself secure for the most part, someone who communicates openly and seeks resolution, this book helped me understand why I sometimes felt anxious in certain dynamics, especially when emotional closeness was met with distance or avoidance. It gave me language for patterns I had been caught in without fully understanding. The section on anxious-avoidant pairings was especially eye opening.. as though someone had finally turned the lights on in a room I’d been sitting in for years. Reading this affirmed that even deeply caring bonds can be built on incompatible foundations. I spent too long in a space of emotional confusion, constantly in fight or flight, craving connection while being met with withdrawal. This book reminded me that my attachment needs are valid, and that secure mutual love does exist. Walking away from something that isn’t good for your nervous system is one of the most loving things you can do for yourself. & now, I feel empowered to seek out relationships rooted in emotional availability, safety, and reciprocity. If you’ve ever felt like you’re too much for someone emotionally unavailable… please read this. You’re not too much. You were just asking the wrong person.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 1 star, not because it was that bad, but because I want to make clear that no one should read this. First of all, my fault is going into this wanting a psychology non fiction book, that would deepen my understanding about attachemnet, the patterns, triggers and emotional basis of it. What this actually is is a book that tells you oh, do this, oh do that, and in this way all your relationship troubles will be solved. ... No, I don't want any hints, nonsensical or unapplicable advice, thanks, no thanks. Only a surface level approach to the science behind this ( also, I learned later that this theory is kind of obsolate). Also, another foul of the authors is that their approach was very absolute and close-minded. What they said was that safe-people (people with safe attachment style) are what everyone wants, the best piece of cake, and they can do absolutely nothing wrong, anxious people have too many needs and want extreme closeness and that's 100% not something they should do anything about, and they should just stop choosing people that can't take it and avoidant people should go and disappear from the face of this earth either/or change everything about how they view or feel in a relationship because they are toxic and the base of all our problems. I feel scammed for being tricked into spending 16 euros for this!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'll be honest, the first several times this book appeared in my Amazon recommended reads, I totally discounted it. "How to find and keep love"? I wondered if they were marketing to lonely college students. That said, after taking a grad course in Social Psychology on the Science of Intimate Relationships from one of the more prolific current researchers in attachment (Jeffry Simpson), I took a second look to see how it compared with/presented the current research in the field that, for me, was transformative in the way I think about how we approach and relate to one another (differently) in relationships. This book is a good place to start understanding what attachment is and how people differ, but don't let this be your final resource, particularly if you have a relationship that you might be able to approach more compassionately by understanding how you're both approaching it differently. From a personal perspective, attachment research is most beneficial helping me to take stressful interactions less personally so that I can better understand them (and what to do) rationally, but you'll likely want to check out Google Scholar for other sources of information.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I feel somehow embarrassed to write a review about a romantic relationship books, which i never did by the way. Because i feel like i know how to handle my feelings and how others responds to them! I dont have a base to compare this book, but u i liked it very much, simple , direct ! It describes how attachment theory can be used to manage romanic relationships. There are three types of attachment: anxious, secure and avoidant. At first when reading each characteristics i thought i was an avoidant person, but then when passing the test it revealed that i was in fact Secure 😁 BUT i do think i have a tendency to act more avoidant sometimes, and i need to find some solutions to that! I liked this book because it gave a general and precise description of how people act in relationships, and i understood why some behaved in a way and others not. Full of exemples, solutions , real life experience and witnesses. Everything to wish for in this kind of books 🖤 I highly recommend this book even for single people like me , very instructive and full of information 🖤

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I have read a lot of books on marriage over the past year. This is one of the better ones. Levine over-promises a little bit, claiming in the introduction that "studies" had unraveled the complexities of relationships between men and women. This is a typical canard of relationship books. And I'm sure that more than three groups (avoidant, anxious, and stable) describe the types of baggage people bring into relationships, but Levine brings the goods anyways. I have found, after reading and reflecting on the book, that I have different attachment styles for my marriage of 25 years and within my family, than I have with friendships, some of which date back even longer. Using Levine's paradigm didn't solve my issues, but it was a valuable way to look at my personal background and how it still impacted my relationships today. What earns this book its 4th star, however, is the final chapter about communications. I think it really gave me useful tools to improve the way I communicate with her wife (through both her attachment lens and mine) as well as to the friend I quit talking to years ago--for very good reasons, of course, LOL.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I had high hopes for this book after hearing multiple recommendations. Ended up disappointed. The first couple of chapters provide a useful general overview of attachment theory but otherwise this book was a waste of time. Most of the remainder focuses on strategies to help those with an anxious style, or information for their (assumed) secure partners to help deactivate the attachment reactions, while demonizing those who lean towards an avoidant pattern. There was a passing mention of the “disorganized” type, which has traits of BOTH anxious AND avoidant responses, but absolutely zero insight or suggestions on how to manage this type of profile. In addition, many of the case studies featuring avoidant partners actually seemed to describe an abusive dynamic and no distinction was made between the two. There was also no mention of the fact that an anxious attachment pattern can also exist alongside abusive behavior. Those who are anxious are certainly deserving of empathy, but accountability for bad behavior should apply to anyone regardless of their attachment style. The authors seem to think that anxious individuals cannot also be abusers. As someone who experiences a “disorganized” attachment response, I was hoping to learn strategies for finding a more secure balance, but I came back empty.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Levine/Heller have done a brilliant job of translating Ainsworth/Bowlby's Attachment Theory into bite-sized, easy-to-apply pointers to use in romantic relationships. They steer clear of jargon-ridden, dry descriptions of theory (*cough academia) and jump straight into the business of identifying attachment styles (Anxious/Avoidant/Secure) and how best to deal with them in conflicts. The value of the Attachment framework lies in its non-blaming, non-stigmatising, focus-on-the-dynamic approach. Anyone who reads it can expect to find solace (And maybe a sigh of relief) that relationship failures and breakdowns aren't shameful markers hinting at personal inadequacy. The duo take typically messy examples and show it to be a predictable tangle of intimacy needs turning up in predictable ways. Importantly, they highlight that one doesn't need a magic wand to fix it and that they're very much solvable. I've been recommending this book to clients in therapy, and on most days, I'm convinced it makes a far more persuasive case for change than I manage to in 50minutes.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I picked up this book as the supposedly best book on attachment styles. Even though going in, I was aware that it's structured as a dating self-help book, I still emerged with mixed feelings. On one hand, it's based on psychological research, and presents the relevant theories in a practical and useful way. It's quite interesting to see just how simple the understanding of some of our supposedly highly unique behaviors can be. On the other hand, the book loves to act as an agent of averageness. It keeps implying that traditional, long-lasting, heteronormative, monogamous partnerships are key to personal happiness. Certainly, its ideas are applicable to any relationship. But be prepared to roll your eyes, and then do some of the thinking for yourself. As this was my first time reading about attachment styles, I feel like I learned a lot. But at the same time, even to a 'beginner', it felt like the book kept oversimplifying. That being said, the topics it discusses are important and not widely known. I feel like nearly anyone could benefit from being aware of their attachment style, what it means for their relationships, and how to handle it in themselves and others.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is centred around romantic relationships but I found it very helpful for relationships in general. There are little worksheets here and there that are nice and easy to go through. If you don’t come out of this book a little people smarter, it’d be sad 🥲 What I found interesting though is the soft bias towards anxious types and the kind of “stay away from dismissives” bandwagon. Being the latter, it was hilarious to read this but to a large extent, I understand why the bias. That being said, I don’t think they did much research on dismissives as they did anxious people. They grouped people into 3 groups = anxious, dismissive and secure. They didn’t include anxious- avoidant (fearful avoidant) people so that was quite limiting. As someone who has some Fearful Avoidant tendencies, I had to then apply anything that was relevant on both the anxious and dismissive sides. Despite the major limitation of excluding one group of people, I enjoyed it and devoured it very quickly! And also applying some of the principles I learned which are working well so far 😃

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book has two main goals: 1 - To try and explain Attachment Theory (a popular psychological theory) to the masses, and 2 - To help the reader identify their (and their partner's) attachment style, in order to improve their relationship(s). The subject is interesting, and the book is easy to read. The examples help identify secure and insecure principles at work in daily situations and dialogues. It is interesting to think and ponder about relationships, and even to (somewhat embarrasingly) find out that the secure attachment has not always been the case for me. In practical terms, I did not find the book itself hugely helpful in my life: maybe because I now have secure attachment style, and so does my girlfriend? But it is a nice read nonetheless. Attachment theory is not the be-all and end-all of relationships: they are inherently complicated – because human beings are complicated. But I believe more awareness towards this theory could only be helpful. In this sense, it is just like the Love Languages: anything that can remind people that their partner perhaps expresses and feels love in a different manner than they do, and have different needs, is invaluable. I recommend this book to pretty much everyone. 5/5. Fun fact: I first heard of attachment theory when reading and essay of Tim Kreider's book I Wrote This Book Because I Love You: Essays , in which he finds out he was one of the babies in the original John's Hopkins study.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: God I love science! I especially love it when science takes a look at human behavior and helps me understand myself and others more. This book did just that! I hate self-help books - abhor them! But this one really resonated with me. The authors did a great job of describing each attachment style (secure, anxious, and avoidant) and how they mix, clash, and function all while providing anecdotes to emphasize their points. And of course I fall in the bucket where only 3-5% of the population fall which is the anxious AND avoidant attachment style. The authors though provide good advice for both styles on how to be more secure and everything of course is backed by research. I read several of the 1 and 2 star reviews and can understand people’s frustration and displeasure with the book. As with any self-help book, not everything will be addressed. There are certainly several nuances and complexities in life that a self-help book about relationships can’t capture. But if you simply view the book for what it is, a book about attachment styles, I think you can appreciate its straightforwardness and simplicity. For me, I found the book insightful and validating. And it will be a book I reference several years from now. 4.5 stars!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Levine explores the concept of people having secure, anxious, or avoidant attachment styles; how said attachment styles might manifest in romantic relationships; and how to either avoid forming relationships of potentially conflicting styles, or how to address conflicts more constructively in existing relationships. Not sure how useful this is to someone seeking a romantic relationship to *find* one, although I suppose it could help people (especially anxious attachment people) *avoid* certain (avoidant-style) pitfalls (namely: by an act of will, they just say "No, I have already determined that Behavior X is a Problem and I must leave"). It's vexing to learn that mathematically, avoidant types are most likely to be in the dating pool. Methinks it would have been more useful, by virtue of being more generally applicable, to examine attachment styles in non-romantic relationships; protest behavior, eg, can appear in all sorts of contexts. But that was not, alas, the scope of the book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: "Attachment principles teach us that most people are only as needy as their unmet needs. When their emotional needs are met, and the earlier the better, they usually turn their attention outward." "Once we choose a partner, there is no question about whether dependency exists or not. It always does. An elegant coexistence that does not include uncomfortable feelings of vulnerability and fear of loss sounds good but is not our biology." 2.5 stars. Turns out I'm not ready for self-help, even when it's backed up with a reasonable amount of research. This book was geared towards finding love or working on a troubled relationship, neither of which are currently of interest to me. There were some interesting points, but ultimately all of the examples of attachment styles in action would have worked well even if the theory wasn't being applied. If someone is being cruel in a relationship, it wouldn't help me to know it's because they're avoidant. A bit dated too, I got fed up with the constant "he or she".

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I have to say, this book came at the right time in my life and shocked me through and through, because the authors were able to put my patterns and behaviors into words - I wasn't aware. I'm really thankful for science explaining what I "did wrong" in previous relationships, as well as the wrongdoing I experienced towards me. It puts me into a confident position to find someone who matches me perfectly, since I now feel like I have the tools at hand. Also I can work with myself on all kinds of levels. I'm happy I know this now :) The authors lost me in the second part of the book where I felt like advices were repeating themselves from all kinds of perspectives. Also agreeing with other reviews before, secure and avoidand attachment types might not draw as much out of the book as the anxious types, therefore maybe not finding it as valuable. Nonetheless it would be great if it was wider known throughout society. Much time can be saved in relationships that aren't meant for each other :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A marvelous book that encompasses seemingly the most helpful ways of finding a romantic partner that could fit your needs, along with helping one understand why they behave in certain manners (which they might see as normal) that might slowly shatter the possibility of having a long-living and loving relationship. I truly believe that everyone who did not understand any of their former partner's behaviors should read this book, but especially those who haven't had any happy relationship that could have been labeled as a "possibly THE relationship" they'd want for themselves. One small note, that is not, in my opinion, enough for lowering the rating of this book, would be that the disorganized attachment style, which was defined in the beginning of the book as being a combination of the anxious and avoidant ones, has not been detailed any further. However, being a mix of those two, a person with that attachment style could find themselves in the descriptions of both categories and could learn what they could apply on themselves from both sides, that were very well analyzed in this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Now I can understand why so many relationship content creators on social media and other counsellors continuously refer to this book - not only does it read easily (for me as non-native English speaker) despite the scientific background, it also uses lots of examples and exercises to reflect on the parts that have been written, which makes the "lessons" even more tangible. For me, after reading this book, I can tell that not only I feel called out in the most non-offended, much needed way, but also that I was able to reflect on my past relationships in a way and depth I wasn't able to before. PLUS this book made me realize once again (big time) how much of a lottery win my secure partner is, by showing how this kind of people/angels is regulating others and by encouraging me to effectively communicate my needs and feelings. Something that always seems to be THE most difficult task. Beyond grateful that I finally picked up this book and can't wait to see how its magic will unfold in the near and further future.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The bit about the phantom ex as a deactivating strategy is so dead on. I thought invented this technique. I guess I did. I guess all avoidant people who do this invented it independently. How funny. The bit about anxiously attached people exacerbating my desire to withdrawal is also 100% correct. And the advice that the author gave to avoidant types, about how we are more likely to bond with people if we spend time with them *doing stuff* is very true. I noticed that the only people I ever really enjoy hanging out with are the ones I *do* things with (dive buddies, climbing buddies, sailing friends; musicians; board game homies). Friendships based on sitting around and talking, where the main point is to spend time together (where I feel as though we are just hanging out to hang out) make me feel suffocated. Ultimately I think how much you like this book has a lot to do with what you expect from it. I expected almost nothing, so I was surprised by its accuracy. I felt as though they really understood me, like they’ve been spying on my private thoughts.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: At the beginning of this book, the authors did a pretty stellar job of dispelling what they term the “dependency myth” and introducing the idea that securely attached individuals are actually more likely to take healthy risks - and, therefore, more fully realize their own potential - because they are properly dependent on the support of their partners. However, it seemed almost all downhill from there… Like others, I thought the examples given were too simplistic and the ‘scientific’ conclusions drawn too prescriptive. “You are this way, you will always be this way, and you suck.” The authors’ claim about intimacy needs being an innate product of evolutionary biology directly contradict their presumption that avoidant-attached individuals lack any desire for relational closeness. This reductive presumption ignores the realities of trauma-informed psychology, which consistently concludes that avoidant attachment stems not from a lack of desire, but from a lack of perceived safety or emotional regulation. Long story short, it just felt thin to me.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: pretty good read, it has been on my TBR for a long time and as a psychology student i think I must read it lol. now in the beginning, i felt that many things were obvious and it wasn't adding much to my information bank - i feared that it may be one of those main stream books that were so generic and didn't really immerse you in the topic the way that you hoped for. however, as i read, i really got to enjoy the reserach that was mentioned all throughout- how our brain is literally wired to choose or assign "a secure person" which happens to be our partner later in life. the book stance on the "independent movement" was quite interesting. what i enjoyed most was the terminology i acquired from the book such as activating/deactivating strategies, protest behavior and secure principles. i feel much more confident in entertaining conversations around attachment styles and the temperaments of the individuals with said attachment styles. i would recommend this to anyone who is interested in gaining more insight about attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: If you are currently attached to someone, in a relationship, situationship, or totally single...just read this. If you are already aware of attachment theory, the first few chapters will be a refresher, but they are worth reading to get an idea of how different aspects manifest in different relationships. I was recently dumped and it sucks. I knew subconsciously that the partner was avoidant, but this helped me see what I did right, and where our anxieties and fears got the best of us and caused a failure of what otherwise was a good match. This will help you so much in your relationships. Please just read it. Do the work and ask yourself the hard questions. It's not particularly dense or imaginative, as it is self-help and psychological, but this should be essential reading for anyone who isn't aromantic, and can probably help platonic relationships as well, if you have friends who are serial monogamists, cheaters, or people who are always single but hate it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Incredibly helpful after dealing with avoidant attachment style cishet men for years. It gives me confidence and strength to be up front while dating (and that I do nothing wrong when I do). I understand where some of the negative reviews come from. Seems people get obsessive or annoyed about putting people (or themselves) in a box. No, the book offers *insight* into relationships and their conflict. It's not the end all, be all. I wish there was more information on effective communication with anxious and avoidant styles. I had many take-aways from this book: people may find me boring because I have secure attachment, stay away from people who believe in "the one", watch out for avoidants who may appear "secure", and just watch out for signs of avoidant behavior because they are in the dating pool more often. Lastly, they mention the co-dependency myth (looking out for yourself, your well-being and happiness depends on yourself, etc) that I have heard over and over again, but this quote rings true: "In a true partnership, both partners view it as their responsibility to ensure the others emotional well-being."

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Super helpful self-help book, encapsulating the attachment theory zeitgeist. Attachment theory has a long and storied past in social psychology research but has only recently hit the mainstream for applications in friendship and romantic relationships. With a limited social psychology research background, I'd say the *causal* assertions made by this book have less value than the applications/observable patterns, which serve as a handy framework to bring to a therapist or intimate chat with a close friend or loved one. Note that this book has one main limitation - it seems geared toward those with Anxious leanings, while Jeb Kinnison's work more thoroughly and compassionately considers Dismissive styles. Overall, this book is a quick and easily digestible read and works as a great springboard into personal growth. I'd highly recommend this to anyone who would like to get a better grasp on how they function in relationships or who would like to better understand a tricky relationship dynamic with a loved one. Though attachment style is just one piece of the human interpersonal puzzle, it gets the cognitive gears turning and the conversation turned toward a productive aspect of emotional self-examination.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Agree with the comments that this is very biased towards people with the anxious attachment style (um me!), and about half way through I really started to notice that all of the examples were making the avoidant partner into the “bad one” in the relationship. One example specifically seems to blur the lines between an abusive partner and a partner with an avoidant attachment type. The anxious partner is always the victim in the examples and isn’t asked to take much responsibility for their actions other than communicate more effectively or find a more secure partner. The avoidant type there is not much advice for. This made me feel great at first like “I’m not the problem!” but once I noticed the bias, I read the remainder with more criticism. I still think I gained a lot from this book and have identified my anxious behaviors and can take a hard look at those and learn to communicate better instead of resorting to my classic anxious tactics.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book has some excellent points and helpful information. I would like to go over certain parts again but in book form instead of audio. I identified with avoidant and I know that was bad.. My main critique of the book and theory is that it has three attachment types and although it briefly goes over how a person can change attachment types over time it doesn't consider that a person can have more than one or doesn't fall completely into one category. Basically if you have a secure attachment style, you are awesome. Anxious= that is okay you just need to feel secure. Avoidant= you suck. Well dang, I am mostly avoidant or at least I was. And avoidant and anxious are usually the worst type of pairing. Well, that is my husband and me so... we get along well and enjoy each other's company. I would also be interested in the research of why people have the attachment types they do, which it only briefly covered.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The theoretical basis of attachment theory makes a lot of sense and can be helpful to integrate into your understanding of self and others, but this book absolutely butchers it by being heavy handed and grossly over-generalised. For all the high hopes I'd had coming into it, I was twitchy within the first few chapters and downright repulsed by the last. The authors focus exclusively on extreme examples, with characters lacking any kind of self-awareness. I know I am anxious, but because I am decently aware of it, and trying my best in partnership, this book makes my behaviours and communication seem secure, without acknowledging the gradient between the types. Here, anxious types are neurotic and obsessive, avoidants are psychopaths, and - worst of all - secure types are strangely glorified and viewed as rare despite being the majority. If attachment type has an effect on our approach to intimacy (which I don't doubt) then it will be in subtle ways, far more significantly overshadowed by individual personality differences and relationship skills, and to presume to judge someone's emotional availability, conflict resolution skills, and self-confidence essentially by attachment type alone sabotages the authors message. I have no doubt that the authors have deep and valuable understanding about the subtlety of their subject matter and equally rue the disrespectful infantisation of the reader but, alas, this was hard to stomach and I can't say I recommend it to anyone.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Absolutely eye opening and fascinating! I read some reviews before finishing this book and writing my own so just read this out. Yes, it’s true, when reading this book, the avoidant attacher will get a bad reputation! The book does have a way of making them seem selfish, cold, and completely aloof in a relationship! I can see why an avoidant would be upset while reading this! But the thing is this..if we are biologically designed to attach to people, especially in a romantic way, and the avoidant uses these deactivating strategies to shut that down, doesn’t that seem cold and completely contradictory to the human race?? I have been able to identify myself as the anxious attacher! No I’m not perfect and being with me may be a lot but I can say that I am embracing the way we were created to be; with intimacy! This book helped me to realize that and understand my relationship needs way better so I know what to look for and what to be aware of.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Super helpful book, especially if you’re an anxious attachment person (like myself.) Biggest takeaways: • “In a true partnership, BOTH parties view it as their responsibility to ensure the other’s emotional well-being” (Pg.271). This goes to a very good piece of relationship advice I always think about which is “If you put them first, and they put you first, everyone is first and no one is left behind.” • “Attachment principles teach us that most people are only as needy as their unmet needs” (pg. 21). I’m needy because my needs aren’t being met, hello! • “Acknowledge and accept your true relationship needs” and “Start assessing people you date on the basis of their ability to meet those needs” (both on pg.99) “Can this person provide what ~I~ need in order to be happy?” (pg.100). Which reminds me of CJ Hauser’s essay, The Crane Wife. So much more, but a pretty decent book for anxious attachment people to learn more about themselves and work towards being secure.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An amazing read that I will continue to recommend to everyone. I enjoyed how this book gave insight in a way that was easy to understand and relate to through specific examples in vignettes rather than just in long paragraphs. This book outlined the importance of trusting yourself while also highlighting how we are made to be in relationship and community with others- our attachment style can continue to evolve and even digress from secure depending on the interactions we are having with others. I enjoyed the quiz at the beginning of the book and how it graphed attachment with a mother figure, father figure, best friend, and romantic partner. This book has the ability to help people understand themselves and others around them in a deeper capacity without the limitation of putting a person into an eternal box or classification. I will continue to refer back to some of these charts in my work as therapist.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was a great insight into the different behaviours which people exhibit in relationships. I did a lot of self-reflection and I was able to identify certain behaviours of my own and understand how these related to my attachment style and that of my (then) partner as well. I loved the examples of real-life relationships in this book, and how different scenarios were broken down to teach us about which forms of communication were effective and which were ineffective (ie protest behaviour). The only point I would make is that this book is probably a lot more helpful to those in a relationship, as it teaches you how to address conflicts and improve communication to reach resolutions, whereas I was only able to reflect on my past relationship. I also feel that my behaviour would vary a lot depending on my partner, so I can’t say my reflections on the past relationship would be applicable to the next. The main takeaway is we love a secure attachment!!!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Recommended to me by a friend, I dived into this book eager to put labels and definitions to feelings and actions that I have experienced in myself and in others. I definitely learned so much about my attachment type, anxious, and how to best communicate with others with this. This book and its stories gave me so much perspective on how we choose to have relationships to others. Rather than seeing my attachment style as a weakness, I see its strengths, and mostly its misunderstood nature. It is so valid to have our own attachment styles, but it's another story about how to personally coexist with myself and others that really determines its effect. The book demystified my thoughts and actions, allowing me to feel supported and heard. I was comforted to hear that I am not the only one feeling my feelings. So many stories I could learn from. One take away is that I strive to have the secure attachment style as one has with their pet. The love I desire to give and receive is similar to the trust, forgiveness, and utter bliss when we are with our beloved pets (thinking of Pumpkin and how I continued to love her through the throw-up and schedule altering events). I am excited to continue learning about my emotions!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I liked learning more about the different attachment styles and it’s helpful to view people’s actions through this lens rather than thinking about “good people” vs “bad people”. The authors mischaracterize codependency, which I found odd for people who’ve positioned themselves as “relationship experts”. They seem to buy in to the common misunderstanding that a codependent relationship is a relationship in which people depend on each other, which is not accurate. I feel like I didn’t have any big epiphanies while reading this one, but I did like the section at the end about effective communication. One concept that will stick with me is: effective communication doesn’t necessarily mean the other person will react in the way you’d like them to, but if you communicate clearly, you can at least make sure your judgments are based on choices they’ve actually made rather than their inability to accurately read your mind. Basically, give them a chance to show you who they are rather than deciding that for them.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5/5 || this was a very engaging and informative book. I enjoyed reading it; although, I have two major issues: The first being, the authors provided a lot of criticism toward avoidant people and almost none to anxiously attached people. If anything, the authors only affirmed those who are anxiously attached. Their advice for them being: find someone secure… and that’s it. As someone who is securely attached but can lean anxious at times, I found this to be unhelpful and a little discouraging that there seems to be no way to improve one’s anxious tendencies causing their partners to suffer that burden and attempt to “fix” them. The second is less of a criticism and more of a disclaimer that I believe should’ve been mentioned. Attachment theory is helpful and interesting, but it is a tool - NOT the key - to finding yourself a loving and healthy relationship. There are many other pieces that need to align in order for a solid relationship to take place.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The first review on this book clearly explores my thoughts in more depth. The book was clearly written through the lens of the anxious attachment style, and demonised avoidants. The devices for the latter lacked depth and the only take away is "distracting yourself" to minimise your deactivating technique. The research into avoidants was lackluster, and they kept bringing up examples whereby the man was avoidant and the woman was anxious. Terrible portrayal. Anyone who rated this 5 star must be anxious cause this book was basically written for them for how much the author infantalised them, and wrote off avoidants being the cause of their relationship issues etc. The only thing I enjoyed reading was the psychological studies between mother and child, and other studies that gave me "ahah" moments. Again, this feeling was overshadowed by negative umbrella shielded upon avoidants, yet again. DNF.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It’s kinda crazy how a partner’s behaviour can shape you, the way you get treated in a relationship can really affect your whole psychology. This book has thought me you cannot work out your issues if the other person doesn’t want to. It explains well how the different attachment styles feel and the best ways to comfort them and make them feel seen. And why you feel a certain way when you’re in a relationship. Key advice is just find a secure person and communicate your feelings. Comes with the caveat that because secure people find it easy to get into relationships you have to catch em in their transition period before they get taken again. Compromise can be completely one sided to end clashs and conflict, adjusting your expectations and “settling”. Essentially choosing compromise/settling to feel the peace and quiet or leaving. Lastly love is not enough to keep a relationship together. It takes work and effort from both sides.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Great book for reading after a tough breakup. I highly recommend this book to anyone looking to learn how to find a partner, or improve their current romantic relationship. Levine's research on attachment styles brought new perspective to my dating life. The many examples used throughout the book help to bolster the author's assertion. Plus, through mini quizzes and interactive pages, the author helps you recognize the attachment styles seen in your own life. While many of the anecdotes ring true for me, I feel like I've exhibited multiple attachment styles throughout my life. I felt like the author could have devoted more time to the development of attachment styles and how they change. A lot of the advice at the end seemed trite and obvious (i.e. communicate clearly in relationships), but it is a good reminder. Overall a captivating read!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I thoroughly enjoyed this book . I'm biased as I did my undergrad thesis on attachment theory and loved talking about healthy relationships with teens as a former youth worker. I can see why some reviews say the book touts common sense. Yes one of the main take aways to be direct and non-blaming in your romantic communication. Most of us know what healthy relationship behaviour looks like. This books answrs the question of why we don't always use this behaviour or leave relationships we find dissatisfying. I think what makes this book special is how it highlights how ingrained certain maladaptive behaviours can be based on attachment style. In some ways maladaptive behviors meet our specific needs for intimacy. I think this book distilled 10 years of research in engaging way. Using multiple approaches like scenarios and journal prompts keeps the book accesible. You'll like this book if you enjoy the trappings of psychology like categorizing people and cognitive behavior therapy. It's not for everyone but it does what it says on the tin.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: As adults we have one of three attachment styles that we cling to in terms of our relationships with others - both platonic and romantic. You’re either secure, anxious. Or avoidant. If you’re anything like me than you can already decipher off the words alone which one best describes you (🥴). But how does our attachment style relate to the people we attract in our lives, whom we work best alongside, and why some people/relationships just don���t work? After listening to this read (I have to listen to non-fiction audibly in order to be fully engaged) so much was brought to light in terms of why I act the way I do in my relationships with others, and next steps I can take moving forward to ensure what’s best for me and my peace. It’s all about ensuring the positive relationships and communication that serves YOU best. This read is a safe space that I highly recommend to all!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a pretty straightforward book about attachment styles in romantic relationships. I was hoping for something a little more general or research driven rather than a guide to relationships, but that’s not the book’s fault. They have a little bit of a bias against avoidant styles, but I think that comes with the territory (if an avoidant’s goal is to avoid attachment, and the goal of the book is to promote intimacy, those are gonna clash). I would absolutely recommend this book to anyone who’s been confused by their partner’s actions or the conflicts they seem to repeatedly face in relationships. I’m a serial monogamist, and I feel pretty secure in my relationship, but it helped me understand conflicts my friends have with dating. The book also provides some great guidelines to keep in mind for effective communication, which anyone can benefit from.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: One of the best self help books I have read. I don’t know if I can categorise it as purely self help since it’s also factual and scientific in its approach. This book immensely helped me to understand my attachment style which was a surprise! And also, gave me retrospective perspective on various other relationships and my reactions on various occasions! Knowing your attachment style is so important to avoid anyone gaslighting you. Also helps you stay clear from self loathing talks. Usually I find self help books to be sort of talking about the same stuff in loops and thereby making me loose interest in it. But this book was a clear exception and the numerous highlights and notes I made stands as a proof! Will highly recommend for everyone to read this book at least once to better understand themselves. Because only when you know and accept yourself can you love another person.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It introduces attachment in layman's terms which makes it easy to follow and to understand the basic theory of attachment. I found it useful to understand how people differ in their needs for closeness and proximity, and the conflict and anxiety this can cause in relationships. I think it would be a good introduction for clients to attachment theory to understanding their romantic relationships. However, I feel the examples don't always reflect the complexity of relationships. There also isn't enough information on avoidant attachment, and I feel the book paints people with avoidance attachment in a very negative light. The book feels designed to assist anxiously attached individuals rather than secure and avoidant, so the book lacks balance. Of course there are limits to the theory, as it fails to consider the importance other factors such as personality, that draw people together romantically.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Wow. This book was really an open minding experience. It has made me become even more interested in the psychology behind relationships and attachment styles. It is very reassuring to read from experts and psychologist that find new explanations on why your attachment style attracts you to certain people or make you acquire certain behaviours. The conclusions of these reading are SO important that I feel very clear headed about the power of self awareness and self knowledge. Firstly, I am so glad that they explain attachment styles and corroborate that all needs are legitimate: not everyone has the same needs and the work is in understanding your own needs and finding adequate companionship. As well as aiming for a more secure attachment yourself (by taking care of yourself). Also, I found very interesting that they guided you through examples that in some or other way I'm sure everyone can relate too.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I would highly recommend this book to anyone who is dating, engaged, or married. It starts off by having you take a short assessment of what your attachment style is. It also asks you to evaluate your partners style too. They are both adapted, shorter versions of the original assessment, so they may not be entirely thorough, but it gives you a general idea of what your attachment style might be. I do like that once you know what yours is, they break down each attachment style in a separate chapter to help you understand how it developed. The rest of the chapters give good tips on effective communication with lots of case study examples and scenarios. I think they might’ve overdone it with the examples, but I think its just to get each point across effectively. Overall, would recommend this read!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A solid introduction to attachment theory. Attachment theory talks about the basic human need to depend on others, which is somewhat the antithesis of codependency. It breaks down the 3 most common attachment styles (anxious, avoidant, secure), and specifically calls out that it will not discuss the 4th one (anxious-avoidant) at all. It helps you discern which one you may be, what your partner may be, and how the interaction of the two plays out in intimacy and conflict. While it gives a few ideas on how you can move towards a more secure base, it doesn’t dive deep into why you may be one attachment style, and how to become more secure. My partner and I read this as part of a small book club and learned so much about each other’s attachment styles in various parts of our relationship. It highlighted how the pandemic (living and working from home together 24/7) impacted us and what we were not communicating (i.e. took for granted during pre-pandemic times) that yielded us to a brief period of unease. As we unlearn those behaviors from our attachment styles, we’ve returned back to the secure base we took for granted that was present unintentionally before the pandemic.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Overall, I liked this book and the basic applicable aspects for all attachment types: secure, anxious and avoidant. There were useful assessments you could take for yourself and one you perceived for a partner which I found kind of odd. I would think you would want your partner to do it on their own and then compare notes. Maybe I missed the boat on that one though. At times, I had a hard time with the severity of some of the examples and was hoping for some more nuanced examples that were harder to pinpoint. It was just so easy to determine attachment styles from different case studies they pitched. What I did like is that it encouraged self reflection and compassion in relationships and gave pointers for how to improve relationships of any attachment style iteration. Even the anxious-avoidant type partnership.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Soms iets te veel gegeneraliseerd en ook weer een vrij fucked up afschildering van vermijders, ik mis een beetje grijze zone en hoe onveilige hechting eigenlijk vooral een chaos is aan verlating- en bindingsangst. Verder is het boek zeer waardevol om te begrijpen hoe diepgeworteld hechting zit in onze hele persoonlijkheid, niet enkel in relaties & om meer naar veilige manieren te manoeuvreren die je op lange termijn veel energie besparen. Ik vond ook wel dat het boek iets meer mag inspelen op het accepteren van bepaalde copingmechanismen die je hebt gevormd door je angst rond je hechtingssysteem. Soms is begrijpen wat er gaande is genoeg en wil je niet de urgentie voelen dat er iets aan gedaan moet worden, daarin vind ik Rika Ponnet haar boek dan weer zinvoller, zij legt meer nadruk op een relatievorm kiezen die zinvol is voor jou.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was on my TBR as I wanted to evaluate all my relationships in my life—friendships, family, relationships. This book heavily mentions only being with secure attachment styles and doesn’t really mention ways to communicate effectively if you are not with another secure style person. It just says if you are an anxious style to wonder around until you find a secure person lol. I disagree and believe there are ways for you to work from having an anxious attachment and grow more secure. I think there are situations where you need to re-evaluate and decide whether a relationship is more abusive vs save-able and this book doesn’t cover that. I also don’t believe it is up to the secure party to drive the bond to ensure the anxious/avoidant is stable. The book also doesn’t go into the WHY of why a person may find themselves in a cycle of being in an anxious-avoidant relationship cycle. I think in the case of it being a cycle there’s reasoning behind why and this book didn’t answer that for me just by “switching partners”. I think there’s something more unconscious going on that causes you to be stuck in that cycle I will say this book gave me a lot of insight on why I am the way I am and think it’s a good resource for awareness when paired with therapy

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm not usually one to pick up a self-help book, but I couldn't resist giving this one ago after seeing meme after relatable meme about attachment theory online. It turned out to be a surprisingly great guide on how to embrace your authenticity and communicate effectively. This is probably the first batch of dating advice I've received that doesn't label people as "demanding" or "needy". It simply depicts them as having legitimate emotional needs in a relationship and requiring a partner who is willing and able meet those needs. It is normal to feel distressed when someone is emotionally unavailable or inconsistently affectionate - who knew! It sounds basic (and I suppose it is), but it was very validating without enabling. In my humble (single) opinion, this is a must-read for anyone (dating or otherwise) - especially those with anxious tendencies. Game changer!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 4 out of 5 stars Wow! I really enjoyed this book. I was a bit worried that it was not going to be helpful, considering my background in social psychology but it definitely was. This gives a good oversight of attachment styles; how to communicate effectively and solve conflict in a healthy way; and how to avoid the anxious-avoidant trap. I specifically enjoyed the fact that they used personal stories of others to illustrate the ways in which attachment styles operate. There are also some helpful exercises in this book that help you gauge your own attachment style and deal with your personal triggers. Why not 5 stars? 1) They focused solely on secure, anxious and avoidant attachment styles but you also have the disorganized type. 2) As other reviewers have mentioned, it seemed that the main focus of this book was on the anxious attachment style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: cok guzel bir kitapti. kaygili baglanma stiline sahip oldugumu fark ettim. gunluk hayatimda hissettigim birçok hissin bu baglanma stilimden dolayi dogal olarak icimden geldigini fark ettim. insallah keyifle 'guvenli baglanma' yetenegi gelistirebilirim. daha da onemlisi insallah benim yakinim olan insanlar ve eşim 'guvenli baglanma' stiline sahip insanlar olur. kaygili baglanmayi biraktiracak 4 ipucunu not edecegim: 1. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I don’t know why I keep reading popular kitchen psychology books as a psychology student even so they keep disappointing me. Did this book have a lot of scientific facts that are not normally known for people? Yes! And it’s great, but I don’t understand, why the authors basically tell people, that there are „good“ and „bad“ attachment types. This stigmatisation doesn’t really help people to figure out what they need in the relationship. My next big concern was secure attached people being the solution for every attachment type in finding relationship. Like what? First of all it’s just unrealistic and stupid to use secure attachment as a solution for everything. Second of all if you wanna give people a piece of advice on how to find happy relationships give some concrete information for every attachment type on how not to rely on other people and change your mindset yourself. I don’t know Just disappointing

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book starts off strong but turns out to provide somehow basic knowledge on attachment theory, mainly focuses on anxious / avoidant attachments and does not explore at al nuances (eg what about secure attachment styles with an anxious tendency?). As a queer person, I found the “some told us we don’t use queer couples as examples but sure look what we say applies to all” very normative and a tad disingenuous. If that’s the case just turn Samantha and Greg into Samantha and Jenny, cause I’m sure you’ve heard about the concepts of “visibility” and “representation”. Also on this note, I am not a psychology expert but the lack of mention of how gender / sexuality (but also beyond, eg race / class) elements shape us and our attachments seems a bit naive. I did like the quizzes at the beginning. Recommend a quick scan but not a cover to cover read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book opened my eyes to many important facts, the most striking being that, as human beings, we fundamentally need relationships for survival, and that others can directly influence our well-being. It offers valuable tips and advice on how to better manage and maintain relationships. While it’s especially helpful for those currently in a relationship, I believe it’s also vital for anyone who wants to strengthen their connections with others. The book explains the different attachment styles and provides guidance on how to navigate them, with the ultimate goal of moving toward a more secure attachment. Some parts did feel like common sense or intuitive, and honestly, I expected it to be a bit more informative. Instead, it leaned more toward casual and fun rather than deeply thought-provoking. Overall, I recommend it particularly to those who fall on the anxious or avoidant side of the attachment spectrum.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I loved how this book didn’t frame one attachment style as better than another, or label any of them as “toxic.” It wasn’t about trying to fix or change your anxious or avoidant attachment, but more about saying, “this is your attachment style and that’s okay.” Often it’s shaped by what your childhood looked like or how love was experienced early on. What it really offered was awareness and acceptance, which led to a lot of healing for me. I realised that in my past relationships I wasn’t asking for “too much”, I just wasn’t with someone who had the capacity to love me in the reassuring way I needed and I also didn’t have the capacity to love them in the way they needed. Now, being with my current partner, I can see how different attachment styles can actually work well together. With trust, communication and learning, it’s possible to grow and feel more secure over time.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached is a very accessible overview of attachment theory applied to adult relationships. It provides a really helpful working theory for describing different attachment styles (secure, anxious, avoidant) and their interactions. I now have a better understanding of some of my past failings in romantic relationships (and also why my current one is so good). I am a lot of fun at happy hours too, now that I can expertly psychoanalyze why your relationships aren’t working. Hit me up. (Picked this up in an Audible Valentine’s Day sale. The book doesn’t really work in audio form – there are multiple hours of audio time dedicated to a recitation of quizzes and descriptions of worksheets. While these interactive self-reflection activities would have been helpful in print form, they make for a laborious listen.)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm torn about this one. Being a psychologist, I already knew about attachment theory and how it extends to relationships in adulthood. But it still gave me more insight into the particular behaviour patterns associated with the different styles, and I really enjoyed that! It helped me understand more about myself and others. What I didn't like is how absolute the authors' voices were. It was as if they were pushing an agenda, and the examples through the book were very black and white, almost caricature-like. I dont fall neatly within one attachment style, and I think that's the case for many many others. However, there was little recognition of this in the book. If you inject your own shades of gray though, I think this book has a lot to offer.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: One of the most useful books I've ever read. Levine and Heller can really help people new to the attachment theory have a quick grasp of it and know how to apply it in their lives. One down thing is that they didn't write much about the avoidant type, which, in my opinion, needs the most help they can get (even though they usually don't seek them). However, the authors stated clearly that the book is meant for the anxious type. So I still give them 5 stars. This book is a must-read for anyone who wants to improve their romantic relationships. The book, however, personally helps me gain more insights into my relationships with friends and family as well. I really hope Levine and Heller can write another with a focus on avoidant type. Thanks for the great book!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Good rebuttal to books like ‘Why Men Love Bitches’ (which advise you to play cat-and-mouse) so it gets one star more than that one. I thought the book had interesting points, but also that people and relationships are more nuanced than the 3 principal attachment types (anxious/avoidant/secure) they talk about. I have definitely felt all three modes at different points in the same relationship and can say the same thing about most of my partners. Also, the book is written for people with anxious attachment styles and it kind of looks down upon the ‘avoidant’ ones - which I thought wasn’t very helpful. There’s also nothing here on unconventional/open relationships. My last thought is that I should take a short break from self-help books because (for whatever reason) they almost always trigger me a bit :/

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The title and the cover make this book look really cringey HOWEVER I found it really interesting. I wouldn’t pick this type of book out usually but I saw someone recommend it and I’m really glad I read it! I’ve learnt a lot about how attachment affects children through my degree and my job as a teacher however I found it fascinating to learn about how attachment theory applies to adults in relationships. I do agree with other reviews that the authors aren’t as generous in their descriptions of people with avoidant attachment styles and all of the examples seem to use hetero “gender typical” couples eg an avoidant man and an anxious woman. Having said this, I gained a lot from this book and I think it has really helped me to better understand myself and I would recommend it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Levine and Heller takes the research of British psychologist and psychoanalyst John Bowlby, who in the 1950s examined the early relationships between parents, caregivers and children and continue the theory to adult relationships. (Bowlby observed three attachment styles Anxious, Avoidant and Secure.) *ANXIOUS people are often preoccupied with their relationships and tend to worry about their partner's ability to love them back. *AVOIDANT people equate intimacy with a loss of independence and constantly try to minimize closeness. *SECURE people feel comfortable with intimacy and are usually warm and loving. Why I started this book: Chosen for one of my Book Clubs, and highly recommended. Why I finished it: Interesting theory and examples. Liked the take away of open and often communication prevents a lot of heartbreak and allows everyone in the relationship to be healthy and happy.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: After hearing so much talk about it, I finally read it. I’d say the book is worth the actual read. Based on all the sound bites, I knew the premises of secure, anxious, avoidant attachment styles.
