But the real golden nuggets were embedded in the real life scenarios of how conversations between couples can go. The biggest takeaway was that people approach romantic relationships differently and that we must be mindful of those differences to be more at peace internally. At the same time, there are objectively superior, healthier styles of communication that everyone can benefit from. The book prescribes a secure-attachment style as the optimal way to relate to your partner. Yet another framework to practice empathy and transparency. Obvi much easier said than done.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book is amazing for (what I imagine) is it’s target audience - anxiously attached people who are in early stages of a relationship or looking to date. It does a lovely job at validating the needs of those anxiously attached, and supporting them to access the right partner for them as well as how to understand and communicate their needs effectively. I think at times it can be a bit black/white, and doesn’t give much to people who may have an avoidant or secure style, or those who are currently in relationships (excepting the effective communication chapter). While there are good descriptors and attachment has usually been described discretely - it’s important to remember that it exists on a spectrum like everything else.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: As an avoidant person, I would have never read the book by the Spanish translation of the title ("Ways to love")🤣 But attachment is my favorite field in psychology, and its English title was the key to read the book, and I highly recommend it, specially for people who are not familiar with how attachment works. The only thing I missed in this book is that there are some aspects of avoidant attachment that are missing, because there also exist people who care about others, but that don't let other people care about them; and I think that it only describes the most generic behaviors (the ones that make them all look like people with no empathy or selfish, just thinking in themselves, but in the book they all look like monsters). They also ignored to talk about disorganized attachment...

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I thoroughly enjoyed this book! A lot of it is very applicable to the work I do as a counselor, and it helped me gain more insights about how attachments impact relational functioning. I realized that I have a tendency to lean more on the side of "You need to be independent and not rely too much on your partner," but this book helped me recognize that some level of dependency is normal! It's okay for people to know what their relational needs are and to seek out a partner who can meet those needs. I enjoyed that it addressed how both avoidant and anxiously attached individuals can communicate their needs while also make changes to embrace more secure principles. I also found it helpful to learn more about the qualities of securely attached individuals!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: My issues: 1. A lot of words, but not a great deal of substance to this book. It was sold as this revolutionary take on Attachment, but it really didn’t feel like it. 2. The heteronormacy!! My goodness, of all the MANY examples I think ONE was a same sex couple. And it just so happened to be the one at the start of the chapter about the most destructive relationships. I mean really?!? Every example made me groan when I realised it was ANOTHER male-female couple. 3. Heavily biased in the ways it presents the attachment styles. Definitely leans towards sympathy for the anxiously attached and disdain for the avoidants. 4. Nothing of concrete use for the anxious-avoidant attached among us!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 9/10 review, this book is a BREATH OF FRESH AIR when dealing with some interpersonal struggles... I even find myself referring back to it for tools and terms after having read it. My only real issue, the reasons I gave one star less than a full "HURRAH!" was the gender-based wording... I found plenty of spots where the authors used "He/She," "S/he," and "he or she," sometimes even followed by a "Them!", it feels like they could have simply used They/Them/Theirs when referring to one person OR multiple of (any gender) throughout the entire book and maintained an equally steady and clear flow. The focus was on Attachment Styles and personal growth afterall, which is clearly not rooted within our gender.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5/5 rounded down. I really wanted to like this book more and it was quite helpful for someone with an anxious attachment style especially, but it also had many pitfalls. This author loves to dickride secure people and villainize avoidant people. They also make it seem like insecure people love to be unhappy and can only be happy with finding these rare Pokemon aka secure people which I don't agree with. Overall the psychology is interesting and useful and I would recommend people to read this book or at least learn more about attachment theory (especially if you are insecure or in a relationship with someone who is insecure), however many of the examples and some of the stuff this author says are so wild.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Really helpful as it takes shame out of the equation, explains the root reason behind and puts terms to thoughts, experiences, expressions you have and also observe in others so that you can have more compassion for yourself and others, helps you recognize when others capacities don’t blend with your own to avoid hurt, and helps you build a more secure attachment stye for yourself. Sometimes simple and repetitive but that’s needed to get the point driven and it only spends a great deal of time discussing the anxiousness avoidant trap and I wish it would’ve explored more mixes like maybe anxious and anxious and the nuances of seeing yourself in traits from all the types but still really good and I think everyone should read it since it would help people avoid arguments or shame.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a great first nonfiction read for me and really made me get a more scientific side to human relations. The book tells what most of us already believe as a relationship should be and extends it to a very simple principle. In a way, it really helped me understand my insecurities even more. Even if you are not in a relationship, this really explains why we behave the way we do and what is the most effective approach to start or deal with a relationship. With the help of studies and examples, we get a clearer explanation, as well as the fill-in spaces to get a better understanding of your own style. Overall, I did enjoy this book, just hoped for more diversity as there were no examples of certain couples only focusing on the trap and the way secure people help insecure ones.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: DNF. I had a lot of problems with this book. It seemed to spend a lot time talkikg about how the needs of people with an anxious attachment style are valid, but seemed to suggest that the needs of those on the avoidant side are not, at least implicitly. This was constantly infuriating and alienating. The former point is an important one to make, because as the authors state, our society tells us quite a lot that we should be self-reliant and not need other people - which is patently ridiculous. But everyones needs should be given validity. Also, there was literally only one mention of disorganised attachment in the entire book, which was basically "its both". This is really unhelpful. Finally, a lot of what it talked about was pretty basic intro to attachment theory stuff, so also wasn't all that helpful.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very interesting to learn about the different “attachment” styles in this book. I loved all of the example stories that were given to demonstrate the different concepts in the book. I also loved that it gave hands on tools so that you can do assessments on your own. I feel like I can detect some of these attachment tendencies in people now which kind of feels like a superpower. Muahahaha. Though this book was mainly about romantic relationships, I also feel like a lot of these concepts also translate over to friendships, family relationships and even work. I think that I can tend to have an “avoidant” style when it comes to work and am already trying to apply some of these concepts to improve my work environment. I listened to this on audiobook and the narrator was engaging. I felt like it didn’t need to read through all of the survey questions but overall it was great!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Great book! Especially a good read for those of you who are anxious or avoidant attached (Read the book if you don't know what those things are). If there's one listen I take away from this book is the concept of dependency paradox; the idea that the more you can rely on your partner as a secure base, the more independent you become in the outside world. All that stuff about "you shouldn't expect your partner to address your emotional needs to be independent" is BS. The book seemed a bit superficial however. I would have appreciated more in-depth analysis and less number of examples for the same thing over and over again. Albeit it serves as a good hands-on guide on your journey of love, regardless of what stage you're in.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: More of a 3.5, but rounding up bc I think the material is important! Lots of examples and tools given to help you sort out your own attachment style, and gain some helpful insight when it comes to engaging with different attachment styles. The emphasis on effective communication feels super applicable to all relationships: romantic, platonic, familial, business, etc. The material did start to feel repetitive after a while however, and I think this book could use an update with more modern examples and inclusivity. It also did feel a bit heavy on the sort of business syntax, but I started to take this with a grain of salt as I went along. Overall, an important read, and it sparked some great discussion and self-reflection, as I was reading this with my roommate. :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is excellent if you want to learn about attachment theory. The first half of the book gives a thorough explanation of the history of attachment theory, the different attachment styles, and an inventory to find out what your attachment style is. The second half of the book attempts to help navigate relationship issues based on your and your partner's attachment style. Considering that one of the suggestions is to break up with your partner based on your incompatible attachment styles, I would not recommend the second half of this book to clients. If you want to learn more about attachment science, the first part of this book is great! If you are looking for suggestions on developing secure attachment, find a therapist trained in EFT and pick up a book by Sue Johnson :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I liked this book quite a bit. At first, I was sucked in, reading nonstop (most likely my mental state being the main factor at the time, but I still have to credit the book for keeping my attention, which isn‘t an easy feat when I am not in that great of a mental space). In the middle it got a bit repetitive for me and thereof a little boring. In general, a good book with many case studies and some behavioral science facts (and I eat that shit up as an anthropology major), but not that many helpful tips for the avoidant type. It felt like a nice intro so you could go and get a book specific to your problem, now that you have honed in on what the problem actually is and what attachment style you think you have. *More helpful for anxious types than avoidant, I would say*

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a practical, research-backed, easily understood introduction to attachment theory. Lots of scenarios were illustrated here to give the reader detailed understanding of how each attachment styles behave, and I had great takeaways from this book: * Having intimate romantic relationships are great predictors of happiness and satisfaction in life as we are social and emotional creatures * Avoidants are overrepresented in the dating market as they tend to cycle out of relationships faster * You cannot change someone’s need/threshold for intimacy * Yet there are effective communication strategies that can cushion conflicts when they arise, but you must be aware of how much you’re compromising on * Anxious people often confuse an activated attachment system where they’re experiencing mixed signals from someone they’re dating as “love”

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a really good book about attachment styles: what they are, where they come from, how they manifest, how to address them. It throws in a lot of science, so you understand that this is just how people are wired and that this concept throughly affects people’s lives. I borrowed it from the library (of course) but I took notes so I could continue to refer to the idea and suggestions. What’s nice about this book, is that it both encourages you to accept your attachment style, ie accept that this is just how you’re wired, and also gives advice about how to push past your instincts and make conscious choices about how to react and behave. You can’t help your attachment style, but you can notice when you’re reacting because of it, and make the choice for effective communication instead. I think it’s a good read for anything thinking about romantic relationships, single or taken.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: First of all, I would like to emphasise that I had this book as a recomendation reading at school and it caught my attention so much that I read it whole. And I'm happy I did. I have liked the attachment theory (baby or adult) from the first time I've heard of it. I think it nicely covers all the differences and problems you can encounter living with different people. Not to mention trying to have a fullfiling relationship with your loved one. Thanks to this book I have finally understood some people and came to terms with their behaviour. It is a real eye opener, to find out how the same thing can have different meaning for every attachment style. I would definitely recommend this book. Some people will finally start to make sence to you ;).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: OK, we get it. The avoidants are the bad guys. In all seriousness, this book is just simply more for anxious individuals. Every scenario where there is a "clear cut" party in the wrong, 99% of the time they were an archetype avoidant. There is good information in here about all attachment styles but as far as exercises to mitigate the risk of jeopardizing relationships (romantic or platonic) as an avoidant... it stemmed down to... "make a list about why you like this person".. and "stop acting like how you act because it can be hurtful to others" (nevermind that when it came to anxious people it was "its ok that you act like how you act cause thats how your brain is wired").... womp womp

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book was a quick read, so I’ll keep this short. It made me think—a lot. Not even necessarily about the specific content or the authors’ arguments (though it did feel pretty slanted against avoidants). What really struck me was the reflection it prompted in me. I’m anxious, and I have work to do. But it also reminded me that avoidants are real people too, with equally valid feelings. Neither attachment style is worse, nor more “worthy” than the other. We’re all just people trying to feel safe, loved, and seen—just in different ways. This book helped spark that thought process, and for that I’m grateful. Still sitting with some feelings, sigh. I can’t change the past, not that I would want to.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book primarily focuses on relationships from the perspective of an anxiously attached individual, so it might not be for everyone. But for me, I've never read a book that's so accurately described my personality in relationships as this one did. I found it very helpful not only in recognizing my own behaviors (what the authors call “protest behaviors”) but also in understanding the actions of others and why these patterns often trigger each other. It also offers plenty of practical recommendations and examples on how to communicate more effectively in relationships. Overall, I think anyone can learn something valuable from this book, regardless of their attachment style. and would defiantly recommend this book to anyone with an anxious attachment style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I like books that unlocks personal insights, and I’d say this book did that for me. It breaks down attachment theory, explains the three main attachment styles (avoidant, anxious, and secure), and walks through relationship scenarios to show how those styles play out in real life. Reading this, I found myself reflecting a lottttt. Dissecting all my current and past relationships lol. I’m not sure I fully subscribe to the idea that someone is one attachment style all the time. Personally I think the theory is a little restricting in that way. I think humans are dynamic, and different kinds of responses can be activated, depending on the relationship/situation. 🤷🏼‍♀️ All said, it was a little repetitive in parts, but overall was a solid read. 4/5 ⭐️

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Book clubbed this with a friend. Honestly felt like pulling teeth to get through this one. I am genuinely wondering why people like this book? I feel like I just read 300 pages of the same surface level paragraph, "A and B wanted something specific out of a relationship. They communicated this. It scared avoidant people away, but eventually they found confidence in communicating their needs and found the right person for them. Then they ran off into the sunset!" Over, and over, and over again. I don't mean to be too scathing; if someone has never heard of attachment style theory before, this book would be a great place to start. But for anyone that has consistently gone to therapy or had a self-reflection practice of some sort, this book might fall short. It's written for too general of an audience, so that it can be a best-seller, but as a result it has no depth and goes nowhere.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This seems to be a very popular book to introduce people to attachment styles, however, I found it to be too simplistic and tending towards pigeonholing people into one of three categories: secure, anxious or avoidant. While there are one or two sentences on those who have a disorganized attachment, it felt very much ignored. Levine/Heller states that Attachment Styles “aren’t good or bad, they simply are what they are.” However, throughout the book they consistently paint the picture of avoidants being abusive cheaters and anxious people being misunderstood victims. The solution they provide to attachment issues is to either only be in relationships with secure people, avoid avoidants, or provide anxious people with the constant reassurance they are looking for. Effective communication and techniques to become more secure are thrown into the end but none of it felt particularly fleshed out in a way that those with attachment issues could find useful. I’ve since discovered the Dynamic Maturation Model of attachment by Patricia Crittendon that feels like it may help explain attachment styles in a more realistic and useful way. My advice is to skip this book if you want to read up on attachment styles, unless of course you are an anxiously attached individual simply looking for reassurance that you are not too needy or toxic. In the case of the latter, you might actually enjoy this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is worth your time whether you are single or in a relationship, IMO. The authors distill human attachment styles into 3 types: secure, anxious, and avoidant, detail how to navigate each of these styles along with strategies for recognizing your own/your partner’s tendencies, and describe effective communication techniques as it relates to your own style. I found this to be an engaging read, although I thought the use of many female “anxious” examples and many male “avoidant” examples was a bit stereotypical and sexist, despite their assurance in the book that this is not always the case. All in all, would recommend, especially if you feel like dependency in a relationship is bad, as I felt in the past (spoiler alert: it’s not!).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I heard of this book from some of the YouTube relationship videos I came across. This book was full of examples; I particularly liked the format where they give a situation and conflict and quiz us (rhetorically) whether he/she is avoidant or anxious. Yes the reality is grey. But it's still good to have a mental framework and categorization. I have to close with the bitter comment though. As someone leaning towards avoidant, the book has a tone to protect anxious people against cold blooded avoidant. It is probably because anxious are the ones who come seek help to psychologists and the majority of audiences. Avoidant would just go "huh🤷‍♂️ Move on". I look forward to a book specifically made for avoidant. (Or anxious for the others)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is an insightful book. It discusses a variety of topics that are useful to know including determining your attachment style, identifying your partner's attachment style, the different dynamics that do exists between the different attachment styles, and how to ultimately grow as an individual to form healthier bonds. The book utilizes examples to help depict the different scenarios that do exist and it does go into depth on the different domains of attachment styles. I do wish that it included more information on how these attachment styles are formed and also more scientific evidence on the topics it discusses.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Easy-to-read overview of attachment theory in relationships. Focuses a lot on anxious attachers and what things can help their relationships become more secure. Advice is decent overall, though I took issues with some of the monogamous-culture defaults. A few stances the authors take that I disagree with: * you are responsible for your partner's emotional well-being * flirting with others is inherently problematic * boundaries around parts of your personal life are problematic / enmeshment is a positive goal. The book is a quick read --- 3-4 hours of content to read plus ~1 hour of workbook material.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: While I don’t think Attached is the end-all-be-all of relationship books, it had a lot of interesting and valuable knowledge in it that helped me better understand past and present relationships. It’s short enough that it’s a relatively quick read, so definitely worth a read. The only reason I don’t give it a five star is that I think it does leave out a lot of important parts of relationships and keeping them fun over years in a healthy and safe way. That said, getting to the secure base the authors talked about is a hugely valuable starting point, so this book will likely benefit most people that read it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I got this book as a gift from a dear friend. At first I didn't really want to read it because it's about relationships and I'm not in one. But my friend convinced me – not only could I look back at past relationships and try to figure out what (if at all) I could have done to make them last. Also, I could take a good hard look at myself and perhaps avoid the worst pitfalls, should a new potential partner present themselves. And really, it's basic principle is very convincing and very simple, not something you forget after you put the book down. I've given it a lot of thought while reading it and also now after having finished it. And I'll surely be giving it more thought, should I come across persons who obviously fall into one of the book's 3 (4) categories of people (in terms of relationships). I've no doubt as to which category I myself fall into and it's not the most attractive one. But now at least I can work on it!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 4.5 Very easy to read while still being technical enough to feel scientific (unlike self help books that feel more touchy feely and less based on clinical studies). If you’re somewhat familiar with attachment theory already this book is still interesting and helpful to read when it comes to you wanting to develop more secure attachment ways of thinking and behaviours, particularly for those who lean towards a more anxious attachment style. For those who are more secure or avoidant, I’m really not sure if this book will do much for you though, though a skim is definitely worth it, particularly on the secure communication chapters.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was an eye opening, confronting book on the different attachment styles we have in relationships. While it was a good intro to attachment styles, the 3 options you fall into (secure/anxious/avoidant) seem limiting and don't include other styles of attachments that are included in other resources (fearful avoidant/disorganised). This book has prompted me to research more on attachment styles and focus more on moving toward a 'secure style' rather than keeping myself in the box of an anxious/avoidant style. I've heard 'The Power of Attachment' by Diane Poole Heller is more gentle and gives a lot of advice on moving to a secure attachment style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is a great starter book to help you understand your relationship needs (as well as potential or actual partners). A big plus for me is the premise that you don’t need to beat yourself up or change what you need to be loveable but there are specific thought patterns you can engage to manage the worst case scenarios that many of us find ourselves in. I think it would be beneficial to re-read this book as you find yourself in different life stages. There’s a lot of content in here that will continue to provide fresh takes on as you find yourself single, dating, married or anywhere in between.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: If you’ve talked to me in the past week or so I for sure have found a way to mention this book and ramble on (sorry) (not sorry🤪). Truly such a necessary read probably for everyone of us out here. Learned a lot A LOT and about attachment theory and adult relationships and intimacy and communication and knowing your own protection methods and ideas of closeness. This sucker had quizzes to take and interactive scenarios to walk through for crying out loud. Reminded and reassured me that dependency isn’t a bad word and how to debunk the idea of “neediness”. In conclusion-we all have basic need to form close bonds and the way we create them varies. Check mate okay bye

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Have I shut up about this book since I've started reading it? No. Will I ever be able to look at someone without analyzing their attachment style? No. Is it embarrassing to post a review for a dating self-help book? Maybe. Do I care? No. Yes, I have anxious attachment so maybe the reviews are right in that this book only helps those with the same attachment as me BUT I greatly appreciated being able to analyze my past relationships in a way that didn't make me feel crazy! So yes! I will take the lessons learned with me and be insufferable about attachment style for years to come!!!!!!!!!!!!!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was… moderately helpful in places? But mostly over-generalized soft science. And I say that as someone who loves to over-generalize relationship science with magical personality tests and (on really rough days) astrology (just kidding, mostly). I don’t think humans boil down to either anxious or avoidant or stable, and the author of this book is certain we do. I know I have been all of these things at different times in my life. On the other hand, it was empowering to recognize some of my more anxious tendencies and re-evaluate their effectiveness. I prefer therapy, but that’s not always available so this book is probably a good resource, if taken with a grain of salt.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is a godsend. It's an absolute must read for those of us with insecure attachment styles (which is roughly 50% of the population, btw) and helped me better understand not only myself, but my relationships with others. It is incredibly insightful and helpful in growing my understanding of empathy and love in relationships. I loved not only the explanations for each style that helped me truly get seen, but also the guide for determining your partner's attachment style and how to better improve your communication within each attachment style. Highly, highly recommend! Might just buy six copies so I can throw them in my friends' faces and force them to read it too lol

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Another deep dive into the self-help / self-improvement genre. This time, I delve into relationship science, something that I will say, I’ve been grudgingly avoiding. I mean for real, who wants to be told what to do and what not to do in their own relationship? No one truly. That being said, I took a lot from this read, some good and some things to grow upon, all of which I am thankful for. I think that anyone who may struggle in relationships or has some unanswered questions in their relationships would benefit from reading this book. Even if it doesn’t help directly with any stuck points in a relationship, I think this should prove itself beneficial to most. Solid and quick read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The material is more of a 5 star rating, but unfortunately for this kind of subject matter there’s only so much you can say without repeating yourself. My honest review is that if you are someone interested in knowing yourself/partner (whether they currently exist or not) better, and want to have a better understanding of relationship dynamics, I suggest this book. It also has the potential to provide closure for past relationships, and provides reasonable explanations for the way people tend to behave in relationships. It was an eye opener to read, and I cannot deny having learned enough where I feel my approach to attachment has matured, and will hopefully continue to improve!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I’ve never read anything like this, but I really enjoyed it. I’m not a scientist lol so I can’t speak to whether or not they are referencing the science with fidelity or if it’s cherry picked in some spots (like some other reviews are claiming). But, this book did provide a great framework to view relationships and allowed me the opportunity to do a lot of necessary self-reflection, which was really enlightening for me. I learned a lot about myself that I wouldn’t have if I had not picked this up. I would definitely revisit this as well, because I could see how you could gain different insight with a reread.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: por incrível que pareça demorei 22 dias a ler este livro. tem letras grandes e consegue-se ler rapidamente. o tema que fala (vinculação) já me tinha sido apresentado no “8 Rules of Love” e este livro fez me aprofundar o tema. gostei das partes mais interativas; do facto de conseguir estabelecer paralelismos com as minhas relações anteriores/atuais e com a dos que me rodeiam. De certa forma, preparou me para relações que terei (não apenas amorosas) porque dá me uma amostra do que tenho de “procurar”/ “atrair” Mostra que as relações não são mares de rosas e a importância da “comunicação efetiva” para evitar o escalar de temperamentos.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a pretty helpful book when it comes to understanding your needs in relationships. I typically struggle to fully connect with one of the attachment styles, and I would say that this book clarified some things for me. My qualms are the same as with any self help book (generalizing, repetition, over simplifying and making it seem easy to fix your problems lol). There was also some glorification of secure people but maybe I’m just projecting. If you struggle with justifying your needs, understanding where they come from, and being able to communicate that (me to all of the above) I would recommend.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is overall a helpful book to look into yourself and how you react to situations in your relationships, whether they be platonic or romantic. It gave helpful examples to look through and gave generalized attributes of people who may have the same attachment as you do. The few downfalls of this book is that it overly generalizes relationships and your type of attachment, it uses research from over twenty years ago so it is slightly outdated, and it's not inclusive for same gender/non-binary relationships. So, take everything with a grain of salt, but I did thoroughly enjoy learning about myself and my friend through this experiment.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A book I would recommend as required reading before starting a relationship. I loved that it is research-based and gives a wide range of examples that illustrate both how to observe in others (and ourselves) the three attachment styles but also how you might change your attachment style from anxious/avoidant to secure. I came away with a lot of good 💡 ideas from it and will definitely come back to it again noting that I, too, still have a lot of work to do on some relationship skills. It was a book that made me aware that relationships are not an abstract concept that we are born skilled at but require intentional work and some learnable skills.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: started reading this like 2pm singapore time and finished 10pm san francisco time on the same "day" good book for learning more about attachment styles and how to apply this theory to relationships in your own life — understand their dynamics better, make them more fulfilling, etc like many people i've heard about attachment styles a bunch as a buzzword, but a few perspectives from this book surprised me - most people are secure - it's valid to be anxious or avoidant, and to use that knowledge to get your needs met — previously i was under the impression that the only option for anxious or avoidant types was to change their thoughts/feelings/behaviors to be more secure

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was such a fun and interesting read. So many ‘ah-ha’ moments. This book squashed some of my thoughts of being too needy, dependent or emotional in relationships and helped me realize it is actually a very normal thing. I learned so much about myself and how I can better serve others that I share a relationship with. So much psychology, research studies and stories in this book that is so insightful. Love love love! “After all, we live in a culture that seems to scorn basic needs for intimacy, closeness and especially dependency, while exalting independence. We tend to accept this attitude as truth- to our detriment”

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The topic of the book was very new to me so I was curious to know more about it. The authors did a great job bringing research to practise in an engaging and informative manner. Knowing the three attachment styles: their traits, manifestations, mismatches, their pros and cons, etc. I feel more aware and cautious on the 'why' and 'how' we behave in a certain way when we're in love. I definitely recommend this book! My only remark is that the book sometimes reads repetitively as it regularly wants to emphasize the same traits of the attachment styles in each chapter. I therefore give it four stars

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I never read self help books, some kind of ego thing I suppose- never felt the need. Despite this, lately I have felt like I have had no hold on my emotions and found myself describing these feelings as ‘crazy’. Because of this a friend recommend this book, stating it helped them when they felt similar. This book isn’t magic, it doesn’t have all of the answers but it does provide easy and helpful tools and information to better identify, address, and adhere to issues in relationships. I feel that after finishing this book I was given much clarity as to why I feel the way I do and how to communicate it in a healthy and effective way. The information was super easy to understand through examples, analogies, and studies.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Simplista, heteropatriarcal, centrado en monogamia, con sesgo de género, situaciones e historias que se resuelven de manera cuestionable, posicionado claramente en favor del ansioso y atacando constantemente al evasivo, ignorando combinaciones entre ambos (apego desordenado) y encasillando en las etiquetas de manera muy rígida. Una lectura totalmente inútil si ya has leído sobre la teoría del apego. Una lectura a evitar si tu objetivo no es encontrar a “tu alma gemela” ya que se centra en eso incluso recomendando tener muchas citas a la vez e ignora por completo el resto de relaciones afectivas que puedas tener ya que la que prima, la única que realmente importa es la pareja.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was truly eye-opening in so many ways. As someone with an anxious attachment style, it helped me better understand my triggers and protest behaviors, which has significantly changed my approach to dating. I’ve realized that the traits I once worried might be roadblocks in my relationships are actually not insurmountable at all. The insights it provides are incredibly empowering and have given me a fresh perspective on attachment, how we function in relationships, and how we react to the world around us. I highly recommend this book to everyone—whether you’re dating, single, or in a long-term relationship. It’s a must-read for anyone seeking a deeper understanding of themselves and their relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Interesting view of relationships, needed that. I only have two small points to make (thus, the lacking fifth star): - Though the authors happen to sooth my bias towards breaking down any event/interaction in small reproducible pieces to try and find correlation and causations in bigger phenomena, I find that sometimes the scientific basis is murky. It is solid to expose the troubles of interacting between people with different attachment styles, much less so to design an arbitrary way of dealing with such; - On the other hand I tend to be wary of simplistic views and univariate dependance links, so I’m slightly triggered by the matter of fact tone in which the authors state, in the beginning, that it’s EASY to understand why people act the way they do in relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a great book on the attachment theory & practice. I have been reading and actively working on the attachment styles, this book made things much more clear for me. All the attachment styles are well explained and the examples from real-life are spot on. The only criticism that I can think of is the authors seem to have favored the anxious attachment type. I understand the reasoning behind it; the avoidants seem to have the upper hand in society & relationships and that is not fair. Avoidants and anxious are pretty much two halves of the same apple. It seems as the authors have tried to level the game. Overall, an excellent book that will make you question your attachment style; which is an important step in your own inward journey.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 0 stars. This book in summary “don’t ever date an avoidant”. It’s not accurate, it’s over simplified and reductionist. The authors clear bias is evident from page 1 and I can’t bring myself to finish it. It completely glorifies anxious attachment as “only wanting intimacy and closeness” and encourages anxious and secure people to avoid avoidant at all costs and paints avoidant attachment as insensitive and hurtful and even abusive. Page 67 -68 “avoidants will devalue you” “avoidant will respond in one of the following ways: you’re too demanding, disregard your needs”. Incredibly lost for words with this book….

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book completely shifted the way I look at relationships. It helped me recognize patterns not only in my own relationship, but also in the lives of people close to me. I realized that our reactions often have a deeper why—and this book helped me connect those dots in such a clear, compassionate way. Even if you have a secure attachment style, I still think this book has so much to offer. It deepened my understanding of how and why people relate the way they do, which is something I truly love learning about. Oh! And if you’re single there is much advice in this book for picking a solid life partner. Highly recommend!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Everyone should read this book while they’re dating. I have tons of quotes from this book in my notes app. In a real personal note this was so validating to read after a breakup. Legit have paragraphs I wrote about how after the breakup I felt crazy and now I’m able to look at things with an attachment theory lens and realize that was not the best fit for me. Will forever be grateful to my therapist for recommending this book and moving forward looking for a secure gentleman 🫡🫡 but also I’m a secure woman so it doesn’t really matter and I feel confident now that I bring so much strength to a relationship.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: DNF at 65% I really tried to finish but it felt like running into a wall over and over. It's poorly written, for one thing, which was a surprise since I was expecting something a bit more academic in tone and approach. As I'm fully sick of this book right now, I feel like it's only useful for people who pin all their hopes for a fulfilling life on romantic relationships and, apparently, need to be told over and over that effective communication with a partner is important. (! who would've guessed that!) Attachment styles are still interesting to me (I did glean some cool insights from the beginning section) but this honestly burned me from reading more about them anytime soon.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: First book I’ve read in like a decade idek. I found it insightful on a surface level - had a couple “ohh yep” moments that made me reflect on my own patterns and behaviours BUT the book didn't fix my attachment style... I guess fair.. It's up to you as the reader to apply the ideas and actively work on yourself so I guess that is the hard part. I also realised that I already knew many of the ideas discussed, so in some ways it felt more like confirmation of things I had already observed rather than learning entirely new insights. It was still validating to see my beliefs validated through a body of psychological research and evidence presented in the book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Keine Bewertung, weil: für mich war das Buch eine 3/3,5 aber bestimmt ist es für andere viel besser bzw. Hilfreicher. Den ersten Theorie-Part fand ich sehr interessant und aufschlussreich, aber nachher als es mehr in die Tiefe ging, fing ich an es extrem langweilig und wiederholend zu finden. Ich muss zugeben, die letzten Seiten habe ich überflogen. Ich glaube, aber dass liegt daran, dass ich mit dem meisten schon bewusst war und ich nur das Gefühl habe ich lese etwas was ich schon weiß. Außerdem fand ich, dass vieles extrem in die Länge gezogen wurde und sehr viele Beispiele benutzt wurden. Was wie gesagt für manche super hilfreich ist, aber für mich extrem langweilig.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached är en tillgänglig introduktion till anknytningsteori för partner relationer. Exemplen är många och pedagogiska, lätt att känna igen sig. Men för den som gillar tyngre litteratur (inklusive jag) känns ramverket lite väl förenklat. Det som stör mest är att boken till stor del verkar skriven för den ängslige i ett förhållande med en undvikande partner. Andra dynamiker, som ängslig-ängslig, behandlas knappt alls och den säkrare anknytningen täcks relativt lite om. Boken känns därmed något skev. Bra som startpunkt, men för djupare insikter behöver man nog hitta fler böcker att fylla gapen med.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I just finished listening to Attached and I think this book is brilliant. It’s written in a way that’s easy to follow and relate to. I was able to pick out my own personal attachment style right away, and also identify a lot of my own ineffective communication in a previous relationship. Had I read this book back in 2010, there probably wouldn’t have been so many years lived in complete turmoil. At the same time, it gave me information I was able to really soak in and use to give myself some grace. Overall, I would recommend this book to anyone in the dating world ♥️ reading this IMO will enhance your experience. Remain true to your authentic self ✨

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Self-help books are not usually my cup of tea, and I actually don’t remember how I even stumbled upon this one. I thought the concept of it was interesting though so here I am! It basically categorizes how people react to closeness within a relationship, and gives you an idea of why someone may come off as needy (anxious) and others as standoffish (avoidant). I think for some people this may seem obvious, but as someone who was pretty secure and dated an avoidant who in turn slowly made me anxious, this was eye-opening.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I feel exposed in a few ways! Great read about closeness issues that occur in relationships, and where they come from. Some of the explanations are a tiny bit simplistic at times, but I think that if the key messages in this book are reflected on, it can help couples work on intimacy-related insecurities, and better the relationship satisfaction from all parties involved. Also interesting is how common attitudes towards relationships - such as the idea that if you have a strong dependency on your partner, it makes you in some form "too needy", or deficient in some way - are given counterarguments with evidence rooted in evolution, biology, or psychology.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: While I didn't agree with everything in here, and the authors' approach was a bit too rigid/'here's the simple categorisation that answers all your problems' for me, I did find this a useful primer on adult attachment that doesn't read like a psych textbook (though is very much a self-help book which brings its own issues). It's accessible, clear and has good strategies and examples for improving secure attachment and practising effective communication, and doesn't demonise people with avoidant attachment traits in the way some similar books do.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Excellent book although not written from a Christian perspective. There was too much willingness to leave a marriage instead of working though things however I found the other parts to be incredibly helpful in learning about the attachment styles and the way they impact your relationships. This book will without a doubt improve my marriage as it gave me several practical ways to be a better communicator and also work towards secure attachment rather than anxious which will relieve a burden I've unknowingly put on my husband! So excited to apply what I learned in this book. Would definitely recommend to anyone interested in attachment theory.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was really helpful in breaking down attachment styles and giving examples of how they play out in relationships. My main problem with it is the lack of queer representation in any of the examples. Throughout the book there was only one very short story from a gay couple, and the research was pretty heteronormative, which is unsurprising but frustrating all the same. However, overall I learned a lot about attachment and what red flags to look for in dating. It was very insightful and informative!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached. This book was left many times on local library’s table. That’s how I had a look and got caught by the first pages. Like unconscious genetic drive in humans for choosing a partner. Then the book does a 90 degrees turn. It tries the reader to identify his own attachment trait. There are three common attachment styles in humans. According to the authors once you reckon your attachment personality there's not room for love to be left at chance. Not twin flames, not soul mates. You can engineer a relationship. Sad. Personaly I think if you wanna find love or keep it, just be yourself.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book helps you to understand different types of emotional attachment styles in your relationships. After reading it, you realize how crucial it was to know about the "attachment theory" earlier in your life! It helps you to understand your emotional needs and feelings, and confront your fears and confusion during any relationships before/after commitments. Moreover, it teaches you to 1) see the smoking-guns (critical signs) instead of ignoring them, 2) communicate your concerns effectively and respectfully, 3) understand your partner's or date's behaviour better, and 4) take over your unconscious activation/de-activation responses and reactions. As a result, there would be less chance to get drown in any drama or regret afterwards. It may also help you analyzing your past experiences in a rational and scientific manner so that you capture your take-home messages and move forward with a peaceful mind.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is such a useful book on relationships. It helped me recognize some of the patterns that I fall into in relationships, and it gave me a toolkit to move away from insecure attachment behaviors and towards secure behaviors. Plus, there's a great bibliography for further reading. I wish they would've addressed how cultural, ethnic, socioeconomic, and other factors play into attachment and relationships. It completely blew "The Five Love Languages" book out of the water. Though, it was also really heteronormative. I think they had one example of a possibly homosexual couple.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Oh yeah, confirmed anxious gal here. While I think there was definitely more in this for me, it did explain some thing about avoidant folk that helped me contextualize past (romantic and non) relationships. I did find the tips/anecdotes repetitive, the take home message really being to just be frank about your needs. However, I don’t think relationship dynamics are always this black/white and conflicts that’s easily resolved. In short, good notes, thought-provoking characters, and I am anxious (for now).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attachment literature seems to be growing, and this book gave me a great start to explore the topic more. I found the book very helpful, but I do think it's worth checking out the criticism of the book from the Podcast "Go Help Yourself." The criticism isn't extensive, but they do suggest there's an inherent value preference for secure over anxious and avoidant. While that preference, on paper, obviously makes sense, there are complicating factors that the podcast hosts Linke and Stinnett dig into more.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is great. I read The 5 Love Languages before and this is so so so much better. Insightful and chock full of useful information. Edit: I just read a review by someone with an avoidant attachement style and I have to say, that I now see the problem. I myself have an anxious attachment style, which made this really helpful to me, but I can see, that it might not be so, if you have an avoidant one. So while it was wonderful for me, it might not be for everyone. Also there is the issue with being extremely hetero normative, which is a shame.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Not quite my typical "so many good quotes and insights" variety. Rather it has one solid main idea (or rather, 3) and runs with the implications. I had heard all about the main concept before but there is a wide gap between "knowing about" something and being *thoroughly familiar. The bio explanations and category tests at the end of part 1 are particularly useful to really get a sense of each attachment style. I sure wish I would have read this earlier in life. Highly recommend for anyone not yet married or wanting to deepen intimacy with their partner.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is pretty short, accessibly written and overall a very good introduction to this framework for understanding yourself and potential partners/your own partner(s). I'll be totally honest, it overlooks a LOT of potential strains on relationships, and that's definitely a shortfall, but only so much can be accomplished in one book, so I don't think it's something that takes away what's good about it. I read this as a single person and found it very useful for getting a better read on folks in the early stages of exploring a relationship :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Cuốn sách được viết bởi các nhà tâm thần và thần kinh học, giúp giải mã sự tương tác trong các mối quan hệ bằng thuyết gắn bó. Dưới góc nhìn của thuyết gắn bó, một mối quan hệ có thể được trao cơ hội để chủ động trong việc tìm kiếm, giữ gìn và phát triển thay vì phó mặc cho sự may rủi. Cuốn sách còn phân tích và đưa ra cách giao tiếp hiệu quả và xử lí mâu thuẫn có thể áp dụng cho các kiểu gắn bó. Đây là cuốn khá mindblow giúp mình nhận ra hình mẫu của bản thân, và hiểu thêm về lí do của xu hướng hành động trong mối quan hệ giữa mình và những người khác.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 5/7. Honestly, this book got me good. I feel like I learned a ton about myself and my past relationships. Every time I thought of something else, the authors already addressed it on the next page. Will be forcing everyone I love to read this. I'm taking off a star/two points because this showed SUCH open disdain for avoidant attachment people (which fair tbh) to the point where I was like okay this isn't really helpful. Also, my GOD just embrace gender-neutral pronouns rather than constantly saying "his or her" or "s/he"!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Muy recomendado, sea cual sea la situación personal/emocional/afectiva en la que te encuentres. Detalla el apego y sus mecanismos, de forma teórica y práctica, algo que yo desconocía al nivel de profundidad que este libro expone. Quizás haya cosas muy evidentes o poco “útiles” para algunas personas -como algunas críticas manifiestan- pero he de decir que no viene mal que nos recuerden la importancia de ponernos en la piel del otro/a en una relación y dejar de mirar tanto nuestro ombligo. ¡Si tenéis oportunidad, leedlo!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book organised the types of relationships out in the world that happens between partners by classifying how humans behave in romantic relationships into three major types: Anxious, Avoidant & Secure. This book is a 5 star read. It will definitely add positively to one’s knowledge. The solutions & tools are easy to apply in life. Nothings is difficult about it. I would recommend this book to those who really want to find the right partner or wants to fix the relationship they are already in.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I wish I read this book years ago. Provides a lot of insights into relationships (not just romantic although that is the main theme) and how we engage and attach. As an anxious attachment type, I took a lot away from this that will be very helpful going forward and I wasn’t made to feel like something is wrong with me (like a lot of self help books can make you feel). I listened to this on audio so will get the book to go through it again and complete the exercises. I think everyone should read this.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was so interesting for someone who had no idea about attachment styles or anything like that. Being an anxious attachment style myself this book was extremely helpfully in explaining some of the things I need in a relationship and I may have known before but can now look for a lot better. I would recommend this book to anyone honestly and the writing style was easy to follow along with and the stories and examples in the book flowed very nicely. It’s funny most women I have spoken to over that last week already knew al lot of the stuff in this book, whereas virtually no men did. I guess that says a lot about our dating culture these days.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book! If you’ve seen me in the last two weeks, it’s guaranteed I talked about attachment theory with you. (Sorry btw). Attachment theory research is eye opening. It gives language to so many frustrating romantic tendencies I’ve either experienced myself or walked friends through. I encourage anyone to read this as a gateway to more self discovery about their relationships. Disclaimer: the authors are scientists, so they do such a bad job of being empathetic to anyone with dysfunctional attachment. I would read this with caution. And a reminder that attachment is a spectrum and growth is always possible.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think it was an okay read. Good introduction to the attachment theory. Maybe more workshops on how to look at things more securely could have been more helpful to me too. But overall a goodish read. Good thing to know attachment theory.. I am better informed now... More aware of my ways.. And what I want to be.. (maybe missing a lot on how - and that is my concern) Full disclosure: I think I'm an avoidant. In the book, I felt as if the anxious were given care and sympathy.. Secure were given respect for being amazing.. Where as the avoidants were given the cold shoulder.. Sed And guess what that does to us? We flip the table and just walk away.. Because it's easier for us that way.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: My psychiatrist recommended this book to me and I am so grateful she did. Knowing I tend toward anxious attachment and why gives me a much better framework to be able to work on not only my behavior, but also my thought life; OCD can be so hard, building a secure relationship with a secure partner feels like healing. The language was clear, accessible, and non-judgmental, and the advice and exercises were incredibly practical. I'm proud of my relationship, and the work I'm doing on myself. This book has given me tools and insight for both.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An unlikely book for me to pick up, but it was recommended by several people at a rather crucial time. Read it to understand past relationships, but ended up finding out a lot more about myself (maybe not so securely attached...). Would have liked for it to delve a little more into the genesis of anxious and avoidant attachment styles (beyond the influence of parents), but perhaps this is not the book for it. Undoubtedly oversimplifies some things, but it's a good intro and certainly has left me with a lot to think about going forward.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is easy to read and a solid introduction to adult attachment theory. It has a myraid of tools and activities I could see myself using personally and in my professional practice. As someone who tends towards an anxious attachment, I found this book validating and hopeful. However, I wonder how those with primarily avoidant attachment traits would feel reading this book and whether they'd feel seen and understood or critised. I think the books use of hierarchical and discrete language when discussing attachment styles is unhelpful. The reality is we're all a bit more nuanced than the discrete categories of attachment, and I think it's important to keep that in mind when reading. Sidebar: Although a problem in attachment literature in general and though the authors acknowledged it in forward, this book would have benefited from the exploration of diverse couples. Also, she/he could so easily be replaced with they, which would not only be more inclusive but easier to read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book should be handed out to everyone at about sixteen years of age. As we all unfortunately learned when Covid hit, we need our attachments with other human beings. This book clearly identifies when attachment styles don't connect with each other. Some of us have secure attachments. Some of us have anxious attachments and need lots of reassurance, and some of us have avoidant attachments and need to feel self-reliant. Guess which types often end up finding each other. This book helps you understand what's really at stake (intimacy). It gives you a clear plan of how to form more secure attachments and, sometimes, it helps you decide when to walk away.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I loved this book! Someone recommended it to me and I found it very interesting to learn about attachment styles, how people behave because of them and how to spot these behaviours. I do think there are some sections which are oversimplified or probably not good behave that way but it made me understand my own attachment style better but it also helped me understand my friends/previous people I’ve dated. Very insightful and would recommend everyone to read this as an introduction to attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: ⭐️⭐️⭐️ 2.75/5: This book was not as insightful for me as a psychotherapist but it can benefit others who do not have the psychological background into attachment based theory. I did enjoy the descriptions and narrative examples of anxious attachment and secure attachment. This book does make it seem that avoidants are bad/troubled people. Another critique is that there is no mention of dual anxiously attached couples and the nuanced dynamics of those types of relationships. I may still recommend this to clients who have no previous knowledge of attachment.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: "The positive messages become mixed once again with ambiguous ones and again you find yourself plunging down that roller-coaster. You now live in suspense, anticipating that next small remark or gesture that will reassure you. After living like this for a while, you start to do something interesting. You start to equate the anxiety, the preoccupation, the obsession, and those ever-so-short bursts of joy with love. What you're really doing is equating an activated attachment system with passion. "

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I have been putting off reading Attached for years and somehow read it in one sitting… I have always known about attachment theories but really feel like I have a deeper understanding now of how the amount of intimacy we crave affects our behaviours in relationships. This was super enlightening and I want to drop this book off at certain people’s houses to make them read and have a come to Jesus moment ⭐️ all in all, really interesting stuff! docking 1 ⭐️ for some of the antiquated examples used that are no longer relevant in 2024!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was my first foray into the concept of anxious and avoidant styles. I learned a lot, and found it insightful in many ways. However, I was looking for a few more examples of how each insecure type can work towards security, and how to work together when you have conflicting styles. I almost feel like reading this now gave me flashbacks to times where I was less secure and made me feel I would always stay who I was in the past, rather than confirming or encouraging the progress I have made.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: At first, I wasn't sure about this book because I was already familiar with the four attachment styles and don’t usually like labeling people, like with zodiac signs. But the book offers fresh insights with examples and practical solutions. Sometimes I’d read about one attachment style and it would resonate, but then another one would too. I realized that for me, it depends on the situation—different circumstances bring out different attachment traits. It's been helpful to understand how a partner or a date triggers certain attachment behaviors in me, and whether those reactions are healthy.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a book everyone should read once at least. It’s such an important knowledge for everyone. It’s must if you want to understand a part of human relationships and how to create and keep healthier ones. Specially if you have anxious attachment this is a really helpful guide to understand yourself and to know your needs and feel validated, and know what to do whit all these uncomfortable feelings that might arise when your anxious attachment gets triggered. Please give it a chance you’ll get really helpful advice to find good relationships, it has been a life changer book for me 🤩

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book called me out in more ways than one, it made me re-evaluate how I create relationships with romantic partners, friends, family. Before reading this book there were some features of my personality that I thought were just unique to me, and therefore unchangeable. Some of these personality features bothered me and got in the way of enjoying connecting to others. After reading this book I realise that I am not as unique as I thought and that is comforting in a way. I feel better about myself now and I recommend this book to anyone - regardless if single or in a relationship.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Goodreads rating: 3 stars My rating: 3.5 stars Overall, I think this book was pretty insightful and did make me think about the way I feel in relationships, both romantic and platonic. It opened my eyes up to not only my behavior, but other people’s behavior as well, which is something I have missed. I have previously felt that I had a hard time identifying the issues of the other person and solely focusing on the ones that I have myself. So it was really interesting to view it from an outsider perspective. I do wish though that they had more tips and best practice’s to become more secure in a relationship and went into my details about being an avoidant, rather than it just being bad.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I skimmed a couple of the reviews before picking this up - and I admit I dismissed a lot of the negative feedback as likely just coming from avoidants 😂 But after reading this as someone who leans more anxious.. I still have to say I think they WERE too hard on avoidants. While I do think they made some good points throughout and had good tips… It often felt like all problems boiled down to avoidant people being kinda shitty and unable to meet an anxious persons reasonable demands. I would argue relationship issues are, simply put, much more complex than this. Regardless, it was an okay read, just feels like it would be pretty unhelpful for avoidant leaning people.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book offers valuable insights, but it doesn't fully meet the scientific expectations suggested by the title "The New Science of Adult Attachment." I noticed that it primarily addresses the needs of anxious individuals and doesn't provide solutions for avoidant types—they do state that the anxious will have more gains, but the emotional needs of avoidants are not portrayed as valid or significant as those of the anxious. They also overlook securely attached people by only telling them to be cautious, not to lose their security. Wrong book title, I suggest.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5 stars from me. It gives insight into romantic relationships and strategies for resolving conflict. It doesn’t matter if you are secure, attached or avoidant- there are key takeaways for everybody. How well explored though is a different question. My takeaway is that secure relationships are based on being emotionally dependent on your partner, despite pop culture saying how we should be self-sufficient. It’s then when vulnerability is present and part of your independence is given away, that people create greatest bonds. Overall a tool for being more aware about your own relationship biases and observant of others. However at parts very generalised and too repetitive.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: DNF at page 120 I don’t take life advice from Zionists. Plus although I would consider myself an anxiously attached person, it was clear to me that the authors were very biased towards only trying to help this type of attachment style. The avoidant style was almost represented as the villain. Read all the other 1 or 2 star reviews and that’s pretty much my thoughts. I have read Anxiously Attached by Jessica Baum and really related to it and got a lot of benefit from it so I think there is something to be said for Attachment Theory. I’m just going to have to learn more from other sources, preferably ones who don’t support genocide and ethnic cleansing.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached was a really helpful read for understanding attachment styles and the science behind them. It was eye-opening to see why we sometimes get stuck in our heads or react more intensely when these styles are activated. The book also paints a clear picture of what a healthy relationship looks like—showing that while conflict is inevitable, there are skills you can use to handle it better by prioritizing both your needs and your partner’s. I especially appreciated how it breaks down disagreements and helps you recognize what’s really at play when emotions run high.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Every time I have to publish a book of this genre on my profile I get icky, but I need to use that audible subscription somehow.. Picked this one up since being in a LDR is harder than I thought... Quite informative, quite general. I like the idea of attachment mechanisms, and explaining certain behaviours via "activation/deactivation" terminology. It does bring light to important parts of a relationship, and as someone not very in touch with explaining/understanding my emotions, this is quite helpful. Other than that, I'm still a cynic when it comes to such topics. Putting people in boxes when it comes to love, and justifying your behaviour using therapy-speak makes me cringe.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was recommended by a few people. The first half felt quite difficult to get through. A lot of it was restating what I’ve learned on Instagram for the last 6 months hahahah. The second half was powerful. I had never been empowered with the words or concept I exhibited when I was demonstrating “protesting behavior” I definitely want to be an effective communicator for others but most importantly myself. I have dwindled my needs out of fear of upsetting my partner. I’ve hid behind not speaking up a truth for fear of upsetting them and then building up a resentment that’s not fair. I hate how much my happiness depends on feeling secure. I am working on that. But I also hate myself when I ignore my needs out of fear. It was amazing to hear that as a partnership enfolds, we are both expected to contribute / care about the other’s well being. Not be entirely responsible for it, but there’s contribution margin that matters. I’ve been led to believe that I’m the only one responsible for my happiness - and that’s contradictory to how I was raised. Friends can have opinions and recommend certain stuff. This whole “self care” age of avoidance and splurge is not what I prescribe to. And it was nice to read about influence others may have, and while it’s well intended, it’s not always best for me and my partner. At the end of the day, I’m responsible for my happiness. And I want all humans in my life to feel the sincerity behind my love and wish for their well being. While it’s heavy on the anxious attachment cycle - and spot on for so many personal challenges- it can be applied to working relationships, friendships, and powerful communication with those around you. Glad I crawled through the first half to hear the really good second half. It’s a 1.5 star first half and a 4 star second half. Great stories, love the research centered text, felt very informative.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Man I really wish I had read this while I was dating, I think it would have saved me some heartbreak! I can’t be too mad because I’m now married to someone whose secure attachment style was very apparent right off the bat and made me realize how many experiences I’ve had with insecure styles. There were a few chapters that didn’t pertain to me at all because neither I nor Nathan are avoidant so I just skipped them, but overall it helped me realize when I have an anxious attachment style and that being with someone who’s secure is helping me out of that in a lot of way. The part about effective communication, I think, is essential for everyone and I would also just recommend the whole book to everyone, single or married!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It is an eye-opening book. It took me a year to read because I often had to pause, reflect, and revisit my own experiences. Be prepared to put in real effort to understand your attachment style and to examine your past dating experiences with scrutiny. Reading the book alone does not solve anything without active work. What I loved about it is that it provides clear pointers and logical explanations for why we behave the way we do, and it reveals common pitfalls in partner selection in an understanding way. Hence, it shows that our emotional state is not an undecipherable black box.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: _Attached._ promises a clear roadmap for understanding relationships, but it often felt like the authors were shoehorning people into neat categories that don’t capture real life. Anxious, avoidant, secure—sure, maybe on paper, but love is messier than a formula. I think we all flow in and out of these categories to varying degrees and tailor our attachment styles to fit the relationships more than a set concrete pattern. Still, it made me pause and examine my own patterns and past relationships, even if the advice sometimes feels too tidy to be fully useful.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Took me almost a year to finish, but with a reading goal on the line, I didn’t mind the push to get it done. I went back and forth on how to rate this book. I found it very helpful in understanding my own attachment style, but that insight comes within the first 25% of the book. The remaining 75% would probably be more beneficial for someone who is single or in couples counseling, where both partners can actively work through scenarios in which their attachment styles show up in conflicts or sensitive areas.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: really well written and easy to understand guide on attachment research. beyond romantic bonds, understanding your own attachment style is useful to having your needs met in all close relationships (friends, family) as well as your ability to meet others needs. I also really liked how it talked about pop culture myths around relationship dynamics. Such as the myth of codependency: that it’s bad to rely on someone, when in reality our biological makeup is to regulate ourselves with our closest bond. Something else to note - it does talk about the avoidant attachment style, but it seems to focus more on navigating relationships if you have an anxious attachment style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I’m a secure person for the most part... I communicate properly and I don’t need too much attention. However, after having been in a relationship with a super avoidant and non committal person (he’s my husband ugh) I find myself adopting anxious behaviors. This book was excellent in explaining the differences and how to become more secure and adopt good communication strategies. I truly hope my husband reads this and decides to step it up or ship out as we are currently in limbo (a separation)!
