If I find myself back in the dating pool however, this book truly has helped me to see what I need to walk away from and now I’ll do it much more quickly so as not to waste time and energy on those who won’t be willing to love me properly!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I was surprised that this book turned out to be more interesting and helpful than I expected. It provides good info on attachment styles, identifying one's own and that of any potentially significant others as early as possible, and what to do about it. Very good, sensible and concrete suggestions based on attachment styles for people who are dating. That said, I would have liked to see more information on folks who are both avoidant and anxious, more elaboration on other attachment variances, and how, for example, something like narcissism fits in with attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: “Despite the importance we assign to our most intimate bonds, most of us still know very little about the science behind romantic relationships and allow ourselves all too often to be guided by misconceptions and myths.” If you have any interest in finding success in the romance department, I highly recommend you read this book. Two decades of research went into this detailed account of life, I hope it enlightens you as much as it did me.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is so clearly written. It presents as a helpful assessment and resource tool for identifying and changing attachment patterns within intimate relationships. I wanna shove a copy in everyone’s face and force-read it to them! So, yes. Pick up a copy. Read it. Make your friends read it. Make your partners read it. Make your families read it. Start talking about these relational patterns - how unmet needs play out in your own interactions, and how to better communicate core needs.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: God made the world perfect; perfect environment, perfect animals, perfect man. But even in a perfect world, it was not “good” that the man was alone. We were made for connection & interdependence. Some connect better than others. Are you avoidant? Anxious? Or secure? Just being aware goes along way toward forming healthy relationships, free from manipulative games or distancing boundaries. It’s okay to need someone. God said it was so.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: “In order to thrive and grow as human beings, we need a secure base from which to derive strength and comfort.” Lots to digest, and I found this remarkably insightful and profound. Wish I had read this sooner. Curious how rigorous the research is and would like to read a more academic slant on this topic (veers to a somewhat cheesy self-help tone at times and some of the examples are a little much).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book has some great information on how to identify patterns in relationships and some solutions on fixing them. I do think it was a little too generalizing and had no acknowledgement that not everyone fits into just one category. They do seem to favor the secure attachment, assure the anxious, and dismiss the avoidant. They do emphasize open communication which I do think is the basis of any good relationship, however, I also think they make it seem way too easy to do. I'd definitely recommend it to a client despite some of my disappointments in the book because I think overall the main point is great.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is a good introductory to attachment styles. It was the first place I learned about attachment in adults and I found it very easy to understand and grasp. My only complaint would be that it only offers help to anxious attachment styles. There are many avoidant and disorganized(anxious/avoidant) attached people that would like to shift their behaviours last and this book mainly focuses on anxiously attached people.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: DNF @45 I was excited about reading this book because I was looking for tips to go by in order to regulate my attachment system. However, I got disappointed and triggered doing so. As someone with an avoidant attachment style I felt invalidated and demonised. Damn! For a psychiatrist the author surely fails to perceive the impact of such a perspective. Anyways, the book managed to ruin my day and make me feel like a pure shit.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A freaking life saver and I wondered why I didn’t come across this book earlier. It could have saved me so many heartbreaks! Well, I’m so glad I picked up this book to read during the end of 2020 because 2020 is the year of tuning inwards and discovering myself. I believe in development science and attachment theory and how we communicate consciously can make or break our relationships. Thinking of buying a physical copy now to re-read when I need reminders

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this book does a very good job at engaging the reader to not only identify their attachment style, but embrace it, recognise potentially good/bad partners & use it to communicate their needs to the best of their ability. I thought there were some examples that were a bit unnecessary/ unrealistic at times. I would’ve liked a little more depth on how attachment styles can change from relationship to relationship but overall a really eye-opening book!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Amazing book I finished in record time! I was expecting a lot of scientific jargon and I was ready for slow-reading to be able to absorb all the information. The opposite happened. While the book is built on scientific research studies and explains relationships from a scientific point of view (be it biological or psychological), it's easy to read for anyone who has ever done some work on themselves (self development, coaching, therapy...). I recommend this book to all my mindful friends as it's gave me a lot! 👌

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A well articulated, basic description of attachment styles. I think if I hadn’t studied attachment, I would have found this book more beneficial. I did gain knowledge from reflecting more intimately on my attachment style and especially appreciated the parts of the book where they give you practical information regarding how your attachment style may impact relationships and how to navigate/change it. Lots of helpful lists of “dos and donts” as well.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: There are few books in my life that as I read them, I feel the trajectory of my life changing. This is one of those. Not every self-help book is helpful to every person, but this one read my mail and helped me look at relationships in an entirely new way. I would highly recommend it to anyone, but especially those who find themselves in the same situation again and again. There is hope for change!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: While there were points where I felt like the authors' division of adult attachment styles was a bit rigid, they had a lot of interesting insights and I do believe everyone would benefit greatly from knowing what their attachment style is and understanding what that means for their relationships. However, the book was too repetitive to be enjoyable all the way through. It could've worked just fine as a short collection of three essays, or maybe even one essay.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Really insightful read on different attachment styles that everyone should know about when pursuing personal relationships. Some of the points were a little vague, or the explanations sometimes too concise for the complexities of the psychology behind human attachment. However, I think there is a lot of merit to this area of psychology; it shows how past trauma and nurturing can affect your relationships later in life. A very interesting read— I definitely recommend.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Well written but I wish there were less examples and of the examples, there were a wider spectrum of relationships, not just a woman and a man in a romantic connection. I'm not big on locking in our identity to any sort of category which is why I appreciated how this idea is told. Less about identifying which attachment style you are and why, and more about how attachment style are displayed and how to move ourselves to practicing secureness.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I really enjoyed listening to this book. As a psychologist, I felt that the concepts were explained in digestible terms and that the book would be very helpful for many people. I loved how well the examples described individuals and relationships I have know throughout my life. In my personal life, this book was a great reminder of healthy communication strategies, even with secure attachment. I would highly recommend this book to anyone looking for a relationship, currently dating, or in a long term partnership who wants to improve both themselves and their connections.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Really wasn’t impressed with this. I guess I expected it to be one of those books about the topic and with lots of references to research, but really it was more of a “how to” for relationships for each type. Even at that though, it was seemingly quite juvenile with references to relational problems that I can’t imagine many immature adults having. Also like half the book was devoted to essentially saying “communicate your needs and feelings” and somehow turned that into 4 chapters. I don’t know. I wouldn’t recommend it unless you really struggle with an anxious attachment, otherwise not helpful or insightful.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
reviewer_name: a u d r e y ♥
review_body: A friend recommended this to me and I immediately bought it. It's the sort of book you should read, ASAP, if you love another human. It doesn't even have to be a romantic relationship, because after all, attachment theory also applies to family and friends. However, while the whole book is centered around research and personal experiences I felt it was lacking. It was all about "here's what you do if you have X attachment style" and "if you're not compatible with your romantic partner, that's a bummer. Find someone secure." Which, isn't practical considering secure attachment is rarer than rare. But overall it was a good read and gave plenty of insight into my own attachment theory (though quite little on how to improve) and I'll be recommending my husband read it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I’d recommend Attached if you’re a cis-hetero-monogamous looking for “the one” to take to your local Olive Garden. It’s a decent intro into the very basics of attachment theory, but there are better books out there. I would have appreciated more inclusive language in regards to gender and orientation. The author spoke in absolutes in regards to your attachment style and made it sound as though you’re largely set in your attachment style and that becoming secure is a rare occurrence (30% according to the book). Not enough depth in what influences the development of your style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was recommended to me by a therapist as a means to gain insight on identifying, understanding, and navigating attachment styles. The book is incredibly interesting and I found myself engrossed from the first page. They cite scientific research which I always appreciate and the language used is simple to read and understand. In terms of the content, I did find it to be oversimplified and overgeneralized at times. I felt like they implied that in relationships, you can pretty much predict the course and outcome based on the 3 attachment styles and their associated behavior however, it has been my personal experience that this is simply not the case. I think there's an oversight by implying that anxious, avoidant or secure is the entire personality when in reality anxious, avoidant or secure are elements of a personality and that other personality traits can impact the relationship. For example, someone anxious can be worried about their partner's ability to love them back but can also be strong in their stances and not worry about losing their partner because they might value their worth. So, as someone with an anxious/avoidant attachment style by definition, I don't feel capable or fully equipped after reading the book to handle situations as they predict. That being said, there were some really good elements of the book, including the chapter on effective communication and the initial chapters on the biology and chemistry of attachment. The main thing I took away was being able to identify which attachment style I related to the most (which I guess is the aim of the book anyways?). However, everything after; the handling of situations, compatibility prospects etc. is not as clear. All in all, a good read. There are lots of things to be learnt in the book and I would recommend it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: *4.2 A really gentle, informative, and practical introduction to attachment theory and healthy/secure relationships. The book avoids the wordiness that is kind of annoying in the psychology genre, and provides ample examples to illustrate the cases. I will most likely reread this in the future. One thing that can be improved on is being more ace-positive. Recommend to anyone interested in attachment theory and/or wants to have a better relationship!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5 stars. I enjoyed this book! It was a nice summary of attachment styles and how they impact relationships in adulthood. A little too self-helpy at times, but generally found it interesting to read, especially when discussing anxious and avoidant types and different research studies. Provided insight to why we engage in different behaviors - I think anyone single or in a relationship could find something useful from this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: За човек, който цял живот живее с тревожност, е толкова важно някой просто да му каже, че не откача. Книгата беше нещо такова за мен. Психологическо обяснение на тип поведение, реакции, които винаги съм смятала за абсурдни, за твърде емоционални, както и повечето хора ти казват. Явно не. И е такова облекчение. Да, не прави нещата по-лесни, но поне знаеш какво да промениш, знаеш, че главата ти е против теб, а не отношенията ти.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: twas fine! straightforward and good examples of real life couple scenarios. i think reading it on my phone made the experience a bit rough bc there a lot of tables and self-analysis sections that just didn’t translate well. i think some of it can be pretty self explanatory if you’ve tried to do the work on becoming secure, but there were reflective questions and scenarios that did give me food for thought.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book had some great points in explaining the three different types of styles in a person. Avoidant , secure and anxious attachment. It explained thoroughly how we all work together in this world and how each attachment type works in a relationship . I liked to hear the examples and stories of other couples and how they improved their relationship. As I went on though, it became boring and repetitive towards the last 70 pages and I had already got the message that they were trying to convey. Overall it was a good book but just a bit repetitive and boring

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: this book truly changed my perspective on relationships. throughout each chapter i learned about all the different kind of attachment styles people have and how to differentiate them. this book gives me confidence to find a secure partnership! i put this book down for awhile earlier this year but picked it back up last week i needed to finish. and im so happy i did! learned a lot about my past relationships and myself in order to find the right person for me!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A great introduction to attachment theory for those who are not yet aware of it. This book explains how childhood experiences can influence one’s attachment style during adulthood. Though the author is seemingly biased against those with avoidant attachment, this book is particularly reassuring and soothing for those who lean more towards anxious attachment, and those who categorise themselves as securely attached but have been a victim of becoming anxious by those who are avoidant.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Counselor recommendation; helpful in explaining different attachment characteristics, but I was expecting a more in depth explanation of where attachment styles stem from (family, etc.). The relationship examples and contrasts given were helpful(ish) but felt too specific to help drive their point that finding someone with a secure attachment style is what is most ideal. Does not provide too much information for avoidant types.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Book give a simple scheme to notice red flags while starting to meet someone, which is common sense basically. But it is worth it to remind it, in order to not waste energy in people who doesnt speak your same language. Other basic techniques, like efficient communication, avoiding protest behaviour, If you want or have a relationship, your own wellness is dependent importantly to your partners, be aware of that. (darwin approves) Best regards, a secure a bit anxious guy

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This should be mandatory pre-reading for relationships. The examples are super clear, the research has the most relatable content ever, and I said “omg same” every page of the book. I wish they elaborated a bit more on effective communication, but I understand why they didn’t; it'd probably be a book on its own. Also, I'd probably give it a 5-star review if I didn't know about most of the stuff in it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a very interesting read. My boyfriend and I decided to read this together and it has been great for deeper discussion about what we both need from each other :-) However, we found it to be somewhat redundant in some parts and I think the "avoidant" partner is written very stereotypically and a little off base but the "anxious" partner is spot on lol. I still think it's a pretty good and quick read that would be great for better communication with your partner!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Gives great information on attachment theory and how exactly it applies to romantic relationships. However it is very pessimistic about developing a secure attachment style in adulthood, without being in a romantic relationship. Makes it seem that you need a secure partner before you can begin any work on healing your attachment style. Lame, but I guess it is probably more helpful to people with an insecure attachment that are currently in a relationship.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I maybe buy it, helpful every two sentences out of a hundred but I already knew everything from Reddit and being neurotic + requires a lot of mental gymnastics to distill messy life into a science such as they propose Important model for people with very little self awareness but I think I’m above it basically, would be very useful for a lottttt of people to read tho or understand at a basic level

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I give this 2.5 stars cause I was ultimately disappointed in the way it presented attachment theory. I think it presents it as very black and white without all of the grey that is present. It reads as really biased against avoidant attachment theory as well. However I do think it gives good tools at strategies to work on gaining more security. Overall not my favorite approach to attachment but does have me wanting to learn more.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 4 stars is probably unjust, as this book is excellent. It suffered a bit from being an audiobook, making it hard to sit and ruminate on principles, to go back and cross reference, etc. So that’s on me, but it’s also a part of my experience. Also, while the content in here is excellent, it does leave out some things, such as disorganized attachment, which I would like to learn more about. Still, the strengths here massively outweigh the weaknesses. Very enlightening and I hope to be able to apply some of these principles in my own relationships (and not just romantic ones).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I couldn’t shut up about this book and have recommended it to way too many people. A really easy read and anyone that has ever been in any intimate relationship should be able to learn something new about the way they behave in relationships. Complex concepts broken down so people can easily identify behaviours they notice within themselves/others and tools to help work on how to work with that behaviour. Personal takeaways. 1. It’s a dating pool full of avoidants. This speaks for itself. 2. Gravitational Pull- The anxious/avoidant diad is such a simple concept but reading it feels like my current knowledge of this relationship now has a neat bow around it. 3. Still water runs deep’. A beautiful way to describe the secure attachment.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Bought this book years ago, and since I'm committed to reading everything I already own before buying any new books, I felt I should give this one another chance. It turned out to be a page-turner, despite being nonfiction. In my opinion, it's far more valuable than anything you'll ever read about love languages. The book offers great insights into different attachment styles, the clashes they can cause, and effective communication and conflict resolution tools. However, I would have preferred the communication section to be more detailed.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I highly recommend this book to anyone no matter your relationship status - single, dating, or married. I learned a lot about myself and feel like there are useful takeaways from this book to carry over into everyday life. This book offers clarity on why you may find yourself in certain dating patterns and how to identify problems AND solutions in your relationships. I imagine this book helps a lot of couples build a healthy foundation that can last a lifetime!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is terrible. Is there no accountability for anxious attached? The author specifically said it's ok to be needy and that you just need to find a secure person who can read your verbal AND nonverbal cues. Hell no. That's seriously so toxic. And would make a secure person turn into an avoidant. Like who wants to be with a person that needs CONSTANT validation and catering to? And how the authors bash avoidants. This book is just toxic. There's no compassion at all.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: While I did appreciate the underlying lessons of this book and gained some useful insights and perspectives, the portrayal of avoidant people seemed pretty negative and lacked sufficient explanation of and empathy for these people. The categorization of people seemed somewhat over- simplified, too. I still feel that the book is useful and worth a read, but it could be hurtful and discouraging for people who are avoidant.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I have a secure, leaning avoidant attachment style. The problem is I learned that in chapter 1 and took away little from the rest. This book is super redundant while being overly simplistic at the same time. Each anecdote felt like a lazy euphemistic piece of gossip If you are an anxiously attached person then this book might have some marginal value, otherwise it’s just common sense but in 300 pages

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An amazing book that I got to read in exactly right time. Having listened to plenty of podcasts and read some more about the attachment theory, this book is giving the best and most clear explanation about why and how we are attached to other people, as well as how to deal with it. The book made me view my relationship from a completely different perspective and brought some extra thoughts on how I myself can build a secure attachment in the future.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: My therapist recommended this book. It was my first intro into attachment theory, so the first chunk of the book had a lot of good info/insight into anxious attachment. This was helpful to feel seen and give more tools to understand thought processes. I did not find the quizzes, exercises or real life story examples to be helpful - they were either way too obvious or way to far fetched to be applicable to my life.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: So basically every anxiously attached person is a sweet angel baby who can do no harm in a relationship and every avoidant is the devil himself. Cool cool cool. Outside of the very prominent anti-avoidant and heterosexual bias (as well as some gender bias as well!! Women can be shitty too), this was a pretty interesting and mildly helpful read. I wish there was a way to go back in time and give 20 year old me a copy of this when it would have been more impactful, but at least I can be a better partner moving forward now.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I enjoyed this book but agree with other reviewers in that it gives the most sympathy to anxious attachment and does not give as much grace to avoidant attachment. It is also lacking substance after describing the types of attachment. I expected it to move into how to become more secure for anxious and avoidant types but it fell short. Overall I enjoyed it and it creates a nice foundational knowledge but it’s certainly missing something.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: came to the english seaside to work on my play and ended up spending the whole weekend reading this book… okay. it was very repetitive and it also gave me visceral anxiety while reading cause it was just repeating the fact that as someone who can be a bit anxiously attached i need to AVOID avoidants at all costs over and over again… okay. we will see if i heed this important advice. no promises… okay

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I was introduced to the theory of attachment a few years back and found this book to be incredibly helpful in understanding the theory as well as myself and past experiences. I recommend this book to anyone wanting to learn more about the theory, improve their relationships, or those looking for a relationship. It will help you to recognize healthy relationships, what you need, and how to communicate.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: “All happiness or unhappiness solely depends upon the quality of the object to which we are attached by love” - Spinoza --- This book is better than I expected. It shows how attachment theory could explain a lot about one’s patterns in both thinking and acting in a relationship, which the correctness can be confirmed by my own experience. Not only that it shows how harmful and hurtful it can be if you have an insecure attachment style (either anxious or avoidant), but the authors indicate in details how to correct and improve it, by (1) simply being aware of these patterns, and (2) by showing how a person with secure attachment style would behave (including mainly effective communication, but also other psychological tips and advice as well). Feeling much more confident to enjoy and maintain a long-term relationship after reading :D

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: THIS BOOK RUINED MY LIFE! My therapist read me to filth with this one and I am forcing the burden of this knowledge on everyone I know. Taylor is reading currently. Katey will be reading next. Caio also needs to read this book and so does Ian. We all have different colored highlighters for our thoughts so if you’d like to flip through and guess who is who lmk! If you’d like to join the queue also lmk!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I'm so glad I finally read this!! It was healing for me to read about the differing attachment styles and what they look like, specifically in romantic relationships. I want to encourage young adults, singles and everyone in some kind of relationship (newly dating, long term relationship and even married) to use this book as a navigating tool!! Attached gave clarity to my past and provided a smoother road for my future.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a good read! The breakdown of attachment styles and how to approach different situations was great. I enjoyed the diagram, the scenarios and interactive exercises. Attachment styles is something I’ve learned about previously so it was nice to learn more them. I enjoyed how they debunked or spoke more about an attachment style myth that is constantly being pushed. Something I would definitely recommend my partner to read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A very good read on a topic I honestly knew zero about. I think some of the solutions are a little rose colored glasses (just find someone secure), and I felt like it was a little skewed on content towards addressing issues with anxious types, with just a quick chapter or two about avoidant types. Those chapters seemed to mostly just be “be a better person” in so many words. All that being said, I still enjoyed it, and felt like I learned a ton about something I knew nothing about.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Read this for my September curriculum which was focused on communication. As a psychology minor, the first half of this book, which focused on the three attachment styles, was nothing life changing for me. The second half, which focused more on communication and how each attachment style communicates, was much more interesting to me. I also wish I read this book in my early 20’s as it would have led me to make less dumb mistakes when it came to my relationships 😂

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I enjoyed this one. I liked how it used real examples of couples to explain the different attachment styles, it made everything so much easier to understand and relate to. I definitely fall more on the anxious side, so it was super helpful to see how anxious people interact with avoidant and secure partners. I found myself comparing those patterns to my past and current situations, and it honestly gave me a lot of clarity about why I react the way I do in relationships. Such a good read for anyone who wants to understand themselves and their partners better.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Zapravo sam pročitala hrvatskog izdavača Puls. Ako vas zanima ovakva tematika (veze, psihologija, odnosi) ovo je nesto sasvim drugačije od svih drugih knjiga na tu temu. Nije isprazno, logično je i poučno. Samospoznajno, ali na drugačiji način u moru ovog žanra. Za teze iz ove knjige nisam nikad do sada čula, a zapravo mislim da sam knjigu trebala pročitati još davno...kao tinejđerka, da mi ju je netko preporučio. Kako nije i kako sam na nju naišla sasvim - evo, moja preporuka!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is a great read for someone wanting to learn about attachment styles and how it interlaces in personal relationships. I think I would have rated this higher if I didn’t already learn on my own (in excess) about the various attachment styles prior, but I liked how they provided studies, and real life examples that explained how it’s not a “one size fits all” fix/scenario. It makes it more real. I think everyone can benefit from reading this book, as it makes you reflect on your own emotional behaviors within relationships, and how to understand your partner better

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Wow this was really eye opening for me! I have an anxious avoidant attachment style you know one of the lucky 4% and having always had difficulty in communication in relationships I see why now! I’m going to put this book into practice and believe it’s a really important read…. I might even add it to my essential reading. I listened to the audio book which I found easier to digest the information!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3.5⭐️ I thought i had learnt everything i needed to before or during the first half of the book. well... turns out i was to learn more along the way. Nice book to understand relationships better... rather why people act the way they do.... putting yourself in other people's shoes... but most importantly knowing yourself better.... and don't we all love this knowing ourselves better..? I loved it!!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very insightful. I found it mildly boring but that’s probably because I kind of knew a lot of it beforehand. It’s good as a work book and/or a book to refer back to when dealing with different attachment styles because each chapter and section can be read without the one before it. It’s like a relationship guide book. If god is real he hates anxiously attached people. Whyyy would he make them most attracted to avoidants. Asshole.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I absolutely loved this book. The examples were relatable and very easy to understand. It was refreshing and interesting to see common miss-understandings from another perspective other than complete failure and how to better handle those situations in the future based on your attachment type. The book also highlights the positive aspects of negative traits and how to reframe them into something useful to help you grow. 10/10 recommendation.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is a good read for anxious people who need a lil help talking through their insecurities with their partner (meeee), especially during conflict (very Me), but the epilogue is literally about 500 Days of Summer so there’s that. Also I’m 95% sure all of the sample couples were hetero which is real weird to read in the year of our lord 2018.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Discover your Attachment - Anxious, Avoidant, or Secure. Truly gained ALOT of insight with my own attachment. You are learning so many different ways to handle a situation in your relationship, & most importantly avoid a relationship as well. You also can learn your partner attachment & discover them on a whole new level from within. Definitely recommend for dating, & married couples to read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Wow, wow, wow! What an amazing and insightful read this was! I absolutely encourage any and everyone to read this book. Whether you’re single, in a relationship, engaged or married. It’ll serve as guide to help you better understand yourself, your past relationships, your current relationship and future relationship. I learned so much. Strongly recommend!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I never read self-help books but it was highly recommended by so many intelligent people, that I had to check it out. And I’m glad I did. It is very interesting. I’ve learnt so much about myself, my partner, friends and family members. I better understand my emotions and my partners feelings and it’s a very useful knowledge to have to lead a happy love life. Everybody should read this book, whether you are single or in a relationship.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was SO helpful.... I like that it reframed being anxiously attached as something neutral rather than inherently negative. And I finally understand why le ex and I didn’t work out (le anxious avoidant trap) and FINALLY genuinely feel like I am getting over him. Whoever I date next is reading this book!!! 4 stars for lack of gender and racial diversity

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: i think everyone in a relationship should learn about attachment theory. it really helps you understand the motivation behind different behaviors and gives you the power to change. as someone with a tendency towards anxious attachment, the authors really normalize it as an attachment style and explain it with a growth mindset.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Ogólnie jest to poradnik napisany w tym typowym poradnikowym stylu. Ale temat który porusza - rodzaje przywiązania - to poważne zagadnienie z zakresu psychologii, poparte wieloma badaniami. Cieszę się że je poznałam, bo uważam że przyda mi się nie tylko w związku romantycznym ale też w relacjach z rodziną i przyjaciółmi. Polecam :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very biased. If you're an anxious attachment style you will probably enjoy the book but it's not meant to offer any support nor advice to those with avoidant attachment styles. The authors encourage people to embrace their attachment needs, but only if they are anxious, if you're avoidant then you're a broken individual and the antagonist of relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I would argue attachment falls more on a spectrum than the authors seem to allude to with their cut and dry categories, but overall I appreciate their combining research, case studies, and experience to show how attachment plays out in relationships, and the practical suggestions and exercises provided to recognize, communicate, and meet intimacy needs.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: پایان کتاب عزیزم 🫠 امیدوارم برام خوش شانسی بیاره :))) خیلی کتاب خوبی بود یه کتاب روانشناسی مناسب برای اشخاصی که می خوان بیشتر در مورد سبک های دلبستگی اطلاعات داشته باشند اینکه دو نفر با دو سبک دلبستگی اضطرابی و اجتنابی و یا حتی ایمن چطور می تونند یک رابطه ایمن داشته باشند راضی بودم کلی نکته جدید یاد گرفتم خیلی خفن بود :) امیدوارم کتاب های بیشتری از این مدل بخونم 1404/10/10 22/19 %69:)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is such a relevant book for today's world. Specifically when navigating the world of dating and getting to know a partner. Since this book gives us the readers the basic tools to recognize our attachment style, it is a useful and simple way of knowing yourself. Thus, knowing what your emotional needs and your reaction to them says about your way of relating to people. I found the secure attachment sections of this book particullarly helpful because it is very straightforward about what it means to "act secure" in an emotional bond. It speaks truth in a very simple way and easy to understand, not wandering on unnecessary details. Overall, it's a very easy read, and full of sense. It was very useful to gain insight on my own patterns and responses in diverse situations throughout my life. I would definitely recommend it to my friends in relationships of any sort, which means anyone . . .

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I almost stopped listening to this in the first half hour, because it sounded like the worst of all possible pop-psych books, where it's mostly a sales-pitch for how this wonderful new science will solve all of your problems. I'd heard things about attachment parenting, most of which make me roll my eyes and/or fume about unrealistic perfectionists who tell you with a straight face how sacrificing 100% of yourself for your squalling infant will eventually be rewarded with unparalleled joy. So: skeptical. But I kept listening, and as it turned out, there were some useful tidbits in this book. The first tidbit may fall into the "no duh" category. People are happier and more secure when they're emotionally bonded with someone who looks out for their well being. The book further divides people into one of three categories: secure, avoidant, or anxious. You either can balance out and communicate your needs with a partner, you're afraid of getting too close and losing your identity, or you are terrified of losing the attachment you have with another person. So I took the test, and of course tested certain people, and found out that I am mostly secure but somewhat avoidant, and he is mostly secure but somewhat anxious. But of course I also have avoidant characteristics, and he has anxious characteristics, which kind of proves (no duh) that people are complicated. I do think it was useful in giving me some terms to describe traits I've seen in other people. Like, you know how there's always a couple where one (usually she) is always throwing tantrums because the other partner (usually he) doesn't return phone calls? Or when people play games because they're testing the other person's commitment? I've seen this relationship play out over and over and over again on TV and movies, and even with some people I know, but I've never been half of one. Apparently, avoidant people are a very common pairing with anxious people. I missed why this was so. I've seen it's so, but I missed

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: absolutely 5 stars ★ ⋆.ೃ࿔*:･ "if you want to take the road to independence and happiness, find the right person to depend on and travel down it with that person." this book was not only super informative but also very digestible and made the science behind the attachment styles accessible to everyone. i loved how they used countless real life examples of couples with different attachment styles and how their compromises and arguments could be analyzed using the ideas of attachment theory. this book provided the attachment style questionnaire so you can read through and truly learn about yourself and your relationships, as well as had many diagrams and activities to dive deeper into your understanding of yours and others attachment styles. this is an absolute must for anyone interested in the psychology of relationships and love!! for anxious people like myself it provides sooo many different ways of correcting anxious behaviours to become more secure in relationships and how to avoid people who won't adhere to your needs. you don't even have to be into non-fiction or psychology to enjoy this, it's just so addictive to learn about yourself and why you do certain things unconsciously. lastly, i especially love how this book breaks the stereotypes of modern advice on love such as having to be independent, confident, and hard to get. humans are social creatures and our biological makeup is the reason we feel such deep emotional connections to other people. learning that it's completely normal and encouraged to be dependent on others is so reassuring. don't settle for someone who undermines you for being dependent and clingy!! ⋆.ೃ࿔*:･ "most people are only as needy as their unmet needs." ⋆.ೃ࿔*:･ "our culture encourages you to believe that many of your needs are illegitimate. but whether they are legitimate or not for someone else is besides the point. they are essential for your happiness, and that is what's important."

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book is marketed as groundbreaking and based on new scientific findings about adult attachment. This naturally has raised my expectations and curiosity to get acquainted with these findings. Unfortunately, most of the statements in the book are backed up with the same old John Bowlby's experiments with children and his theory which was formulated roughly speaking in 70s. Of course, I can not argue, the author presents new research on adults. However, those researches are not extensive enough and are scattered that you would be able to make such conclusions and practical implications the author suggests in the book. The book gives many examples of real life situations in order to explain the statements of attachment theory. Which is great for someone who does not have a degree in psychology and wants to understand the basics of the theory. Though, some of the examples were vaguely related and not quite the right examples to prove the point. When I was reading the book, I was actually concerned, how this book will be understood by people who do not have right education in order to discern what might hold as a true and what is just speculation. Therefore, I see that this book will do more harm than good in general and truly do not recommend reading it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Such a helpful and informative read! This book provides really good tools for not only understanding yourself, but understanding others in romantic relationships. I know I personally struggle with certain aspects of relationships, and I feel like I learned a lot about why that could be the case, and things I could work on going forward. I would love to read a book like this that focuses on more of a friendship lens, since I think that would be super helpful as well, but a lot of what they talk about for romantic relationships could be adjusted and applied in other relationships as well. As a whole, this book was a good introduction to attachment theory as applied to romantic relationships, but there were a couple things that they missed. First, it was almost exclusively from a heteronormative lens, so it would be interesting to read a book that was more inclusive of other types of relationships. Second, I wish they included more on disorganized attachment (I know it’s the most rare style, but I feel like the authors would have such insightful advice for folks with that attachment). Overall, though, this was great! I definitely think attachment theory is something everyone could benefit from learning about.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: tough day to be an avoidant

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I had quite an interesting and fulfilling journey with this book over almost 7 months. It assissted me in analysing and unloking many attachment and communication issues both in my past relationships and my current one. I navigated a new path of self discovery, acceptance and development, and i am very grateful for the person who recommended it to me. Despite the ugly book cover, some over simplified parts, and the only heterosexual assumptions/language across the book, i enjoyed and benefited from the analysis and tips it presents. I treat this book as a working book, so i keep a copy close to me and reread some parts when in need, it helps soothing me as i reflect calmly on what happened/is happening. I recommend this book to anyone who had suffered/is suffering relationship issues especially those connected to communication and insecurity. If it doesn't help save your relationship, it will help you understand some of what happened and walk you on the happiness road again. A final thought and advice: Never undermine your partner's needs, and never underestimate the importance of effective communication.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is everything you'd want a self help book to be: well-written and scientifically sound, with clear explanations of concepts, and sprinkled with many examples along the way. It even has exercises. Moreover, it does not let you depend your understanding of a concept on one example, and gives you at least two for each. I recognize myself as an ex-anxiously attached person turned securely attached, and my own former and current behavior is reflected back to me loud and clear in the many examples. I now have the explicit tools to consistently react more securely to my partner, without falling back unknowingly into my previous protest behavior. What I used to label as "irrational behavior" on my side, I can now see for what it is (unhelpful protest behavior), therefore aiding me to react in a secure way more consistently in the future. That has always been my goal, but now I have the vocabulary and conceptual ideas to talk to myself about it. This book has been very helpful and clarifying.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Loved it! Insightful and helpful. BUT, I’m acknowledging that the book worships/victimizes the anxious and demonizes the avoidant, so it likely was a more pleasant read for me than for others (🤪🤪🤪). Filtered thoughts: -I don’t buy it that everyone fits squarely into one of the three categories—the authors never acknowledged that someone might be one type in one relationship and another type in another? -Felt a little too simplistic. Attachment theory & its associated feelings/behaviors are one part of the puzzle—there are other factors at play that influence a relationship -This book was incredibly redundant, could have been half as long Unfiltered thoughts: -50% of people are secure!?! Who???? I know 2 maybe -Book says an equal amount of men/women are secure/avoidant/anxious I DONT BELIEVE IT as 95% of the men I know are deeply avoidant (if you’ve gotten this far in my review you are likely a woman anyway and won’t be offended xoxo)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A useful and accessible book for everyone to read. It definitely feels like it would be more affirming and helpful for those with anxious attachment than those with avoidant attachment, who were portrayed somewhat negatively and unsympathetically in this book. While the authors really showed deep empathy and got into the heads/psychologies of those with anxious attachment, they unfortunately did not do the same with avoidants. This book also conflates dismissive avoidant attachment with avoidant attachment, neglecting the nuance between fearful/disorganized vs. dismissive avoidant attachment. Nonetheless, I think it was very helpful in understanding what secure mindsets and behaviors actually look like and the importance of mutual security in relationships. It is also ultimately quite validating and encourages us to be more gentle and patient with ourselves and our instinctive feelings/reactions/behaviors, even if they do hurt ourselves/others.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book speaks in broad generalities that harm everyone. It argues: if you're secure, you're a golden god; if you're anxious, that's fine just say what you need; if you're avoidant, stop stringing people along. In the anxious sections there is no mention of anxiety disorders, despite the fact that many of the stories we're told sound like they qualify. In the avoidant sections there's no talk of different levels of commitment. Not everyone is looking for forever. A lot of the avoidant people just sound like they're not that into the person they're dating. That doesn't make them avoidant. The book is so biased toward anxious people, it's kind of shocking this book was published at all. Why not just write a book that soothes anxious people? I think there's plenty to attachment theory. Unfortunately this book is not a good representation of it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: "... Relationships should not be left to chance." Read this book, whether you're secure, anxious or avoident. I've always been curious about why certain things keep happening in my life, over and over again, in all kind of relationships, family, friends or romantic. This book gave me the glance I needed to dig deeper from now on, it explains in a very simple way what kind of attachment one or one's partner can have and gives some vey logical advice to make things better. So yeah, if you're curious or like everyone who read this book, you kind of struggle, pick this one up. Because after all "Relationships are one of the most rewarding of human experiences, above and beyond other gifts that life has to offer" and you and your loved ones deserve a better shot at it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This felt like it took forever for me to read! I'm really glad it provided good insights to the friend who recommended it to me, it just wasn't for me. The attachment styles and their descriptions seemed kind of oversimplified and the examples were repetitive. There was a clear bias toward the anxious attachment style over the avoidant, which wasn't as fleshed out imo. This was too bad because it seemed to take out some of the complexity of different relationships. Ultimately I'm always kind of suspicious of anything lumping people into clearly defined categories of personality/behavior and this didn't change my mind about that.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: incredibly useful information on how attachment styles can impact our relationships, and ways to become more secure in our attachments! one of the main shortcomings is that every relationship problem ends up being attributed to differences in attachment styles, even when some of the examples show good ol’ fashioned misogyny, so I wonder about how the authors might account for oppressive behavior in interpersonal relationships, even in people who might otherwise have a secure attachment style. the book also makes the assumption of monogamous / heteronormative relationships, so requires some translating for people who don’t fit into those relationship styles / structures.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An important read about relationship patterns and how we can improve our connections. This book helped me to better understand attachment styles, how certain people respond to conflict, and the science behind it. It's written in an easy to understand manner. I gave it a four because I think in some ways it's oversimplified and doesn't take other mental health issues, like trauma, into consideration of how we attach. I love that it has exercises in the back and I think it could be helpful to use with my clients.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: And I thought I could go through life with a shallow knowledge of attachment styles??? This book is so insightful and practical. It also is very accessible and thorough in its examples. I am excited to now psychoanalyze everyone I meet hehehe. But for real this book would be beneficial for all people (single or in a relationship)!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book starts out fairly strong with good explanations for the 3 attachment types, but it doesn't really talk about the anxious-avoidant type. The advice towards of the end of the book falls flat and isn't very actionable/useful. An interesting read to get you started thinking about the psychology of relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is honestly a super practical book I wish I had read years ago! I had to read this for my internship but ended up gleaning so many nuggets of things that have helped grow my marriage and helped me address the anxious attachment that I’ve always known I had! Great read for all to help strengthen their relationships!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The best relationship book I've ever read. I've never felt more seen by a book in my entire life. I feel like I've been looking for this book for a decade. Read it! Plus its not super long so not a huge investment if you disagree :)

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
