book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The kind of book you’d recommend to all your friends! You get to learn a lot about yourself and how to navigate relationships. Also makes you go if only I knew this before…

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: i dont have an avoidant attachment style i just hate needy babies.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Prob should have read this 10 years ago.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Tldr: just read the Wikipedia article on attachment theory

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It’s actually crazy how well this book described the relationships of so many people I know. I really appreciated the insight this book gave, it definitely helped me feel better about stupid situations and made me feel much more sane and rational! Definitely a good book if you’ve ever been played by an avoidant. While this book does offer a lot of good information on attachments styles, I really wish it discussed attachment in areas other than your romantic and maternal relationships. I can definitely see how the scenarios presented resemble relationships with lots of other people in my life, but it is a book aimed at providing dating advice after all. I also wish it looked more into how certain people bring out specific attachment styles from you. I act much more secure around secure people, and anxious around avoidants but the book seems to act like we all just have one attachment style at a time. One of my biggest gripes is the authors almost seem to glorify an anxious attachment style, even above a secure one. So much of the book is focused on reassuring anxious people about how there’s nothing wrong with them, and all their needs will be fixed if they date a secure person. It seems clear that anxious attachers would benefit from going to therapy and working on becoming more secure before dating, instead of relying on finding an already secure person to somehow save them. The book is very clear in stating avoidants need therapy to heal their issues, and I just don’t get why it didn’t say this same message to anxious people. If you’re insecure in any way, it would be beneficial to work on that before dating! The book is not the most empathetic towards avoidants. This attachment style is caused by bad experiences so it would’ve been nice for the authors to acknowledge where this comes from instead of just putting them down, although they’re probably sick of all their clients being emotionally destroyed by avoidant people. My last piece of criticism is not enough t

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I know, I know--it's basically a relationship self-help book. I didn't seek it out, though; one of my coworkers happens to be an ex-professor of psychology, and the topic is a shared interest. We recently discussed The Invisible Gorilla: And Other Ways Our Intuitions Deceive Us and the next day he brought this in and said that he found some value in it, so he was lending it to me. Proper review forthcoming. ********* Final review : 1.5 stars. As interesting as the avoidant/secure/anxious model is, I’m skeptical that people can not only be a.) neatly sorted into three categories and b.) that these categories break down (even roughly) to 25%, 50%, and 25%. The authors give a throwaway mention to a fourth type, the supposedly-rare Anxious-Avoidant, but I’ve certainly met enough people who might be known to say “I hate you, you are suffocating me! Wait, please don’t leave me!” that I don’t think that’s as rare as they say (certainly higher than 0%...). The authors pay lip service to the idea that these aren’t strict labels, and that they’re “stable but plastic,” but the entire book seems directed at people who do neatly fit these labels (as opposed to the more-likely spectrum that exists). There's a lot of speculation and not a lot of citation. There’s also advice on how to “diffuse” (sic) a stressful situation (as opposed to defuse) and while I’d ordinarily look past nitpicky grammar issues, there’s really no excuse for this one, since it’s what the book is supposed to be about. The authors are supposed to be experts on defusing relationship issues and they can’t even pick the right version of diffuse/defuse to use in their book? That frustrated me more than it probably should have. It’s a neat concept, though, which I suppose is useful in its own way. Some of the content (such as an actual section called “Why Use Effective Communication?”) seemed a bit unnecessary. The purported solutions to example issues seemed kind of obvious to me, but then again, I am approaching

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Easy 5 stars. Throughout this book, I just kept thinking to myself that I've stumbled upon a gold mine. I wish I'd read this book sooner, it just explains so much and although I haven't applied it in the real world yet, I can see how it makes perfect sense. This has to be the most informative and gripping psychology self-help book I've ever read; I just devoured it in less than a week and I'm glad I'm ending the year with such a great read. Definitely adding it to my favorites. I believe attachment theory needs to be taught in schools, and it needs to be discussed more in mainstream media not only because it explains so much about relationships but also because it helped me understand myself better by knowing my attachment style. I think I'll need to get back to this book in the future and reread certain parts or maybe all of it xD. I love how to the point it is, how easy it is to understand and follow along and most importantly how relatable it is and the numerous AHA! moments when I finally understood why I felt or acted in certain ways in the context of past relationships or why a partner did this or that. Of course as the author points out, for secure individuals, many parts of this book might seem obvious like duh! However it will help them immensely if they want to better understand their anxious or avoidant partner. For insecures though, most of it serves as an eye-opener; it explains how attachment theory applies to relationships, helps you recognize your attachment style as well as that of others so you can pick a partner suitable for you and your needs, in addition it serves as a practical workbook for identifying and solving relationship issues in a secure way that brings couples closer instead of creating rifts between them. Furthermore it equips you with the basic tools necessary to transform your relationships to a more secure style; which is why I think every single person out there should read this book at least once.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was such a revelation for me! Before reading it, I was only slightly familiar with attachment theory but after reading it, I can see how attachment theory applies to relationships. Whether you're anxious, secure or avoidant, this helps to explain so many relationship issues people have. Attachment really helped shed a lot of light on the issues in my relationships. I see now that people have different capacities for intimacy. Some people have a need and desire to be close and intimate and others do not. These needs aren't bad but the authors explain why it is so important for people to be with other people who can fulfill their intimacy needs and to leave relationships where those needs aren't being met. I love that authors implore readers to be direct about their needs and not to ignore or dismiss them (for instance, anxious types have to accept that they want closeness, intimacy and warmth in their relationships and not see this as being "needy" or "clingy"). I would definitely suggest this book to people who are just starting or not yet in a relationship because I really think it will help to avoid relationship pitfalls and be clear about what you expect from a relationship. I think this book can even be helpful for people already in relationships. It will definitely provide some clarity to why you and your partner act the way you do. The only critique I have is that I don't think the authors really did enough to address what avoidants should do to have successful relationships. The tips they suggested seemed a bit far fetched because they basically involved avoidants becoming more close to their partners (which is what they don't want to do!). Other than that, I really think this is a wonderful book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An excellent, insightful overview of attachment theory and its practical implications on our relationships with others. I found the book’s discussion of and emphasis on effective communication strategies to be particularly useful. I think anyone who is interested in fostering emotionally healthy, well-adjusted connections with others could benefit from reading this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Interesting and illuminating. It is by no means the ultimate secret to relationships or self-actualization, but it does a damn good job demystifying some of the long-held beliefs. Fun colloquial language without leaving out the scientific references (although some parts were too grocery store magazine article-y for my tastes). I think there is something useful here for everyone.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was so eye opening! I learned a lot about myself, my relationship needs and the potential needs of others. It was enlightening to dive into the “why” behind certain behavior patterns in romantic partnerships. Definitely recommend this book for anyone trying to find a secure partner while remaining authentic to him or herself.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: if i could give this book 6 stars, i would. this was an amazing, insightful and reflective read. it opened my eyes to different attachment styles that we all have, how they come together, the conflicts that arise, and how to work with it. most of all though, i learnt so much about myself. i loved this book.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Very heteronormative in its ideas of monogamy (and a queer relationship is mentioned literally ONCE in 300 pages), plus I feel like it was very much directed towards people with anxious attachment (*ahem*), but I still found it rather insightful into my own tendencies in romantic scenarios — and ultimately what/why things have gone wrong for me.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: as a 21 yr old with 0 prior relationship experience, this book has saved my live on so many occasions altho relationships are complex and no 2 attachments are the same, i haven't found a fear/behaviour/thought pattern that wasn't described in the book. i'm amazed how these guys have been able to break down all of these so succinctly. a must read imo

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a great book because it gave me insight on attachment styles which I had no idea existed. The best part about the book was the evaluation within the book. I think part of solving the problem is understanding where you stand on the spectrum and having concrete data to evaluate your case. It wasn't just theoretical because it told us where we stand. A very insightful read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Gosh I wish I had read this earlier, and it made me realize how much I overthink relationships. It’s more simple and straight forward than I want to believe. This book helped me think about 1) what do I want 2) trust my gut; give people a chance and rule out people early 3) wear your heart on your sleeve 4) communicate effectively 5) believe in abundance.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A great read! I learned so much from this book! It has so much information on a topic that I wish was discussed more! It’s fascinating to know what type of attachment style we fall under and how to use the tools in the book to identify others and understand why people respond the way that they do in relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: 3,5. insanlari net olarak sinirlandirmak zor oldugundan ve kosullara gore endiseler/tavirlar cok farklilik gostereceginden basta on yargilarim vardi ama kitap nesnel bir bicimde gercekten baglanmalar ve bu baglanmalardan kaynaklanan iliskilerdeki yaklasimlara yonelik arastirmalari ve cikarimlari sunuyor. kitapla okuyucu arasinda icindeki gorus soran ve cikarima iten bolumler sebebiyle interaktif bi iliski olusuyor. ben sans verilmesi gerektigini dusunuyorum cunku hepimizin bildigi gibi insan sosyal bir varlik ve kurdugumuz baglar, bizim icin kiymetsiz sandigimiz anlarda bile, cok kiymetli; kisiligimizi de hayatimiza bakisimizi da etkiliyor. oturup kendi uzerimden dusunup cikarim yapmak ve cevremi de degerlendirip daha iyi anlamaya calismak hostu.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Das Buch hat mich stark dazu angeregt, mich mit mir selber auseinander zu setzen und gewisse Dinge aus einem anderen Blickwinkel zu betrachten. Mich überzeugt, dass das Buch auf wissenschaftlichen Hintergründen basiert. Mit einigen Aufgaben / Inhalten konnte ich mich zwar nicht identifizieren, trotzdem hat mich das Buch überzeugt, weil es in mir so viel ausgelöst hat.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An absolutely amazing book! Easily written and filled to the brim with interesting ideas. If you've ever struggled with unsatisfactory relationships or want to learn more about possible problems in relationships, then I think this could be an eye opener. It gives tips for people who are still dating but also for people in long term relationships. Want to buy this book for all my friends!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: an insightful deconstruction of why certain romantic relationships fail while others succeed; and how to maximize one’s satisfaction in any romantic relationship. takes a very objective and no-nonsense pov on the techniques and skills one needs to develop in order to ensure long lasting, secure love.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is perfect for identifying behaviors in interpersonal relationships. It was great reading the personal examples and the bulleted behaviors and characteristics to help us identify the toxic traits we may display. I read this book at a perfect time in my life. I was able to identify someone with an avoidant attachment style and pivot early to prevent heartache.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Interesting perspective on adult attachment theory. I had some self help book critiques yet it did a good job at summarizing the differences between the attachment types, ways to identify them in yourself, and ideas to alter intimacy patterns so our needs can be met. I’d recommend first 30 pages as most interesting.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This shit will rock your world. Took me a while to read but I learned so much about myself and my behaviors - it shook me to my core. Gives you perspective as to how you value intimacy and closeness in a relationship and offers tips on ways to take advantage of that. Takeaway? Your needs are legitimate no matter what they are.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: my favorite types of media are those that give you a vocabulary to discuss things you feel so deeply you sometimes can’t give them a voice. i started this book at a really rough point in my life and i finished it in a much better place. this book brought a scientific view to something most of us view as abstract, our relationships with others. 10/10 recommend for anyone who wants a more secure relationship with the world around them.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I only finished this because it was so bad it became entertaining again I'm spoiled by reading polysecure first but this is so comically hetero- and mononormative it's hard to believe it was written in the 2010s. the way misogyny and abuse are attributed to (avoidant) attachment? yikes. quick summary: if you're anxiously attached, you're a victim, if you're avoidantly attached you're a monster and if your attachment is anxious-avoidant you are statistically irrelevant and shall never be mentioned again. attachment theory is interesting but this is not it.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was extremely well written. I loved that it partnered extensive research with easy to understand scenarios. The book, however, was extremely dense and difficult to read all the way through. In the future, I feel as though I’d skim through it, using the book more as a quick reference than a fun read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I read this book as a therapist to help me provide insight to clients who are having relationship issues. It was very helpful in clarifying anxious and avoidant behaviors and why clients become addicted to the highs and lows of avoidant relationships when they are anxious themselves. However, this book was weirdly hetero? Instead of just using them as a pronoun they specifically used he or she when it would've fit to use "them" like they had to actively go out of their way to use he or she. Also, not sure why the scenarios were so caricature-ish. Overall, a helpful book that I gained insight from to use with clients. However, I didn't love some of the ways they put anxious behavior into a "oh they're just a silly goofy mood" category. Calling your partner 10 times in a row is harassment - and people shouldn't be applauded for that.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is something I wish I had read sooner, it would have helped me understand my relationships so much. That being said, it's very straight. I think there is one gay couple example used in the whole book. I also don't know if I buy into the whole "biological essentialism" aspect of attachment styles or that they cannot change. This book seems to be very set on you have the attachment style you have and that will never go away when other research suggests otherwise. It also doesn't cover disorganized attachment.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was absolutely fascinating. I’d vaguely heard about attachment theory before, but this was my first introduction into a comprehensive outline. So why four stars, then? It’s a mixed bag, but overall, I think the mixed bag is worth it if you can navigate it. As other reviewers have mentioned, the authors have limited sympathy towards avoidant attachment style types, which was annoying for an avoidant who is clearly trying to be proactive about it. There’s also a great deal of bias and forgiveness towards anxious styles, and neglect of proactive discussion for avoidant and secure attachments styles in a lot of their dialogue. However, I still think this book was incredibly insightful. Just kind of keep an ear open for bias as you’re reading and you’ll be fine.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: the first 70 pages were insightful and the rest was kinda repetitive examples that didn’t really explain the ~science~ behind attachment styles. I learned something in the beginning though, and maybe the book will be more useful when I’m actually in a relationship… normalized having needs and effectively communicating them which was comforting I guess to an anxious rat like myself

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Fascinating and eye opening! Anyone trying to jump into the dating pool should read this. I did take it with a grain of salt because it is still based on a *theory* and I'm not a professional psychologist but it explains so much nonetheless. For example that most people in the dating pool are "avoidant" attachment style and "play games"...play games and you'll get a player. I would give this 3.5 stars since some of the science is not "solid" but the info it presents is useful, and not just for analyzing people you're dating, but friends, family, etc.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: An easy read about adult attachment and relationships. It’s nice to have a language and way of reframing behaviour as something external and workable (opposed to us/them being inherently broken and unfixable). Also, it has very clear and easy tips for improving relationships. Too heteronormative and traditional for my taste. Nothing earth-shattering but overall fine! 2.5 but rounded to 3. -edit- this book should come with a warning that after reading you will likely label all love songs/love stories as the participants various attachment styles.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book has definitely helped me while going through a really painful breakup. It opens your eyes to your own attachment needs and your partners. You realize what you need in a partnership to be okay and feel loved. It’s very insightful. I would recommend it no matter what your relationship status is.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was really eye opening and made me feel a lot less alone. It’s really good to know it’s not just you experiencing things a certain way. The only thing I have with this book that made it not 5 stars was just that all the info for the other styles etc wasn’t super useful if not your or your partners style. I still really enjoyed reading it non the less and would definitely recommend.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Overall, the book did a good job of outlining each attachment style and providing strategies to maintain healthy relationships. I wish they had explored the anxious-avoidant attachment style as they only really touched on secure, anxious, and avoidant. Plus, it got pretty redundant in almost every chapter.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: terrific and insightful illustration of attachment styles and ways that it shows up in relationships. it was everything i needed to understand my own situation of being an anxiously attached person and what i needed to do and red flags to look out for. now i compulsively screen people for red flags and even though its excessive its better than being hurt!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: One of the most important books ive read so far! It answered a lot of questions in my head! I highly recommend everyone to read it. It explains what type you are and how to tell what type people around are and how to deal with them and how to change your behaviour to secure if youre not one. Its a big life changer and will save you time before getting into wrong relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I probably would have gotten more into this books if I could clearly relate to one of the attachment styles, but I found them too polarized and used as an over simplification of relationship problems. Overall, book had a good message of “don’t assume someone has the same intimacy needs as you” and effective communication is always a good thing.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Realmente, no pudo llegar a mi en un mejor momento. No fue sorpresa para mi descubrir cuál era mi estilo, pero descubrir el porqué suelo caer en ciertos patrones me ayudó a romper círculos viciosos y permitirme entrar en un espacio seguro. Gracias, gracias, gracias. Todos, solteros o en pareja deberían leer este libro. Sin excepciones.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Really great scientific book on attachment theory and how to use it to your advantage in relationships. The book is interactive and has you fill out a quiz to determine your (and your partner’s) attachment type. It also has knowledge checks throughout to help you identify different concepts in practice. Overall, I would recommend this book to anyone. Especially someone looking for a different perspective on human relationships!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Super informative and helpful. But they only alluded to a combo style and didn't dedicate any sections to it. So the very few of us (they kept stressing how rare it was 🤷🏻‍♀️) who got that on their quiz are just left to figure out the nuances alone. Other criticism is that it's very hetero biased and all the pronouns were "she/he" instead of just using "they" which was really annoying.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I think this is a great book for anyone hoping to learn more about how to navigate relationships in a healthier way. although I did see a review saying this book was only good for those with anxious attachment and that’s me so maybe I’m bias. but I learned a lot, even just about recognizing and identifying someone else’s attachment style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I really liked learning about attachment styles and how to apply strategies in the dating and relationship world, relative to your attachment style. It was definitely more focused on anxious attachment versus avoidant, but that worked for me lol. I think it’s important for everyone to learn this about themselves.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I wish they delved more into the avoidant attachment style and all of its causes, needs, and coping strategies. It felt like there was a bias in the writing leaning towards anxious and secure attachments and I think if I had an avoidant attachment style I might feel jilted or disappointed by this book. However, for both my personal and professional development, this book was illuminating and very enriching. Will definitely be reading again.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Smashed through this one while at work today. I did skip through 1 or 2 chapters because I wasn’t too interested in them (hence the no stars rating). That being said I would still highly recommend this quick read. It taught me a lot about myself and former relationships as well as how my fiancée is absolutely the right one for me ❤️

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Me lo recomendó mi psicóloga. - A veces es muy redundante, pero al final está bien porque te quedan las cosas claras. - Me enfadó que mis dinámicas fueran tan obvias como para salir en un libro. - Me ha ayudado bastante. - Me ha puesto triste a veces. - Y tranquila porque saber que no eres rara es siempre reconfortante. - Los ejercicios son estúpidos

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: From start to finish this book was very informative! I liked how the authors backed their findings with various research and provided real life examples of how different attachments interact, resolve conflict, etc… I HIGHLY recommend this book to not only my clients but to those who are single and to those wanting to enhance their relationship. MUST HAVE.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Another book with another set of simplistic theories on how to make sense of people! Sort of. Pop this on the pile with mbti and love languages. Although, to be fair here, attachment theory itself isn’t nonsense at all. It’s worth understanding and thinking about. Rather it is the authors’ simplistic conclusions that are the problem.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: A really interesting book! It provides an insight into understanding different attachment styles and how this can impact communication and relationships. Although this book is written towards a more romantic aspect, it’s actually really informative on why and how others react in certain situations and is a useful tool in learning how to handle and communicate. A quick listen on audiobook 📚 🎧

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I’ve read a lot about childhood attachment and it’s importance. It was interesting to read about attachment styles and how they impact adult relationships. This is most useful for avoidant-anxious pairings, with less practical insights into other couple types. So of only limited use for my own daily life.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Finally finished this after starting it 2 years ago 😅 I have to give the book credit for bringing attachment theory to the mainstream. I know many people who have benefited from learning the framework of this theory through this book. I don’t believe people fall so neatly into each attachment style, and the book lacks a nuanced discussion on how trauma impacts attachment. There’s also a weird vibe of “secure is best” and “avoidant is worst” but overall I think provides a nice and helpful framework for thinking about attachment.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: No se dejen llevar por la portada y el título cursis. Este es un libro basado en estudios de varias universidades y múltiples investigadores en torno a la teoría de los apegos. El plus es que es un libro de divulgación por lo que no es difícil de entender, por el contrario, incluye herramientas que podemos aplicar a la vida cotidiana.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: this was honestly all about anxious attachment and really painted people with an avoidant attachment in a bad light. if you have done any minor research into attachment theory, skip this. Also looking at this from a Christian worldview there was so much that I just fundamentally could not agree with.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: (Mid-read: Part self-help and part research. I'm digging the ideas about adult attachment so far, and using it as a catalyst to reflect on the patterns between my partner and me.) After finishing it, I would recommend this book to anyone interested in attachment research, especially what it means for adult relationships and how much control one has if early attachment was insecure. Because it gives anecdotes from several couples, and names a lot of actual research (that can be found in the bibliography), it gives a sound, relatable argument that couples really do need to have emotional needs met by each other, and despite cultural messages, this is not dependency in a negative way. I liked the attachment style questionnaire, which is optional since they give enough examples to profile the reader (or people the reader is close to). What I found more helpful was the relationship inventory, which provides a format for looking at all adult relationships in order to find patterns. Rather than just diagnosing my current relationship in an absolute (and therefore unhelpful) way, it helped me to see my own tendencies and take some responsibility for them.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book came into my life when I needed it the most... After some time struggling after a break-up and desperately trying to understand why it happened and the reason for some behaviours leading to the it, a friend of mine suggested that I read this book. Plenty of psychological matters and data from studies are covered in this book so that all the facts and claims are made clear. Reading it has given me the chance to understand that my attachment style is anxious and that I've always been dating avoidant people. Now, I know how to spot what's best for me and how to deal with my protest behaviour when I'm feeling the most insecure. In my opinion, this book is hard to read if you're going through a rough time, because it gives the reader explanations about the reality of a relationship and sometimes, they can get a reality-shock, as it was my case. Even so, a much needed one to not repeat behaviours from the past in my future experiences.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book is a bit old at this point and probably contains outdated information, but I think there are plenty of good concepts for anyone to learn. I think there is some disservice in specifically focusing on romantic attachment relationships, but I think that a good reader can generalize. I personally believe the evolutionary and psychological thinking is a bit misrepresented or oversimplified, but for the most part I think that they did a good job trying to stick to scientific research. For instance, I think that attachment system was evolutionarily selected, but that attachment styles are more akin to something like a coping mechanism and not something that should be attempted to understand through evolutionary psychology as much. https://reeswrites.com/posts/attached/

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is nonfiction. I read this one last week and just realized I didn't ever get around to marking it as "read". That felt like genius that he could define relationship attachments so precisely with just a few labels. I liked the way he broke it apart. What I struggled with were the wide and sweeping generalizations. I saw myself in all of the separate labels. So I'm not sure how to rate this one. I'm going with 2.5 stars. review_body: Feeling extremely seen, heard, validated, but above all, challenged to become a more effective communicator. The book anchors strongly to using romantic relationships as the key examples. While I found those relevant and sometimes painfully relatable, I also believe there is as much application to familial and platonic relationships of significant intimacy as well. If you’ve never heard about “attachment styles” you must pick this book up. If you think about them every day, pick it up. This book is for the anxious, the avoidant, and even the secure. Throughout the book I was highlighting and spamming screenshots and rambling voicememos. FOOD FOR THOUGHT to bring into the new year.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I feel like this would be so much more impactful if it explored platonic relationships as well as romantic. Attachment styles manifest in the ways we “attach” to everyone, not just romantic partners, and I’d be curious to read some findings on how they appear in friendships, with coworkers, and with parents - as well as more exploration into how your own attachment style can affect/change others. Overall, this was a nice intro, however some of the examples were over dramatic and the focus on solely romantic relationships left a lot to be desired.

review_body: Really enjoyed this one and breezed through it, though there are some active exercises to do as well. I especially appreciated all the stories alongside the research which helped to make the advice concrete. I would definitely recommend this book to someone looking for something on this topic. The book is great at describing attachment styles and how to deal with relationship conflict in secure ways. I liked that they had chapters dedicated to each attachment style as well as advice for people in all phases of relationships (searching, just starting out, committed). My only large issue was the advice to those with anxious attachment styles that there are many people you will be compatible with, so you shouldn't worry about ending a relationship because you think you'll never find someone else. I really don't think that there are many people an individual will be compatible with. (Is my attachment style showing?? 😝) I think it's true that there are many people you will be emotionally compatible with, but if we start talking about lifestyle compatibility (life outlook, interest in having children or pets, religion, relationship goals, lifestyle (drinking, gym, etc.), etc.), the field narrows and narrows. Especially if you are niche in one of these areas, because even if you are flexible (ex. okay with being with someone from a different religion), other people may not be. So I think it's reasonable to worry about finding someone else if you're already with someone who lines up with you on a lot of those things. Obviously you shouldn't stay in an unproductive relationship, but it can be hard to tell what to look for as the signs of a meaningful relationship beyond just emotional compatibility, especially when the authors say that a "spark" isn't always a good sign and may be indicative of an anxious-avoidant pairing (another thing I don't really agree with but the definition of spark and butterflies are basically non-existant so it makes sense that people will have dif

review_body: Grateful for this book. Helped me see my relationship through a new lens. Do not recommend reading this book if you are in “the trap” and are RUDELY awakened by this book. A good book to read in tandem to this (to gain some empathy for avoidant people, that are shit on throughout) would be the will to change by bell hooks which is a really interesting piece on how the patriarchy affects all of us in relationships. Specifically though how it socializes men (which are more likely to be avoidant). And it asks the question: where do good men go for love if no one is willing to stand by their side as they unlearn what the patriarchy has taught them? They go to therapy hopefully haha, but like also the message is to like have grace for people you love that want to change to be better. But that doesn’t mean you have to sacrifice your well-being either. I did really enjoy this book, it came at the right time. Question for thought: what things can you accept and what things must you change? This book gave me the wisdom to discern between what I can change and what I can’t, which leaves me feeling empowered and grounded.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: What initially drew me into this book was seeing myself represented in the conflict scenarios discussed. From anxious, avoidant, to securely attached, the book unpacks what the needs and desires of each attachment style are, and the pitfalls of being insecurely attached. The book highlighted and reassured me of my anxious needs. Often shunning those for being overly needy and perhaps demanding, the book had a lot of empathy and grace for the anxiously attached. It brought recognition to the biological and evolutionary desires of intimacy and connection, and the importance to effectively communicate and voicing one’s needs. However, there was a lot of emphasis throughout the book on staying clear of attachment styles that oppose yours. One MUST STAY CLEAR of the avoidantly attached, as their distance, “independence” and detachment will leave the anxious continuously dissatisfied. And vice versa where the anxious' desire for intimacy will leave the avoidant urged to create even more distance as intimacy continues, likewise painting their partner as the enemy for essentially wanting to build a connection. Although I do not disagree with some of these notions and scenarios, I really finished the book feeling dissatisfied and perhaps even more confused. Firstly, I disagree with the concept that individuals are distinctively one style or another. I found myself resonating with both the secure and anxious attachment style, hence making it difficult for me to apply their “tips" and theories to my own applications. Quick to categorise an individual as being avoidantly attached by them wanting to set boundaries, be independent, keep distance, but what if someone is just afraid of intimacy? What if certain cultures or religious backgrounds have engrained certain ideals around how the course of a relationship is experienced, which further dictates their needs and expectations? It seems to me that being insecurely attached is not as distinct as being merely anxious or avoidant.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This was a very informative analysis. I'd give it a higher rating but the data on secure attachment styles seemed limited and did not give any real feedback aside from those people are gods and everyone should seek to date them. There was quite literally only one sentence, maybe two, dedicated to saying secure styles aren't perfect (more than halfway in, I'm assuming this was an editor decision), as it went on to describe how perfect and committed they are. That being said, I'd have to agree with avoidant and anxious styles (insecure is mentioned a few times). It was actually eerie reading many of the case studies and there was one that resonated way too well, down to the exact years into the relationship and even the "needs" being a constant excuse for non-commitment in every relationship. Wow. I do wish there was more involving those who have a mixture of both. This was only briefly hit on. I'd have to say reading about the "phantom ex" was also enlightening. Overall, it was actually pretty eye opening, not only about myself but those I have crossed paths with. Note to self: NEVER date an avoidant attachment 😅 (that's quite literally the repeated message from start to finish). The reasons were valid about why not to date these people, and I can see why avoidant folks reading this are so offended. However, it was spot on from what I have encountered in comparison to the examples and research. I'd recommend entering it with an open mind and really think about the groundwork before dismissing it completely. A lot of takeaways, even if you disagree with the logic.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: this is very, very outside the orbit of my usual reading diet but it came up in conversation with someone on board my ship and i figured - eh, if the ideas are interesting enough why not give the book a go the book is in fact pretty insightful. talking to my sis - who's done a lot more reading on attachment theory than i have - it does seem that it simplifies attachment theory somewhat and doesn't always give the full picture. that is a minus, as is the fact that it doesn't really go in depth into the origins of various attachment styles (anxious/avoidant/disorganised). but it doesn't purport to do so. ultimately this is a pragmatic guide of sorts and it quite succeeds at doing that: it singles out problematic romantic tropes in unfortunate currency and argues persuasively for why they ought to be jettisoned, while supplementing the reader w what seems to be a healthier perspective on what a partnership should be like. not a deep book by any means but educational nonetheless

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I wish I had read this book a decade ago. Even though it focuses on romantic relationships, there are really incredible insights here that can be helpful in all relationships. I believe that many theories in books like this provide a lens through which you can look at the world and find some truth. None of these theories provide the perfect understanding of truth. But by looking at the world various frameworks you can get closer to the truth. I highly recommend this book to anyone who cares deeply about relationships and in understanding themselves.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book has some valuable insights into attachment theory, and the three different types of attachments. I’m mostly rating it two stars because it felt *very* dated (I didn’t realize when I checked it out that it was over a decade old), and feels extremely preachy and judgmental in many parts, often speaking about people in ways I found infantilizing and condescending. So, some valuable insights, but too hard to get past the apparent distaste that the authors had for the people they were writing about.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I've never felt so validated from a book. I didn't know much about attachment styles beforehand, so hearing the tell tale signs of an anxious attachment style felt like the authors were looking into my soul. It made me realize that while there is nothing inherently "wrong" with me, there are a number of tools I can utilize to ensure my relationship with my spouse remains happy, healthy, and fulfilling. I highly recommend this one anyone who wants to understand their own attachment style, what that means, and how to find or keep a partner who compliments their specific needs.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: such an amazing book for anyone in any kind of relationship — romantic or friendship — and who wants to learn more about their or their partner’s behavior. truly helps decode so many thoughts, emotions, and actions in relationships and helps you understand when attachment theory is at play. feel like i’ve become so much more aware of when my attachment system is activated so i can go back to a more secure place and realize that it stems from childhood wounds and communicate effectively. a must read!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It helped me organise my own thoughts about relationships. I like the general idea of attachment styles and how they work. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Struggle to find and sustain love? Then learning more about your attachment style might hold the key to understanding why that is. According to Attachment Theory there are 3 distinct styles of attachment: anxious, secure and avoidant. 🔹Anxious: Anxiously attached people are preoccupied with thoughts about their relationship and the ability of their partner to love them back. (~25% of the population.) 🔸Secure: You feel secure with intimacy and are usually warm and loving. (~50%) 🔹Avoidant: The intimacy of relationships feel like a threat to the Avoidant persons independence. (~25%) The missing ~5% fall into both the Anxious AND Avoidant category. 📝 The avoidant make up a large part of the dating pool since they seldom stay for long in a relationship and bounce back fast after being rejected. 📝 Sometimes the anxiously attached mistake the emotional rollercoaster they experience when dating avoidant partners for love. When that drama is missing, like with a Secure partner, they feel like the spark is missing. 📝 The basic premise of adult attachment and the essence of attachment theory: “If you want to take the road to independence and happiness, find the right person to depend on and travel down with that person.” 📝 Most People are only as needy as their unmet needs. When their emotional needs are met they usually turn their attention outward. By responding to a need early on we can save ourselves a lot of hassle of putting out fires later. ⭐️ TAKEAWAY: Even if I fall into the securely attached category I learned from this book that I also have a few Avoidant traits as well. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: ~MAIN TAKEAWAYS~ -"Dependency is not a bad word." While an extreme level of dependency can certainly cause dysregulation and enmeshment, we sometimes take it too far and assume ALL dependency is a sign of weakness or clinginess. -The Dependency Paradox. I related this to rock climbing: in order to climb, explore, and push yourself, you need someone belaying you. If their grip is too tight, you can't move at all. If their grip is too loose, you have no safety net if you fall. Thus, secure attachment is, ironically, the key to developing the independence necessary for healthy relationships. -Protest behaviors are often a means to getting our attachment needs met. Many behaviors we dismiss as "clingy" or "crazy" are often rooted in extreme attachment distress. -Our cultural obsession with the infatuation stage makes us more prone to jump into unsteady yet exciting relationships, while simultaneously writing off secure attachments as "boring." We dismiss them once we get "the ick." Secure attachments are not always as thrilling, but they are more satisfying in the long run. -Our relationships with our pets tend to be pretty secure and can serve as a model for our human relationships! -This book has some great pieces of advice for people with Anxious Attachment. Some of my favorites were to approach dating with an abundance philosophy, wait before jumping to conclusions, ask for clarification, and don't mistake an activated attachment system for love. ~CRITIQUES~ -The author seemed to have a bias towards Anxious over Avoidant. Anxious was often written as having valid needs that needed to be communicated and met by the partner, and Avoidant was often depicted as the unwilling, unloving partner who couldn't be bothered to try to meet their partner's needs. The Avoidant's fundamental need for space was not validated in the same way as the Anxious' need for closeness. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached by Amir Levine and Rachel Heller is an extremely quick pop-psychy read filled with magazine-style quizzes, scorecards and geegaws designed to assist with love relationships, but distinguished by a skeleton of very real psychological and social science research on attachment theory. Levine and Heller's thesis is that we all fall into three categories of attachment style: anxious, secure or avoidant, and the various combinations, with their attendant strengths and pitfalls, constitute the bulk of the book. I learned a couple of new things (current research does not support the idea that our attachment styles are solely the result of infant/parent bonding, for example), and gained some insight into a variety of relationships, not just those of the romantic variety. The anxious/avoidant relationships detailed in the book march right up to, but don't cross the line into, outright abuse. So those who see themselves, their lovers or loved ones in those pairings might be better served by reading Women Who Love Psychopaths by Sandra Brown and Lianne Leedom, to gain insight into that particular corner of hell. There are many parallels between the avoidant personality and the narcissistic/sociopathic one. And I'm so intrigued by the parallels, I'd like to see Levine and Heller continue this same theme with a look at attachment theory and workplace relationships, much the way that Robert Hare took his theories to the workplace with Snakes in Suits. Attached was the first library ebook I managed to get all the way through before it expired and disappeared, and it suffered by virtue of the medium. The charts did not show up in a readable form on my device, but nevertheless it was an enjoyable enough read.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: It’s interesting. A lot of these types of books give me really big pseudoscience vibes. We’re so good at pattern matching that we will find correlations in anything. I remember doing a test for ADHD as a kid where I sat at a computer and pressed a button if a W appeared on the screen, and didn’t press anything for all other flashing letters. And, by the end of the test, I was sure that I could figure out the pattern. I asked the guy administering the test afterwards, “so like if it’s a vowel, then the W is two letters afterwards, but if it’s consonant, then it could be one afterwards or not at all. Except when it’s an X where W always follows X” he was like “no it’s totally random. It just goes on for like ten minutes and we see if you get bored or not.” so yeah… baby Rick had a lot of learning to do. I thought this book presents a really overall helpful narrative towards helping talk about relationships and connection. There’s patterns that you learn and we can kind of bucket those generally around certain traits. I wouldn’t worry too much if you don’t fit strongly into one or where are the lines between different ones as this is ultimately a made-up way to help explain what’s going on. The human experience is so widely varied that you can shoehorn a lot of theories into it. And whether or not this book is ultimately truth with a capital T, it was generally helpful for helping me understand my own failings and strengths in relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was an absolute GODSEND for me. Ever since beginning to date men, I've suffered difficult, heartwrenching, miserable relationships in which I constantly feel clingy, desperate, and filled with anxiety and fear. Self-help literature (and societal norms at large) labeled me "codependent" and overly-needy, and told me I needed to learn to be totally independent and not depend on anyone for anything. I tried to get used to the idea that I needed to never need anything from anyone, but it never felt right. This book debunks that "codependency myth" and recognizes that we all have attachment systems (some more sensitive than others) and a secure, healthy relationship should make us feel supported and confident, not constantly afraid our partner is going to leave. Levine's attachment paradigm (secure/anxious/avoidant) explained ALL of my painful relationship experiences so precisely and point-blank, I was dumbfounded, and finally felt understood. I'm left with a newfound confidence that I CAN find healthy relationships, if I simply accept my intimacy needs from the beginning, filter for those who can meet them, and never be afraid to effectively communicate when I feel disconnected. THANK YOU, AUTHORS, for giving me hope, confidence, and tools!

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Ok, creo que todos deberían leer este libro en algún momento, sobre todo desde jóvenes! Decidí leerlo ya que es muy recomendado por psicoterapeutas. A raíz de varias conversaciones que he tenido, hay un consenso que en países de habla hispana, sobre todo en Latinoamérica, el tema de los tipos de apegos emocionales no se habla mucho o no es muy conocido. Y después de varias experiencias dolorosas ahora entiendo su importancia! Es un libro muy ligero, aunque a veces sus ejemplos son algo cursis. Los autores explican de manera clara cómo nos presentamos en relaciones de pareja, por qué reaccionamos de ciertas maneras y tips para navegar conflictos. Según la teoría, existen 4 estilos de apego principales: apego seguro, ansioso, evitativo y desorganizado. Muchas reseñas del libro critican que se enfoca solo en uno, y es verdad, se enfoca principalmente en el apego ansioso y tiende a villanizar un poco al apego evitativo. Sin embargo, considero que este libro es bueno como introducción a esta teoría; cuando se comienza a estudiar sobre apegos este es una introducción, mas no pretende ser una enciclopedia.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Helpful, non-stigmatizing relationship read! Cool that the website to determine attachment style is the same as the study I participated in since 2015. Can have state vs trait attachment styles, attachment styles can change. Securely attached ppl can help partners become more secure. 2 secure partners or 1 secure + 1 insecure are same levels or satisfaction. Secures need to guard against getting pulled to become anx or avoidant which can happened based on our life experiences. Basically, all our attachment needs are reasonable and make sense evolutionarily/w what happens in our bodies, and it’s important for us to communicate our attachment needs in clear, non blaming ways before things become big problems. Secures believe they’re worthy of needs being met, which is a healthy perspective to have. If you’ve asked for your needs to be met and they aren’t being met, it’s worth finding a new partner who can meet your needs so you can be happier. Breaks ups mimic broken leg pain reaction on scans but book offers coping strategies for how to get thru like leaning on others and reminding yourself why you left. Would recommend this to couples who like bibliotherapy & whose arguments tend to be around negotiating closeness (not “bread and butter” arguments).

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Attached is one of the most useful books I've ever read. If this were required reading in sex ed classes, we'd have a lot fewer people stuck in disastrous relationships (or unable to form relationships to begin with). The attachment framework is quite simple, but has a remarkable capacity to explain dating and relationship problems. This book allows you to understand your own dating pathologies as well as those of your partners (and your friends' partners!). It also provides strategies to make your attachments more secure and a helpful assortment of red flags. The book is easy to follow and its thesis rings true. My one complaint is its heteronormativity – nearly all the examples given were of straight couples, and I can't help but feel that some dynamics are different for LGBTQ people, but I can't honestly say that this prevented the book from feeling incredibly relevant.

On the other hand I found this book SO repetitive. Half of the pages could be cut out because I felt I was reading the same thing over and over again. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I also had been wanting to read a book on this subject for some time, particularly to understand the science behind attachment theories. From this book, I learned several fascinating things. We all have an attachment system, a combination of emotions and behaviors designed to keep us safe by staying close to our loved ones. The need for close relationships is embedded in our genes—we are biologically wired to depend on a significant other. We all have a basic need to form close bonds, but the way we create and maintain these bonds differs. In dangerous environments, it is less advantageous to invest time and energy in just one person (avoidant style), or it might lead to becoming hyper-vigilant about staying close to loved ones (anxious style). In contrast, in a safer environment, deeply investing in an intimate bond benefits both partners (secure style). It’s particularly interesting to realize that the myth of independence is untrue. People often say that happiness must come from within and that depending on others is a sign of weakness. However, science tells us otherwise. Once we become attached to someone, the two of us form a psychological unit. Dependency is not a preference or choice—it’s a biological fact. However, how we handle this dependency varies by attachment style. Secure and anxious individuals embrace it, while avoidants tend to suppress it. The book also discusses the “anxious-avoidant paradox.” Anxious individuals seek intimacy, while avoidant individuals avoid it. Yet, they often end up together. Why? Anxious individuals tend to confuse the anxiety, preoccupation, and obsession they feel, as well as those fleeting moments of joy, with love. When you think like this, you are essentially programmed to attach yourself to people who are least likely to make you happy. Er gebeurde veel in korte tijd, dat leverde (zeer) veel onrust en ruis op en legde veel zwakke plekken bloot, en mijn partner raadde dit boek aan omdat het haar ook geholpen had. Uiteindelijk heeft dat lezen me enorm geholpen. Het gaf me - maar pas na ruim een half jaar het boek wegleggen en het toen pas uitlezen - het gevoel dat ik ook had toen ik mijn therapie verliet: de wil om vast te leggen van ik geleerd heb, uit angst de inzichten weer te verliezen en terug te vallen in oud gedrag. Dat is absoluut een zeer positieve zaak, want de meeste (schrijvers van) zelfhulpboeken wil je diagonaal door een botte wortelrasp trekken, vanwege hun kortzichtigheid, pedanterie, een-persoonlijke-anekdote-is-geen-universeel-fenomeen-valkuilen en toepassing van slechte wetenschap. De auteurs, Amir Levine en Rachel Heller, hebben een zeer comfortabele plek gevonden tussen een goede theorie en veel praktische uitleg. Natuurlijk gaan ze wel érg hard op hun binaire indeling van personages en gaan ze er (ik hoop onbedoeld) vanuit dat avoidant-mensen de redding voorbij zijn (terwijl secure-mensen een soort Romeinse goden zijn), maar dat is klein bier in het grotere geheel. Ik vond (en vind) dit boek extreem behulpzaam in het beter begrijpen van mezelf, mijn partner en de dynamiek van relaties. De persoonlijke context bij dit alles, opdat ik niet vergeet wat ik geleerd heb: Ik las dit boek in twee fases: de eerste helft tot ik serieus achter was gekomen dat ik geestelijk wat uitdagingen heb en in therapie ging, de tweede helft toen ik klaar was met therapie. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I want to believe this book has pointed me in the correct direction for becoming a more secure individual. My main issue is that I have an introverted nature along with an anxious desire for companionship. I've learned so much in such a small amount of time and have cringed at myself for my own "protest behavior" and avoidant thoughts after reflecting on past relationships and friendships. I know my parents divorce and abandonment of my father has ingrained my attachment style fairly deep, also the mistakes I've made in previous relationships where I would notice the smallest changes and over react or just react too quickly to what I perceived as turbulence in my relationships, and also the avoidant behavior in relationships where I felt like the other persons reliance was a burden and I lied about being busy to avoid my partners needs. The good news I discovered after listening to this book is that it's not hopeless and the first steps towards becoming more secure is by recognizing your own anxious behavior as something you don't need to react to and it's possible (but very difficult) to avoid protest behavior when it feels like a way to repay someone's perceived avoidance. Protest behavior is basically things anxious or avoidant people do in protest to too much or not enough reciprocation of their emotions. An avoidant might lie about being too busy with work or completely ghost someone for a few days after feeling a connection starting to form and an anxious person who is waiting for a response or phone call back might do something like post a story to see if the person is noticing them on their story so they can reinforce their anxiety of being ignored. (Totally not something I've done before) :| But anyway, this book has helped me to realize a goal I can start working toward, and that goal is a SECURE foundation. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I personally loved this book and got too much out of it to not give it 5 stars, but I will provide a disclaimer that I don’t think this book would necessarily be universally loved. You will likely get a lot more out of this book if you have an anxious attachment style or are with or have ever been with a partner that has an anxious attachment style. If you have no idea what those are, you’ll like this book if you’ve generally had intimacy issues in your relationships but don’t know why i.e. the desire to be close to a romantic partner but having a hard time fully trusting them/ the situation or the desire to be in a relationship but having a hard time committing to a partner. Additionally, if you just have a general interest in psychology and learning more about why people act the way they do, you will also probably like this book. If you find yourself in a committed relationship that seems completely void of intimacy issues (congrats) and don’t really give a fuck about psychology, this book will probably be very boring to you. However, I will say, there are a lot of strategies laid out in the book about conflict resolution and effective communication that I think could also be applied to non-intimacy related conflict within intimate or non-intimate relationships. I found the arguments of this book to be clear and the anecdotes to be engaging and insightful. I learned a lot about attachment theory during undergrad, but still found a lot of this to be new information and more practical than the information I had learned previously. Would love to discuss this book with anyone who reads it! I would love to see a 2024 update to this book that discusses the impacts of social media and the pandemic on attachment styles and also that looks at generational differences. While gender is not a huge factor discussed in attachment theory, this book was published in 2010, so you will find some pretty heteronormative themes to in the book that might not sit well with some. book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book held up a mirror to me. Did you ever have someone tell you about yourself and they were dead on the money? That was this book for me. Just wow. I not only enjoyed learning about the attachment styles,behaviors and thinking patterns ,but also I appreciate learning why my ex acted the way he did,even unconsciously . Why meeting (my)Mr.Right has been challenging but also why so many men and women act the way they do. What was really enlightening was that we exhibit these behaviors from childhood ,but it’s not necessarily from trauma. There was no pointing the finger, just funny enough science and studies. When someone has a disability you can understand their limitations with the insight that you have. I get why my attachment style is diametrically opposed to the one I’m attracted to. However with the warnings,it also provided tools to cope if I decided to continue pursuing that type in a relationship. I highlighted and marked that book all up. I would recommend this to anyone,even if you’re already in a relationship,you can gain new understanding into your partner and maybe things can go a little bit smoother. I find that with knowledge and understanding,then you truly can act with wisdom.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: Probably one of my all time favorite books. I could go on and on about it. I’ve always struggled with relationships to the point of it being a huge trigger of mine. I’ve always had people tell me that I need to work on myself and be happy alone before getting in a relationship but I’ve always felt very independent. This book made me realize that I’m not needy, it’s not bad to want your SO to text you, or want quality time, it’s just what you need. I think this book could help out so many people. Mostly in romantic relationships but also in other relationships as well. I do think this book is MOST helpful for those who have anxious attachment styles, pretty helpful for those with avoidant attachment styles and maybe not so much for secures. Either way, I think everyone should read it. At the end of the book, they talk about a movie. I’m almost positive the movie is 500 Days of Summer because it’s my favorite movie of all time. There’s a huge debate about this movie and whether Tom or Summer is the villain. I used to think Summer and then it switched to Tom but still didn’t like Summer. Well, after reading this, I realized that Summer is avoidant (most of my partners) and Tom is anxious (me) and neither are bad, they are just bad together.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This is one of the most influential books I’ve ever read. My therapist recommended this to me after several sessions of my anxious ramblings and from the first page this book read ME. I had a general sense of the attachment styles and always knew I was somewhere between anxious and secure but learning about the studies was wildly interesting and I finally understood my feelings and actions in all my previous relationships. I’ve since been this book’s #1 advocate, shouting its influence from the rooftops. I do think some of the workbook style portions can be skipped, but Attached allows you to utilize the book as you see fit.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: I chose this book since I’m getting married this year and want to have all the right tools in my toolbox for a successful marriage. I think a former, single, psychology major me would have gobbled this up. Now as a 31-year old engaged woman, a lot of this was stuff I’ve already learned through experience. There were nuggets that helped me reflect on my own attachment style and that of my partner. I was able to figure out some of my relationship patterns. Most of it, however, was examples that I couldn’t see myself or partner in. In those instances, I tried thinking about friends or even TV shows that pertain to what was being discussed in order to try to stay engaged. Sometimes I just skipped the anecdotes to get to the science and explanations.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: The book is very informative and I have to admit that the attachment theory explains so much. As an anxiously attached person, the book explained lots of the patterns I went through and explained why those patterns occurred. The book also mentioned some of the emotions I constantly feel as if the writers were living my life and not just writing this based on a study. The way the book is written and the way everything is explained is brilliant. It starts by explaining what the 3 types of attachment are. Then, the book goes to explaining what are the cues or the traits you can notice to categorize yourself -or your partner- to a certain type of the 3 attachment types. After that, the book talks about relationships and what happens when 2 types of the 3 collide. Lastly, it give some tips to make all relationships better so that all partners can reach the level of intimacy and comfort they need in their life. Simply brilliant. The thing I didn’t like about the book though, is the way they want the insecure to handle their relationships. The book didn’t help with how an insecure person can become a secure. It gave a few tips and tricks here and there. It said that some insecure people can do some secure actions and this will help in the relationship in the long run. The book didn’t say how can an insecure person after doing some things and changing their life style they can become a secure person one day. I think as someone who’s insecure (anxious) I would have wanted that. I would have wanted to know what can I do specifically to become someone secure in his relationships.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: This book was an interesting look at three attachment styles: secure, anxious, and avoidant. Each style was explained thoroughly, with ways to identify and explain the behaviors of people with these attachment styles. Reading this made me feel more justified in my feelings and able to accept them as normal and not a character flaw. I discovered that I have an anxious attachment style, and what that means for me. I was also able to identify the attachment styles of some people around me, including that of my partner. Definitely worth reading to understand not only romantic relationships but all relationships and how to effectively improve your relationships, with suggestions for each attachment style.

book_title: Attached: The Science of Adult Attachment
review_body: In a quick version: Well. This book, even though I was very excited about it in the beginning, after some thought gets 3 (maybe 3.5) stars from me. However, I will still highly recommend this (or a similar, better book about this topic) to anyone who even thinks about going into a relationship (or already is in one)(especially if one party has the anxious style). The initial excitement came from the style of the book - which is based on research and psychology. The book does a good job explaining the different styles, but also almost ignores the disorganized style (mentioned once in the whole book). It also explain the research behind it and then offers a test to find your own style. After that, however, the book changes its initial objective tone into a biased one - it highly favors the anxious people, giving them a long, soothing chapter, after which they go to the avoidant types, which are described in a distant, cold-hearted, almost cruel way. At one point the book discourages anxious people to even start a relationship with the avoidant ones. This bias continues almost throughout the whole book. Now - as an anxious person, I think the book does a really good job describing what it means and feels like to be the anxious type. It also explains really well that these feelings and needs are normal, connected to our psychology and the way we work. It also explains well how to communicate and work in a relationship. However, I think it is being very unfair to the avoidant ones. Anyways - I would have to study more about this subject to give a good review. But despite some major minuses, I would still recommend this book to either learn more about yourself as an anxious type, or about your partner.
